In a separate bowl, whisk eggs, milk, vegetable oil, and vanilla extract.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Carefully pour cake batter over the peaches in the pan. Spread gently.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let the cake cool in the pan for 10 minutes.
Place a serving plate over the cake pan. Carefully invert the cake onto the plate. Remove the pan.
Let the cake cool completely before serving.
notes: Great for family gatherings or a simple weeknight dessert.
Best served at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Fried Chicken Livers with Caramelized Onions and Bacon
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. A generous portion of pan-fried chicken livers, each a whole, irregularly shaped piece, is arranged loosely in the center. The livers are rich reddish-brown with darker seared edges. Thinly sliced, deeply caramelized onions are interspersed, their golden-brown strands adding softness. Crisp, 1 cm bacon bits are scattered over the top. A sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley provides a vibrant pop of color. Components touch and overlap, forming a natural, comforting mound. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table with a casual beige linen napkin and standard flatware. Warm kitchen lighting creates a cozy, lived-in atmosphere, with subtle background elements hinting at a family meal.

ingredients.name: Dry white wine or chicken broth

instructions: Clean chicken livers. Pat them dry. Trim any visible fat or green spots.
Cut bacon into 1 cm pieces.
Heat a large pan over medium heat. Add bacon. Cook until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon and set aside. Keep rendered fat in the pan.
Thinly slice onions. Add them to the pan with bacon fat. Cook on medium-low heat for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Onions should be soft and deeply caramelized.
Mince garlic cloves. Add minced garlic to onions. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Increase heat to medium-high. Add butter and olive oil to the pan.
Season chicken livers generously with salt and pepper.
Add chicken livers to the hot pan in a single layer. Cook in batches if needed. Sear livers for 2-3 minutes per side until browned and an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) is reached.
Remove cooked livers from the pan.
Deglaze the pan with white wine or chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce liquid slightly.
Return cooked livers, caramelized onions, and crispy bacon to the pan. Toss gently to combine.
Chop fresh parsley. Stir in the chopped parsley.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hähnchenschnitzel mit Röstkartoffeln und Butternudeln
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown, crispy chicken schnitzel, pounded thin, occupies the center of a clean white porcelain plate. Beside it are fluffy, pan-roasted potato wedges with slightly crisped edges and a rich, golden hue. A small mound of glossy, buttered egg noodles, subtly seasoned, complements the main components. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley and a bright yellow lemon wedge positioned to the side. The arrangement is balanced and professional, with appropriate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, standard silver flatware, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional lemon wedges for squeezing.
Offer a side of traditional lingonberry or cranberry sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad with a light vinaigrette.
instructions: Prepare chicken: Slice each chicken breast horizontally to create two thinner cutlets. Place each cutlet between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound with a meat mallet to 0.5 cm thickness.
Set up breading station: Prepare three shallow dishes. In the first, place flour. In the second, whisk eggs. In the third, place breadcrumbs. Season flour and breadcrumbs with salt and pepper.

Bread chicken: Dredge each chicken cutlet first in flour, shaking off excess. Then dip in beaten egg, allowing excess to drip off. Finally, coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs, pressing gently to ensure adherence.

Cook potatoes: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash potatoes thoroughly. Cut into 2 cm wedges or chunks. Toss with 15 ml vegetable oil, salt, and pepper. Spread potatoes in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and golden brown.
Cook noodles: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add egg noodles. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain noodles well. Return to pot and toss with butter.

Fry schnitzel: Heat 85 ml vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Once hot, carefully place schnitzel pieces in the skillet. Do not overcrowd. Fry for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Transfer cooked schnitzel to a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.

Plate: Place one schnitzel on each serving plate. Arrange roasted potato wedges and buttered noodles alongside the schnitzel. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley and a lemon wedge. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Do not overcrowd the skillet when frying schnitzel; cook in batches if necessary.
traditional_techniques: Pounding meat thin for even cooking and tenderness
Pan-frying until golden brown and crispy

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Paprika Eggplant Consommé with Bell Pepper Brunoise and Basil Oil
recipes.visual_description: A crystal-clear, amber-hued Smoked Paprika Eggplant Consommé presented in a shallow, matte white ceramic bowl. The consommé fills the base of the bowl, allowing for ample negative space around the edges. In the precise center, a small, vibrant cluster of finely diced red bell pepper brunoise (2mm cubes) creates a focal point of intense red. Around this central element, a few delicate drops of bright green basil oil are artfully dotted, creating a sophisticated color contrast. The surface of the consommé is perfectly still and reflective. The bowl rests on a light grey marble surface, accompanied by a single, pristine white linen napkin folded into a sharp triangle. Dramatic, directional lighting casts soft shadows, emphasizing the dish's minimalist elegance and precision.
instructions: Dice 150g eggplant, 50g tomato, and 20g red bell pepper (for base). Crush garlic.
In a pot, sauté diced eggplant, tomato, 20g bell pepper, and garlic until softened. Add smoked paprika. Deglaze with white wine.
Add 500ml water. Simmer gently for 30 minutes. Strain solids, reserving liquid.
Whisk egg white with finely chopped parsley. Add to strained liquid.
Heat liquid gently, stirring constantly, until egg white raft forms. Stop stirring. Simmer very gently for 20 minutes without disturbing raft.
Carefully ladle consommé through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth, avoiding the raft.
Blanch basil leaves briefly. Immediately shock in ice water. Squeeze dry.
Blend blanched basil with olive oil until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for clear oil.
Dice remaining 30g red bell pepper into very fine brunoise (2mm cubes).
Gently warm consommé. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour warm consommé into a shallow bowl. Place bell pepper brunoise precisely in the center. Drizzle basil oil artfully around the brunoise.
notes: For optimal clarity, ensure the consommé simmers gently without disturbing the egg white raft. Strain very carefully.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Root Broth with Crispy Peels
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Roasted Root Broth is presented in a handcrafted, smooth ceramic bowl of natural cream tone, placed on a light, textured bamboo surface. The clear, golden-amber broth fills the bowl. A few roasted root vegetable chunks (parsnip, carrot, celeriac, potato), cut into irregular 2 cm pieces, rest at the bottom, their edges lightly caramelized. A vibrant green herb oil is subtly drizzled, creating an organic swirl. Delicate, golden-brown crispy root vegetable peels, artfully arranged on the broth's surface, provide natural texture. The composition is clean and minimalist, highlighting ingredient colors. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is beside the bowl. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, emphasizing the organic feel. A hint of green from a distant plant is in the clean background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash all root vegetables thoroughly. Peel parsnip, carrot, celeriac, and potato. Reserve all peels.
Cut half of the peeled parsnip, carrot, celeriac, and potato into 2 cm chunks. Dice the remaining halves into 1 cm cubes.
Halve tomato. Smash garlic cloves.
Toss 2 cm chunks of root vegetables, tomato halves, and smashed garlic with 10ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and lightly caramelized.
While roasting, place reserved root peels, diced root vegetable cubes, and celery stalk into a pot. Add 750ml water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Simmer for 30 minutes.
Strain the broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard cooked vegetables and celery.
Spread reserved root peels on a separate baking tray. Toss with 5ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Bake at 180°C for 10-15 minutes until crispy. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
For herb oil, blend basil and parsley leaves with 15ml olive oil until smooth. Strain through a fine sieve if desired for a clearer oil.
Reheat strained broth gently. Season with salt and pepper.
Ladle broth into a bowl. Add a few roasted root vegetable chunks. Drizzle with herb oil. Garnish with crispy root peels. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing vegetable peels for a crispy garnish, enhancing flavor and texture.
Adjust vegetable roasting time for desired caramelization.

recipes.recipe_name: Summer Peach & Rosemary Almond Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly cut slice of Summer Peach & Rosemary Almond Cake rests off-center on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate. The cake slice reveals a tender, golden-brown crumb with visible, soft peach cubes and tiny flecks of green, finely chopped rosemary. Its top crust is a light golden-brown, showing a subtle rustic texture. A delicate, translucent drizzle of plain cream glaze cascades gently over one side of the slice, adding a soft sheen. The plate itself is presented on a light-colored, naturally textured bamboo or stone surface. An undyed, natural beige linen napkin is subtly folded to the side. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the cake's textures and colors. The background is minimalist and clean, featuring a hint of soft green from a blurred plant, maintaining focus on the dish's natural beauty and unforced composition. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space around the cake slice, emphasizing clean, ingredient-focused plating.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Lightly grease a small oven-safe ramekin or mold.
Wash and dice the peach into small cubes. Finely chop the fresh rosemary.
In a small bowl, whisk together almond flour, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk the egg with milk until combined.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Gently fold in the diced peach and chopped rosemary.
Pour batter into the prepared ramekin. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
While the cake bakes, prepare a simple glaze. Whisk cream until slightly thickened.
Remove cake from oven. Let cool in the ramekin for 5 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Serve a single slice of cake. Drizzle lightly with the plain cream glaze.

recipes.recipe_name: Seasonal Fruit & Nut Pressed Bites
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine perfectly uniform miniature squares are meticulously arranged on a sophisticated, natural wood serving platter. Each square features distinct layers: a dense, rich hazelnut-almond base, a vibrant, jewel-toned mixed berry and stone fruit paste, and a final delicate nut layer on top. The edges of the squares are clean and precise, showcasing the layered texture. Colors are deep and natural, with the fruit paste offering reds, purples, and oranges contrasted by the earthy browns of the nuts. The overall presentation is minimalistic, emphasizing the pure beauty of the ingredients with ample white space on the platter. The platter rests on a light bamboo table surface, complemented by an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the scene, creating a clean, inviting aesthetic. A subtle, out-of-focus hint of green foliage from a plant provides a clean, natural background element.

ingredients.name: Mixed stone fruits (plum, peach, nectarine), pitted and diced

instructions: Combine mixed berries, diced stone fruits, and water in a small saucepan. Cook over low heat. Stir occasionally. Cook until fruits break down and mixture thickens into a jam-like paste. This concentrates the fruit flavors. Stir in cinnamon and nutmeg. Cool completely.
In a bowl, combine ground hazelnuts and ground almonds. Add egg yolk. Mix well until a crumbly dough forms. If too dry, add milk, a few drops at a time, until the mixture binds.
Press half of the nut mixture evenly into a small, parchment-lined rectangular mold (e.g., 10x5 cm).
Spread the cooled fruit paste over the nut layer. Gently press the remaining nut mixture over the fruit paste, creating a top layer.
Cover the mold. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, or until firm.
Carefully remove the block from the mold. Using a sharp, hot knife, cut into 6-9 uniform miniature squares or rectangles for serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Summer Fruit Conserve Tartlets
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine delicate miniature tartlets are elegantly arranged on a light, unpolished natural stone platter. Each tartlet features a crisp, golden-brown almond shortbread shell, its natural texture subtly visible. The shells are filled with a vibrant, jewel-toned mixed berry and peach conserve, showcasing rich reds and purples from the berries and soft orange from the peaches. A small, creamy white dollop of light almond cream sits atop the conserve, smooth and inviting. Each petit four is crowned with a single, fresh green peppermint leaf, providing a subtle contrast and fresh aroma. The tartlets are evenly spaced, allowing ample negative space around each piece. The platter rests on an undyed natural linen cloth, set against a clean, minimalist background with soft, natural light illuminating the scene, emphasizing the pure colors and textures of the ingredients.
instructions: Combine almond flour, all-purpose flour, powdered sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Cut in cold butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add ice water gradually, mixing until dough forms. Do not overmix.
Wrap dough in plastic wrap. Chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Press small pieces of dough into mini tartlet molds or mini muffin tins. Prick bottoms with a fork.
Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until golden brown. Cool completely on a wire rack.
For the conserve: Combine mixed berries, diced peach, natural sweetener, and lemon juice in a small saucepan.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until fruit softens and mixture thickens (about 10-15 minutes).
Mash lightly with a fork if desired. Cool completely.
For the almond cream: Heat milk and heavy cream in a small saucepan over medium heat until warm, not boiling.
Whisk in finely ground blanched almonds, natural sweetener, and nutmeg until smooth.
Remove from heat. Chill thoroughly, at least 1 hour, until thickened.
To assemble: Fill each cooled tartlet shell with a spoonful of the fruit conserve.
Top each with a small dollop of the chilled almond cream.
Garnish each tartlet with a single small peppermint leaf.
notes: This recipe adheres to the special request for no fermentation, focusing on cooked fruit preserve.
Use ripe, seasonal fruits for the best flavor and natural sweetness.

recipes.recipe_name: Apple & Hazelnut Spiced Bites
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine perfectly uniform miniature apple and hazelnut spiced bites, golden-brown and slightly domed, are arranged with clean, mindful spacing on a rectangular, light-colored stone serving platter. Each bite is lightly dusted with fine powdered sugar, creating a delicate white contrast against the warm cake hue. Visible within the tender crumb are small, soft cubes of baked apple and crunchy pieces of chopped hazelnut. The overall presentation is minimalistic, highlighting the natural textures and colors of the ingredients. The platter rests on a light-toned reclaimed wood table surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is subtly folded beside the platter. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows and emphasizing the organic beauty of the sustainable ingredients. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of natural greenery visible, maintaining focus on the delicate sweets.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a mini muffin tin or small silicone molds.
Dice apple into small cubes, approximately 0.5 cm.
Chop roasted hazelnuts coarsely.
In a mixing bowl, whisk egg, sugar, melted butter, and vanilla extract until combined.
Add almond flour, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt to the wet ingredients. Mix gently until just combined.
Fold in diced apple and chopped hazelnuts.
Spoon batter into prepared molds, filling each about two-thirds full.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown and a toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Cool mini cakes in molds for 5 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
Dust cooled mini cakes with powdered sugar before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Dark Chocolate Hazelnut Sablés with Raspberry Gel
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine miniature Dark Chocolate Hazelnut Sablés are meticulously arranged on a pristine white porcelain serving platter, leaving generous negative space between each piece. Each petit four features a crisp, golden-brown hazelnut sablé shell, precisely baked with clean edges. The shell is filled with a rich, glossy dark chocolate ganache, piped smoothly to create a slight dome. A vibrant crimson dot or two of shimmering raspberry gel is delicately placed atop the dark ganache, providing a striking color contrast. Each petit four is crowned with a single, perfectly glazed candied hazelnut, adding a subtle textural element and shine. The overall presentation is one of sophisticated minimalism, emphasizing flawless execution and the interplay of deep chocolate, bright red, and warm brown hues. The platter rests on a polished white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic, professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the textures and refined elegance of the composition, with an ultra-minimalist background ensuring the focus remains solely on the exquisite confections.
instructions: For the Hazelnut Sablé Tartlets: Combine 30g cold butter, 30g all-purpose flour, 20g hazelnut flour, 10g sugar, and a pinch of salt. Mix until crumbly.
Add 1 egg yolk. Mix until a dough forms. Do not overmix.
Chill dough for 30 minutes. Roll out thin. Cut small rounds. Press into miniature tart molds (2-3 cm diameter).
Prick bottoms with a fork. Bake at 170°C for 10-12 minutes, until golden. Cool completely.
For the Dark Chocolate Ganache: Chop 100g dark chocolate. Place in a heatproof bowl.
Heat 100ml heavy cream and 20g butter until simmering. Pour hot cream over chocolate. Let stand 1 minute.
Stir gently from center outwards until smooth and glossy. Stir in vanilla extract. Cool to room temperature.
For the Raspberry Gel: Combine 50ml raspberry puree, 10g sugar, and 0.5g agar-agar in a small saucepan.
Bring to a boil, stirring constantly. Simmer 1 minute. Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until set.
Once set, cut into small cubes or blend until smooth. Pipe small dots or place small cubes onto ganache.
For the Candied Hazelnuts: Toast whole hazelnuts lightly. Heat 5g sugar and 15ml water in a small pan until sugar dissolves.
Add hazelnuts. Cook, stirring, until sugar crystallizes and coats nuts. Cool. Roughly chop a few.
Assembly: Pipe cooled chocolate ganache into baked sablé tartlet shells. Fill almost to the brim.
Place 2-3 small cubes of raspberry gel or pipe a small dot of smooth gel onto each ganache-filled tartlet.
Garnish with a single candied hazelnut piece or a few chopped candied hazelnuts on each petit four.
Arrange 6-9 finished petit fours artfully on a serving platter.

recipes.recipe_name: Dark Chocolate Hazelnut Entremet with Raspberry
recipes.visual_description: The entremet is a cylindrical form, approximately 6 cm in diameter, showcasing precise layers. A thin, golden-brown hazelnut dacquoise forms the base. Above it, a rich, glossy dark chocolate crémeux layer, followed by a vibrant, translucent raspberry gelee. The top layer is a light, airy milk chocolate mousse, impeccably smooth. The entire entremet is coated in a mirror-like dark chocolate glaze, reflecting light. It is presented centrally on a pristine white porcelain plate, leaving abundant negative space. A single, perfectly fresh raspberry is placed delicately beside the entremet, and a small, artfully placed chocolate curl adorns the top. The scene is illuminated by dramatic professional lighting, casting soft shadows. The background is ultra-minimalist, emphasizing the entremet's architectural precision and sophisticated simplicity.
instructions: Preheat oven to 170°C.
Whip egg whites and 20g granulated sugar to stiff peaks.
Fold in sifted icing sugar, ground hazelnuts, and flour.
Spread thinly onto a parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake 12-15 minutes until lightly golden.
Cool. Cut into a 5 cm circle for dacquoise base.
Melt 75g dark chocolate over a double boiler.
Whisk egg yolks and 10g granulated sugar until pale.
Heat milk and 50ml cream in a saucepan until simmering.
Temper egg mixture with hot milk mixture. Return to saucepan.
Cook gently, stirring constantly, until thickened. Do not boil.
Pour hot cream mixture over melted chocolate. Emulsify until smooth.
Pour crémeux into a 5 cm silicone mold. Freeze 30 minutes until firm.
Bloom 1g gelatin leaf in cold water.
Combine raspberries, 10g granulated sugar, and 15ml water in a small saucepan. Simmer until raspberries soften.
Pass mixture through a fine-mesh sieve to remove seeds. Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved.
Pour gelee over the firm crémeux layer in the mold. Freeze until solid.
Bloom 1.5g gelatin leaf in cold water.
Melt milk chocolate over a double boiler.
Whip 150ml cream to soft peaks.
Gently heat 20ml cream. Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved.
Combine melted chocolate with gelatin mixture. Fold in remaining whipped cream until just combined.
Place the dacquoise circle at the bottom of a 6 cm diameter entremet ring or silicone mold.
Unmold the frozen crémeux-gelee insert. Place it on top of the dacquoise.
Pour milk chocolate mousse around and over the insert, filling the mold to the top.
Smooth the top. Freeze overnight until completely solid.
Prepare chocolate glaze: Heat 50ml cream and glucose syrup until simmering.
Pour over 50g chopped dark chocolate. Let sit 1 minute, then whisk until smooth. Cool to 30-32°C.
Unmold the frozen entremet. Place on a wire rack over a baking sheet.
Pour the glaze evenly over the frozen entremet, ensuring full coverage.
Allow excess glaze to drip off. Carefully transfer the glazed entremet to a serving plate.
Garnish with a fresh raspberry and a delicate chocolate curl.
Allow to thaw in the refrigerator for at least 2-3 hours before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Dark Chocolate Raspberry Hazelnut Entremet
recipes.visual_description: A single, impeccably cut slice of Dark Chocolate Raspberry Hazelnut Entremet is centered on an elegant, round porcelain dessert plate with a subtle gold rim. The slice stands tall, revealing distinct, architectural layers. The top is coated in a flawless, ultra-glossy dark chocolate mirror glaze, reflecting soft ambient light. Beneath the glaze, a rich, dark chocolate mousse forms the main body, exhibiting a smooth, creamy texture. A vibrant red layer of raspberry confit provides a striking color contrast, nestled above a thin, crunchy layer of hazelnut praline. The base is a delicate, light brown hazelnut dacquoise. The plate features abundant negative space, emphasizing the dessert's minimalist elegance. A single, perfectly ripe fresh raspberry is placed precisely beside the entremet, accompanied by a small, artfully placed dark chocolate shard and a delicate wisp of edible gold leaf. The setting is a pristine white marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that creates soft shadows, enhancing the dessert's sculptural quality. The background is ultra-minimalist and uncluttered.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.

For Hazelnut Dacquoise: Toast 15g hazelnuts. Grind finely with 5g powdered sugar and 2g cornstarch. Whip 30g egg white to soft peaks. Gradually add 15g caster sugar, whip to stiff, glossy meringue. Fold in hazelnut mixture. Pipe a 6cm diameter disk onto parchment paper. Bake 12-15 minutes until lightly golden. Cool.

For Hazelnut Praline Crunch: Toast 10g hazelnuts. Make dry caramel with 5g caster sugar. Pour over hazelnuts. Cool completely. Break into pieces. Process into a coarse praline. Melt 5g dark chocolate. Mix with praline until combined.

For Raspberry Confit: Combine 30g raspberries, 5g caster sugar, 2ml lemon juice, and 1g pectin in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Cook 2-3 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened. Cool completely.

For Dark Chocolate Mousse: Bloom 2g gelatin leaves in cold water. Heat 15ml milk in a saucepan. Whisk 15g egg yolk with 5g caster sugar. Slowly pour hot milk into egg mixture, whisking constantly. Return to saucepan. Cook over low heat, stirring, until thickened slightly (nappe consistency). Do not boil. Remove from heat. Stir in 30g finely chopped dark chocolate until melted and smooth. Squeeze excess water from gelatin; stir into chocolate mixture until dissolved. Let cool to 30°C. Whip 50ml cold heavy cream to soft peaks. Fold whipped cream into chocolate mixture in two additions. Add 1ml vanilla extract.

Assembly: Line a 7cm diameter ring mold with acetate strip. Place cooled dacquoise disk at the bottom. Spread hazelnut praline crunch evenly over dacquoise. Spoon raspberry confit over praline layer. Gently pour dark chocolate mousse to fill the mold. Smooth top. Freeze for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, until solid.

For Dark Chocolate Mirror Glaze: Bloom 2g gelatin leaves in cold water. In a small saucepan, combine 25ml water and 30g caster sugar. Bring to a boil, then remove from heat. Stir in 25ml heavy cream. Pour hot mixture over 25g finely chopped dark chocolate. Let sit 1 minute. Squeeze excess water from gelatin; add to chocolate mixture. Blend with an immersion blender until smooth and glossy. Avoid incorporating air bubbles. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Let cool to 30-32°C.

Glazing: Remove frozen entremet from mold and acetate. Place on a wire rack set over a tray. Pour mirror glaze evenly over the frozen entremet, ensuring full coverage. Let excess drip off. Gently transfer entremet to a serving plate.
Thaw entremet in the refrigerator for 2-3 hours before serving.
Garnish with a fresh raspberry, a tiny chocolate shard, and a small piece of edible gold leaf.
notes: Ensure each component is properly chilled or frozen before assembly for clean layers and stability.
The mirror glaze temperature is critical for a smooth, even coating.
Use high-quality dark chocolate for best flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Dark Chocolate Crémeux, Raspberry Fluid Gel, Hazelnut Praline
recipes.visual_description: The dessert is presented on a pristine white bone china plate, allowing ample negative space. A perfectly formed quenelle of dark chocolate crémeux, deep brown with a silken sheen, is positioned slightly off-center. Adjacent to it, a vibrant ruby-red pool of raspberry fluid gel, its surface smooth and reflecting light, creates a striking color contrast. Scattered artfully around these elements are irregular shards and crumbles of golden-brown hazelnut praline, providing a crucial textural counterpoint. A single, delicate, and precisely curved vanilla tuile stands upright, adding architectural height and a subtle cream hue. The composition is organic and flowing, each element intentionally placed to create visual harmony and elegance. The setting features a premium grey veined marble surface, a crisp white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle, and minimalist silver flatware. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the sculptural quality of the dish.
instructions: For the Dark Chocolate Crémeux:
Chop dark chocolate finely. Place in a bowl.
Split vanilla bean. Scrape seeds into a saucepan with cream and milk. Heat gently until simmering. Remove from heat. Steep 10 minutes.
Whisk egg yolks and granulated sugar in a separate bowl until pale.
Slowly pour hot cream mixture over egg yolks, whisking constantly. Return mixture to saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly with a spatula, until mixture thickens slightly and coats the back of a spoon (nappe consistency). Do not boil.
Strain custard through a fine mesh sieve directly over the chopped chocolate. Let sit 1 minute.
Emulsify with an immersion blender until smooth and glossy. Pour into a container. Cover surface with cling film. Chill minimum 4 hours, preferably overnight.
For the Raspberry Fluid Gel:
Combine fresh raspberries, 10g sugar, and 50ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes until raspberries soften.
Pass mixture through a fine mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids. You should have approximately 70ml raspberry juice.
Return raspberry juice to a clean saucepan. Whisk in agar-agar powder. Bring to a boil, whisking constantly. Boil 1 minute.
Pour liquid into a shallow dish. Chill until firm (about 30 minutes).
Once firm, cut into cubes. Blend in a high-speed blender until completely smooth and fluid. Store in a squeeze bottle or covered in the refrigerator.
For the Hazelnut Praline:
Toast hazelnuts in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant. Rub in a clean towel to remove skins. Cool.
Combine 30g caster sugar and 10ml water in a small saucepan. Cook over medium heat without stirring until it turns an amber caramel.
Remove from heat. Add toasted hazelnuts. Stir to coat evenly.
Pour mixture onto a silicone mat or parchment paper. Spread thinly. Let cool completely and harden.
Break hardened praline into small pieces. Process in a food processor until a fine, sandy texture or until it forms a paste (depending on desired consistency). Store in an airtight container.
For the Vanilla Tuile:
Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking tray with a silicone mat or parchment paper.
Cream unsalted butter and icing sugar until light and fluffy.
Gradually whisk in egg white until combined.
Fold in plain flour and vanilla extract until just combined. Do not overmix.
Spread a very thin layer of batter onto the prepared baking tray using an offset spatula or stencil to create desired shapes (e.g., elongated curves).
Bake 5-7 minutes, or until edges are golden brown. Watch carefully as they burn quickly.
Remove from oven. Immediately drape over a rolling pin or curved surface to create a curved shape as they cool and harden. If they harden before shaping, return to oven for 30 seconds to soften.
Assembly:
Spoon a quenelle of the chilled Dark Chocolate Crémeux onto one side of a pristine white plate.
Spoon a generous dollop of Raspberry Fluid Gel next to the crémeux, allowing it to spread slightly.
Sprinkle Hazelnut Praline around the crémeux and gel, focusing on varied textures.
Carefully place one curved Vanilla Tuile upright, leaning subtly against the crémeux or gel for height and visual interest. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Rhubarb and Strawberry, Basil Crémeux, Almond Tuile, Vanilla Chantilly
recipes.visual_description: The dessert is presented on a pristine white bone china plate with a subtle grey rim, resting on a polished grey veined marble surface. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, emphasizing the dish's architectural precision and abundant negative space. A small, organic dollop of pale green basil crémeux is positioned off-center. Alongside it, vibrant red roasted rhubarb batons and halved strawberries are artfully arranged in a flowing, natural composition, showcasing their tender texture and concentrated color. A delicate, golden-brown almond tuile is elegantly placed upright, providing a crisp, airy contrast. A small, perfectly formed quenelle of ivory vanilla chantilly sits gracefully beside the fruit, its smooth surface inviting. The overall presentation is minimalist, emphasizing the purity of ingredients and the precision of technique, with colors harmonizing against the stark white plate.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Cut rhubarb into 5 cm batons. Halve strawberries. Toss fruit with 30g granulated sugar on a baking sheet. Roast 10-15 minutes until tender but holding shape. Cool completely.

Bring 100ml heavy cream and milk to a simmer. Add basil leaves. Remove from heat. Steep 15 minutes. Strain, pressing basil to extract flavor. Whisk egg yolks with 40g granulated sugar until pale. Slowly temper hot basil cream into egg mixture. Return to low heat. Stir constantly until mixture thickens, coats spoon. Do not boil. Strain crémeux into a bowl. Chill completely.

Preheat oven to 160°C. Whisk egg white until frothy. Sift almond flour, powdered sugar, and a pinch of salt. Fold into egg white. Gently fold in melted butter. Spread thin circles of batter onto a silicone mat or parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake 8-10 minutes until golden brown at edges. Immediately shape over a rolling pin or cylinder while warm. Cool.
Scrape seeds from vanilla bean half into 100ml cold heavy cream. Whip cream until soft peaks form. Do not overmix.

Spoon a dollop of basil crémeux onto one side of a deep plate. Arrange roasted rhubarb batons and strawberry halves artfully next to crémeux. Place an almond tuile upright into the crémeux. Add a small quenelle of vanilla chantilly near the fruit.
notes: Ensure all components are thoroughly chilled before assembly for best texture and presentation.
The basil crémeux can be made a day in advance.
Tuiles must be shaped immediately after baking as they cool quickly.

recipes.recipe_name: Celeriac and Apple Terrine with White Wine Reduction and Toasted Hazelnuts
recipes.visual_description: A single, meticulously cut rectangular terrine portion is centered on a minimalist, matte white bone china plate. The terrine, displaying distinct, compressed layers of pale cream celeriac and light yellow apple, rises elegantly from the plate. Alongside, a controlled, artistic swoosh of deep amber white wine reduction adds a contrasting liquid element. A scattering of coarsely chopped, golden-brown toasted hazelnuts provides textural contrast, with a few resting delicately on the terrine and around its base. Two small, vibrant green sprigs of fresh dill are precisely placed on top of the terrine, offering a final touch of color and height. The plate sits on a premium grey-veined marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, rests adjacent to the plate. Dramatic, professional lighting casts soft, intentional shadows, highlighting the dish's textures and forms. The background is ultra-minimalist, emphasizing abundant negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a refined main course, optionally accompanied by a very small, crisp green salad with a light vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a small terrine mold (approx. 15x5 cm) with parchment paper.
Peel celeriac and apple. Slice both thinly, about 2 mm thick, using a mandoline for uniformity.
Season celeriac and apple slices lightly with salt and pepper.
Arrange alternating layers of celeriac and apple slices tightly in the prepared terrine mold. Press down firmly after each layer.
Drizzle lightly with olive oil. Cover the mold tightly with foil.
Bake for 45-60 minutes, or until celeriac is tender when pierced. Remove from oven.
Place a weight (e.g., a small board with cans) on top of the foil-covered terrine. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight, to press and set.
For the white wine reduction: In a small saucepan, combine white wine and vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Reduce liquid by half, until slightly thickened and syrupy. Stir in butter until melted and glossy. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Toast hazelnuts in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant and lightly browned. Chop coarsely.
To serve, carefully unmold the terrine. Cut one precise rectangular or square portion, about 2 cm thick.
Garnish the terrine with a few delicate dill sprigs.
notes: Ensure celeriac and apple slices are uniformly thin for even cooking and clean layers.
Pressing the terrine is crucial for its firm texture and clean presentation.

recipes.recipe_name: Tatlı Kabaklı Aşure
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Tatlı Kabaklı Aşure is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl of a natural cream hue, resting on a light, textured bamboo mat. The pudding itself is a creamy, rustic blend of soft, tender red lentils and pearl barley, showcasing warm, earthy tones of beige and light brown from the grains and legumes. Interspersed within are inviting, soft orange cubes of roasted kabocha squash, their caramelized edges adding depth. Subtle flecks of dark, sweet onion paste are visible, along with chewy pieces of diced dried apricots, dates, and plump raisins. The texture is thick and comforting, yet still yielding. The dish is garnished minimally with a small scattering of roughly chopped, raw pistachios and a few thinly sliced rounds of dried fig, offering contrasting natural textures and muted colors. A single small, fresh mint leaf adds a subtle green accent. The composition is clean and ingredient-focused, with ample white space around the bowl. The setting features a light, reclaimed wood table surface. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from the side, creating gentle shadows and highlighting the natural textures of the food and ceramics. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is casually placed beside the bowl. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of natural greenery out of focus.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm or at room temperature.
Traditionally garnished with chopped nuts and a sprinkle of cinnamon.
Often prepared and shared communally during the Islamic month of Muharram.
instructions: Soak lentils and barley separately overnight. Drain thoroughly.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Peel and dice kabocha squash into 2cm cubes. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly caramelized.

Finely mince the red onion. In a small pot, combine minced onion with 50ml water and a tiny pinch of salt. Cook over very low heat, stirring occasionally, until water evaporates and onion is very soft and translucent, about 15-20 minutes.
Add 10ml grape molasses to the onion. Continue cooking slowly until deeply caramelized and jam-like, another 10-15 minutes. Set aside.
In a large pot, combine drained barley, drained lentils, cinnamon stick, diced dried apricots, diced dates, and raisins. Add 1.2 litres water.

Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer, stirring occasionally, for 45-60 minutes. Cook until barley and lentils are very tender and creamy. Add more water gradually if the mixture becomes too thick.
Stir in the roasted squash cubes and the caramelized onion paste. Add the remaining 30ml grape molasses.
Simmer for another 10 minutes to allow flavors to meld. Remove the cinnamon stick.
Serve warm in individual bowls.
notes: This recipe emphasizes plant-based ingredients and natural sweeteners, aligning with sustainable culinary practices.
The use of dried fruits serves as a form of preservation and adds concentrated natural sweetness.
The deeply caramelized onion paste transforms the vegetable into a sweet, complex flavor note, demonstrating a zero-waste approach to ingredient transformation.
traditional_techniques: Aşure preparation (slow simmering of grains and legumes)
Pekmez (grape molasses) as a natural sweetener

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Mushroom and Brown Rice Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, centrally mounded with a natural, organic flow. The warm brown rice forms the base, interspersed with rich, earthy roasted mushrooms, their surfaces lightly caramelized and varied in shape (sliced, quartered). Bright green baby spinach leaves and vibrant red halved cherry tomatoes provide pops of color and freshness, artfully distributed. Small, creamy cubes of Taleggio cheese are visible, some slightly softened. Chopped toasted walnuts are sprinkled over, providing texture. A light drizzle of the grains of paradise vinaigrette coats the ingredients. Freshly chopped green parsley is scattered as a garnish. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple, light wooden table surface. Beside the plate, a neatly folded cotton napkin and standard European flatware are placed. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a cozy restaurant ambiance. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish.

ingredients.name: Mixed mushrooms (cremini, shiitake, oyster), sliced or quartered

instructions: Cook brown rice according to package directions. Fluff with a fork. Set aside.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss sliced or quartered mushrooms with 2 tbsp olive oil, minced shallots, minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Spread evenly on a baking sheet.
Roast mushrooms for 15-20 minutes, until tender and lightly browned.

While mushrooms roast, prepare the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 2 tbsp olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, honey, and ground grains of paradise. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine cooked brown rice, roasted mushrooms, baby spinach, halved cherry tomatoes, and chopped walnuts.
Pour dressing over the salad. Gently toss to combine.
Add cubed Taleggio cheese. Toss lightly.
Garnish with fresh parsley. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Chili-Oregano Crusted Pork Medallions with Creamy Parmesan Orzo
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, positioned on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. Creamy Parmesan orzo forms a natural, free-flowing bed, its pale ivory color contrasting with flecks of green parsley. Two or three golden-brown, pan-seared pork medallions, each 2.5 cm thick, are arranged thoughtfully atop the orzo. The pork crust is visibly seasoned with dark specks of dried oregano and red chili flakes, showcasing a crisp exterior and tender, light pink interior. A scattering of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley provides a fresh, aromatic garnish over the dish. Moderate negative space surrounds the central elements, emphasizing the food. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting textures and colors. A white cotton napkin rests beside the plate.
instructions: Slice pork tenderloin into 2.5 cm thick medallions. Season generously with salt, pepper, dried oregano, and red chili flakes. Press spices onto pork.

Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear pork medallions for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 63°C/145°F). Remove pork from skillet. Set aside to rest.
In the same skillet, melt butter with remaining 1 tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add orzo pasta to the skillet. Stir for 1 minute to lightly toast.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, until orzo is al dente and most liquid is absorbed, about 10-12 minutes.
Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Cook for 2-3 minutes until sauce thickens and is creamy. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve creamy parmesan orzo onto plates. Arrange pork medallions on top of orzo. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Herb Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of herb roasted chicken and potatoes is presented on a simple, round, cream-colored ceramic plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh is the focal point, positioned slightly off-center. Surrounding it are several rustic, deeply roasted potato wedges, their skins a rich golden hue with soft, fluffy interiors. Large, caramelized onion chunks and smashed garlic cloves are interspersed among the potatoes, adding depth of color and texture. Fresh sprigs of rosemary and thyme are casually placed on top, providing a vibrant green contrast. The arrangement is natural and unforced, with components touching and overlapping slightly. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, with a casually draped cloth napkin and standard flatware visible, all bathed in warm, cozy kitchen lighting. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a hearty, comforting home-style portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty bread for soaking up any pan juices.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 600g, peeled and cut into 2 cm wedges

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season chicken generously with half the salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges, onion wedges, smashed garlic, olive oil, remaining salt, remaining pepper, chopped rosemary, and chopped thyme. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange chicken thighs and vegetable mixture in a single layer on a large baking tray. Ensure chicken skin is facing up.
If using, pour chicken broth around the vegetables, avoiding the chicken skin.
Roast for 40-50 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden brown and crispy, potatoes are tender, and the internal temperature of the chicken reaches 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Always ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Garlic Chicken with Crispy Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Garlic Chicken with Crispy Potatoes is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, whole chicken thighs, rich with a glossy, savory garlic sauce, are positioned towards the plate's center. Beside them, a generous portion of roasted potato cubes, uniformly cut to 2-3 cm, exhibit a crispy, golden-brown exterior and fluffy interior. The sauce lightly coats the chicken, revealing bits of thinly sliced garlic. A sprinkle of vibrant green fresh parsley garnishes the dish, with a bright yellow lemon wedge placed on the side. The overall composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, standard European flatware, and a cotton napkin, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere with natural, even lighting. A small piece of rustic bread is subtly placed nearby, honoring traditional Spanish serving.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Pair with a glass of Spanish red or white wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut potatoes into 2-3 cm cubes. Toss with 30 ml olive oil, 4 crushed garlic cloves, salt, and pepper.
Spread potatoes in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast for 30-35 minutes, or until golden and crispy. Turn halfway through.
Season chicken thighs with salt, pepper, and smoked paprika.
Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add 8 thinly sliced garlic cloves to the pan. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant, do not burn.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce by half.
Stir in chicken stock and lemon juice. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pan. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Simmer for 10-15 minutes until chicken is cooked through and sauce slightly thickens.
Stir in most of the chopped parsley.
Serve chicken with crispy potatoes. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley and a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Milanese with Arugula and Parmigiano
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown, crispy pan-fried chicken Milanese cutlet is centrally placed on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The chicken is a whole piece, not sliced. A vibrant, slightly mounded pile of fresh, dark green arugula, lightly dressed with lemon and olive oil, rests artfully atop the chicken, positioned towards one side. Delicate, thin shavings of Parmigiano-Reggiano are scattered over the arugula and around the plate. A bright yellow lemon wedge is placed beside the chicken, offering a pop of color. The dish features a balanced composition with moderate negative space. The texture is a contrast of crispy chicken and fresh, tender greens. The setting is a simple light wood table with natural, even lighting. A classic silver fork and knife rest beside the plate, with a folded white linen napkin. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a modern, inviting bistro environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of simple pasta like Spaghetti Aglio e Olio or roasted potatoes.
Offer extra lemon wedges on the side for squeezing.
Pair with a crisp, dry Italian white wine such as Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
instructions: Prepare chicken: Place each chicken breast between two sheets of parchment paper. Pound with a meat mallet to a uniform thickness of 1 cm.

Set up dredging station: Place flour in a shallow dish. Beat eggs in a second shallow dish. Combine Panko breadcrumbs and 50g grated Parmigiano-Reggiano in a third shallow dish. Season each dish lightly with salt and pepper.
Coat chicken: Dredge each chicken cutlet first in flour, shaking off excess. Dip into beaten egg, letting excess drip off. Press firmly into the breadcrumb mixture, ensuring full coverage.

Pan-fry chicken: Heat 50ml olive oil and 25g butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. When butter foams, add 2 chicken cutlets. Cook 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Transfer to a wire rack. Repeat with remaining oil, butter, and chicken.
Prepare arugula salad: In a medium bowl, combine arugula. Squeeze juice from half the lemon over arugula. Drizzle with remaining 50ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss gently.

Plate: Place one cooked chicken Milanese on each plate. Top with a generous portion of dressed arugula. Using a vegetable peeler, shave additional Parmigiano-Reggiano over the arugula. Place a lemon wedge beside the chicken. Serve immediately.
notes: Pounding the chicken to an even thickness ensures even cooking.
Using Panko breadcrumbs provides a crispier crust.
Resting the cooked chicken on a wire rack prevents it from becoming soggy.

recipes.recipe_name: Aromatic East Asian Chicken Noodle Soup
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant East Asian chicken noodle soup is presented in a clean, white ceramic bowl, showcasing a single generous portion. The clear, golden-hued broth forms the base, with tender, shredded chicken pieces nestled amongst thin, delicate rice vermicelli noodles. Bright green bok choy, lightly blanched, adds a pop of color and crisp texture. The soup is artfully garnished with fresh, verdant coriander leaves, vibrant thin slices of red chili, and finely chopped green spring onion. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a light wooden table. Chopsticks and a small ceramic spoon rest beside the bowl on a simple cotton napkin. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and inviting warmth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra lime wedges for squeezing.
Offer additional fresh chili slices or chili oil on the side.
Serve alongside a small dish of bean sprouts for added crunch.
Use chopsticks and a ceramic soup spoon for an authentic dining experience.
instructions: Place chicken thighs, water, ginger, smashed garlic, white parts of spring onions, star anise, cinnamon stick, and black peppercorns in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and tender. Skim any foam from the surface.
Remove chicken from broth. Shred chicken meat into bite-sized pieces. Discard bones and skin. Set shredded chicken aside.
Strain the broth through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot. Discard all solids.
Return broth to medium heat. Stir in fish sauce, soy sauce, and sugar. Taste and adjust salt as needed.
Cook rice vermicelli noodles according to package directions. Drain well.
Blanch halved bok choy in the hot broth for 1-2 minutes until tender-crisp. Remove and set aside.
To serve, divide cooked noodles among 4 bowls. Arrange shredded chicken and blanched bok choy over noodles.
Ladle hot broth over the ingredients in each bowl.
Garnish each serving with fresh coriander, thinly sliced red chili, thinly sliced green spring onion, and a lime wedge.
Serve immediately with a side of bean sprouts.
notes: Using bone-in chicken thighs provides a richer, more flavorful broth.
Adjust the amount of fish sauce and soy sauce to suit your personal preference for saltiness and umami.
traditional_techniques: Broth simmering for deep flavor extraction

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken is elegantly presented on a round, matte white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, pan-seared and roasted boneless chicken thighs, each tender and glistening, are positioned slightly off-center. Surrounding the chicken are vibrant, roasted vegetables: several bright red, plump cherry tomatoes, thick-cut planks of tender-crisp zucchini with slight char marks, and soft, caramelized red onion wedges. A light, savory pan sauce, infused with lemon and herbs, is artfully drizzled over the chicken and vegetables. Fresh sprigs of green oregano and thyme, along with a bright yellow lemon wedge, are placed strategically as a garnish, adding color and freshness. The arrangement is organic and balanced, allowing for moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cream-colored cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors in a clean, modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the pan juices.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette complements the richness.
Roasted potatoes or couscous can be served on the side.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large oven-safe skillet, heat 30 ml olive oil over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down (if skin-on) or presentation-side down for 4-5 minutes until golden brown. Flip and sear for another 3 minutes.
Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add remaining 30 ml olive oil to the skillet. Add minced garlic, cherry tomatoes, zucchini planks, and red onion wedges. Season with salt and pepper.
Sauté vegetables for 5-7 minutes until slightly softened.
Return chicken to the skillet, nesting it among the vegetables.
In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice, lemon zest, chopped oregano, chopped thyme, and chicken broth.
Pour mixture over chicken and vegetables in the skillet.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are tender-crisp.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest in the skillet for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken is thoroughly cooked to 75°C (167°F) for safety.
Do not overcrowd the skillet during searing to ensure proper browning.
Adjust herbs based on personal preference; fresh is highly recommended for flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Lentil Shepherd's Pie
recipes.visual_description: A generous, rustic portion of Hearty Lentil Shepherd's Pie is served on a simple, round white ceramic plate. The golden-brown mashed potato topping, slightly mounded, shows peaks and valleys from a fork, with a light crispness on its surface and scattered melted Parmesan. Below, the rich, savory lentil and vegetable filling, visible where the mash is slightly uneven, reveals diced carrots, onions, and mushrooms in a thick, herb-flecked gravy. The colors are warm and earthy: deep brown for the filling, golden-cream for the potato, and flecks of green from fresh herbs. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table. In the background, the full ceramic baking dish of the pie is visible, suggesting a family meal. A plain cloth napkin is casually placed nearby. Warm, natural light from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served directly from the baking dish at the family table.
Often accompanied by a simple side of steamed green vegetables like peas or green beans.
instructions: Prepare lentils: Rinse lentils. Boil lentils in 1 litre water for 20 minutes. Drain.
Prepare vegetables: Dice carrots, onions, celery. Mince garlic. Slice mushrooms.
Sauté aromatics: Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven. Add diced onions, carrots, and celery. Cook 8-10 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook 5 more minutes.
Build base: Stir in tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes. Stir in flour. Cook 1 minute.
Add liquids and lentils: Gradually whisk in vegetable stock. Add cooked lentils, chopped thyme, and rosemary. Bring to a simmer.
Cook filling: Reduce heat. Simmer gently for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens and flavors meld. Season with salt and pepper.
Prepare mash: Peel and cut potatoes into large chunks. Boil potatoes in salted water until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.
Mash potatoes: Return hot potatoes to the pot. Add butter and milk. Mash until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Assemble pie: Preheat oven to 190°C. Pour lentil filling into a large oven-safe baking dish (approx. 30x20 cm). Spread mashed potato evenly over the filling.
Bake: Sprinkle grated Parmesan cheese over the potato. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until topping is golden brown and filling is bubbling.
Rest and serve: Let pie rest 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Cucumber, Shrimp, and Mussel Salad with Sesame-Ginger Dressing
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, showcasing a vibrant mix of colors and textures. Julienne cucumber, shredded bright orange carrots, and thinly sliced red bell pepper form the crisp base. Tender pink shrimp and dark, plump mussels are artfully distributed amongst the vegetables. Diagonally sliced spring onions add green accents. A glistening sesame-ginger dressing lightly coats the ingredients. The salad is garnished with fresh green cilantro, mint leaves, and scattered roughly chopped roasted peanuts for crunch. The plating is organized yet natural, allowing for moderate negative space. The dish sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by dark wooden chopsticks and a small ceramic sauce dish, reflecting its Southeast Asian inspiration. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its freshness.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chopsticks.
instructions: Prepare vegetables: Julienne cucumbers. Thinly slice red bell pepper. Shred carrots. Diagonally slice spring onions. Chop cilantro and mint.
Prepare seafood: If raw, steam shrimp and mussels until cooked. Cool completely. Ensure shrimp are peeled and deveined. Remove mussels from shells.
Make dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, lime juice, grated ginger, minced garlic, sriracha, and honey/maple syrup.
Assemble salad: In a large mixing bowl, combine julienned cucumber, sliced bell pepper, shredded carrots, and sliced spring onions. Add cooked shrimp and mussels.
Dress salad: Pour dressing over salad ingredients. Toss gently to coat all components evenly.
Garnish: Add chopped cilantro, mint, and roasted peanuts. Toss lightly again.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Bell Pepper & Grilled Chicken Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Mediterranean salad is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple, light-toned wooden table. The base consists of a colorful medley of roasted bell pepper strips (red, yellow, orange), crisp diced cucumber, halved ruby-red cherry tomatoes, thinly sliced crimson red onion, and dark, briny Kalamata olive halves. Grilled chicken breast chunks, golden-brown and juicy, are artfully arranged atop the vegetables, not fanned. Crumbled white feta cheese is scattered generously, contrasting with the fresh green of chopped parsley, which serves as a garnish. A light sheen of lemon-herb vinaigrette coats the ingredients. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. Beside the plate, a small, rustic ceramic bowl holds a few extra olives. A folded off-white cotton napkin and a simple fork complete the casual bistro setting under natural, even lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut bell peppers into 2cm strips. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20 minutes, until tender and slightly charred. Let cool.
Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Grill over medium-high heat for 6-8 minutes per side, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes. Cut into 2cm chunks.

While chicken rests, prepare remaining vegetables. Dice cucumber into 1cm cubes. Halve cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice red onion. Halve pitted Kalamata olives. Crumble feta cheese. Roughly chop fresh parsley.
For the dressing, whisk together remaining 85ml olive oil, juice of one lemon, red wine vinegar, and dried oregano in a small bowl. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
In a large mixing bowl, combine roasted bell peppers, diced cucumber, halved cherry tomatoes, sliced red onion, halved Kalamata olives, crumbled feta, and chopped parsley. Add grilled chicken chunks.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Gently toss to coat all components evenly.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Roasted Chicken Breast with Garlic-Thyme Jus
recipes.visual_description: The pan-roasted chicken breast is the centerpiece, presented whole with its deeply golden, crispy skin facing upwards. The chicken is plump and juicy, showing a slight sheen. It rests slightly off-center on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, creating balanced negative space. Beside it, a pool of rich, glossy pan jus, infused with roasted garlic and fresh thyme, shimmers. The sauce is a warm amber-brown. Scattered around the plate are a few bright green fresh thyme leaves and perhaps a single roasted garlic clove, adding subtle color and texture. The overall presentation is clean and elegant, highlighting the quality of the chicken and the refined simplicity of the dish. The background features a simple wooden table surface and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, emphasizing textures and colors.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry thoroughly.
Season generously with salt and black pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken breasts skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden brown and crispy.
Flip chicken breasts. Add whole garlic cloves (lightly smashed) and thyme sprigs to the skillet.
Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 200°C (390°F). Roast for 12-18 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Baste chicken occasionally with pan drippings.
Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest on a cutting board for 5-10 minutes.
Return skillet to stovetop over medium heat. Remove thyme sprigs and garlic cloves if desired.
Pour in chicken stock. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Reduce liquid by half, about 5 minutes.
Remove skillet from heat. Whisk in butter until melted and sauce is glossy.
Serve chicken with pan jus.
notes: The resting period is crucial for juicy chicken.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Butternut Squash and Thyme
recipes.visual_description: A hearty single portion of Braised Beef with Butternut Squash and Thyme is presented centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The beef appears as tender, dark brown, irregularly shaped chunks, generously coated in a rich, glossy, deep mahogany-colored sauce. No slices are visible; the beef is in robust, whole pieces. Interspersed among the beef are soft, golden-orange cubes of butternut squash, some slightly caramelized on the edges, others gently integrated into the sauce, providing a contrast in color and texture. The thick, savory braising liquid pools around the ingredients, clinging to them, indicating a well-reduced consistency. A small sprig of fresh green thyme is artfully placed atop the dish, adding a vibrant pop of color and aromatic freshness. The arrangement is natural and inviting, not overly geometric, with moderate negative space on the plate. The colors are rich and warm, showcasing the depth of flavor. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. Beside the plate, a neatly folded light grey cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are arranged. The scene is illuminated by soft, even natural lighting, casting gentle shadows that enhance the texture without harshness. The background is subtly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 4-5 cm cubes. Pat dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Dredge beef cubes lightly in flour.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Dice onions into 2 cm pieces. Mince garlic. Peel butternut squash, remove seeds, and cut into 3-4 cm cubes.
Add onions to the pot, sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add garlic and tomato paste, cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine, scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer, reduce by half.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add beef stock and 4 thyme sprigs. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover and reduce heat to low.
Braise for 1.5 hours. Add butternut squash cubes. Continue to braise for another 45-60 minutes, or until beef is very tender and squash is soft.
Remove thyme sprigs. Skim any excess fat from the surface. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste. If sauce is too thin, simmer uncovered for a few minutes to reduce.
notes: For best results, braise the beef slowly until fork-tender. The sauce will thicken naturally from the flour on the beef and reduction.

recipes.recipe_name: Lomo Saltado
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lomo Saltado presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features 3cm chunks of seared beef sirloin with a deep brown crust. These are mixed with thick, glossy wedges of purple red onion and bright red Roma tomatoes. Golden, thick-cut potato batons are scattered through the beef mixture, all coated in a dark, shimmering sauce. A neat, molded dome of fluffy white rice sits on the side of the plate. Fresh green cilantro leaves garnish the top. The scene is set on a light wooden bistro table with a white cotton napkin and a small side bowl of spicy green aji sauce. The lighting is natural and even.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Aji Verde (green chili sauce)
Accompany with Inca Kola or a glass of red wine
Traditionally eaten with both rice and potatoes in the same meal

ingredients.name: Red onions, cut into thick wedges
Roma tomatoes, cut into thick wedges

instructions: Season beef chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Sear beef in batches until browned and medium-rare.
Remove beef from wok and set aside.
Add remaining oil to the wok.
Stir-fry onion wedges for 2 minutes until slightly charred but crisp.
Add garlic and aji amarillo paste. Stir for 30 seconds.
Return beef to the wok.
Pour in soy sauce and red wine vinegar. Toss quickly.
Add tomato wedges. Stir for 30 seconds to warm through.
Fold in the cooked potato fries and half the cilantro.
Remove from heat immediately.
Serve with white rice.
notes: Ensure the wok is extremely hot before adding beef to achieve a smoky flavor.
Do not overcook the tomatoes; they should be warm but hold their shape.
The potatoes should be added at the very last second to maintain some crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Turkey Piccata with Lemon-Caper Linguine
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Turkey Piccata with Lemon-Caper Linguine is presented on a pristine, round white porcelain dinner plate. Golden-brown pan-seared turkey breast medallions, cooked to a tender finish, are arranged artfully atop a mound of perfectly coiled al dente linguine. The pasta is coated in a glossy, light-yellow lemon-caper sauce, flecked with small, dark capers. A generous sprinkling of finely chopped fresh green parsley provides a vibrant contrast, scattered over both the turkey and pasta. Two bright yellow lemon wedges rest on the side of the plate. The overall color palette is warm and inviting, with varied textures from the seared turkey, smooth pasta, and fresh herbs. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, with standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin positioned beside it, under soft, natural, even lighting that highlights the dish's freshness and simple elegance. The background is a subtly blurred, casual restaurant setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the sauce
instructions: Prepare turkey. Slice turkey breast into 1.5 cm thick cutlets. Pound lightly to 1 cm thickness. Season with salt and pepper. Dredge lightly in flour.

Cook turkey. Heat 15 ml olive oil and 30 g butter in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear turkey cutlets 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (75°C internal). Remove turkey. Set aside.
Cook pasta. Boil salted water in a large pot. Add linguine. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 125 ml pasta water.
Make sauce. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil and 30 g butter to the pan. Deglaze with chicken broth. Add lemon juice and capers. Bring to a simmer.
Finish sauce. Stir in reserved pasta water. Simmer until slightly thickened. Stir in half the fresh parsley.
Combine. Add drained linguine to the pan with the sauce. Toss to coat.
Serve. Plate linguine. Top with turkey cutlets. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Dulce de Limón Fermentado y Almendras
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a rustic, light beige handcrafted ceramic plate with a subtly textured finish, reminiscent of traditional Spanish pottery. The surface beneath is a light, reclaimed wood table with visible grain. A natural, undyed linen napkin in a neutral tone rests casually beside the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene from the side, creating gentle shadows. A generous portion of "Dulce de Limón Fermentado y Almendras" is scattered naturally across the plate, avoiding any rigid patterns. Small, irregular pieces of candied lemon zest, translucent and golden-yellow, are interspersed with roughly chopped, toasted Marcona almonds, showcasing their varied shapes and light golden-brown color. The candied lemon pieces have a slightly crystalline, sugary coating, adding texture. A very subtle, almost imperceptible dusting of fine anchovy powder delicately settles on some pieces, offering a hint of umami without being visually dominant. The overall presentation is clean and minimalistic, emphasizing the natural beauty and texture of each ingredient. The negative space on the plate is ample, allowing each element to stand out. The scene is uncluttered, with a soft, out-of-focus background that might include a hint of a green plant, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a sweet 'tapa' or small bite after a meal.
Offer alongside strong Spanish coffee or a glass of sweet sherry.
Present on small individual ceramic dishes or a single sharing platter.

ingredients.name: High-quality anchovy fillets in olive oil

instructions: Wash lemons thoroughly. Peel zest from lemons using a vegetable peeler, avoiding white pith. Cut zest into 1 cm wide strips.
Place lemon zest strips in a clean, sterilized glass jar. Add 100g caster sugar.
Seal jar loosely. Shake to coat zest. Let ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Shake daily. Zest will soften and release liquid.
Drain fermented lemon zest. Reserve liquid for other uses.
Rinse zest under cold water. Place zest in a saucepan. Cover with fresh water. Bring to a boil, simmer 5 minutes. Drain. Repeat this boiling and draining step two more times to reduce bitterness.
In the same saucepan, combine remaining 200g caster sugar and 200ml water. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar dissolves.
Add blanched lemon zest to the sugar syrup. Simmer gently over low heat for 45-60 minutes. Zest will become translucent. Syrup will thicken.
Remove zest from syrup with a slotted spoon. Place strips on a wire rack set over parchment paper. Let dry at room temperature for 24-48 hours until firm but still pliable.
Preheat oven to 160°C. Spread Marcona almonds on a baking tray. Toast for 8-10 minutes until lightly golden and fragrant. Let cool. Roughly chop.

Prepare anchovy dust: Gently blot anchovy fillets very dry with paper towels. Place on a small piece of parchment paper. Bake in the preheated oven at 100°C for 15-20 minutes until completely dry and brittle. Cool completely. Grind to a very fine powder using a mortar and pestle or spice grinder.
Once candied lemon zest is dry, cut into small, irregular pieces (approx. 1-2 cm).
Combine candied lemon pieces and chopped toasted almonds in a bowl. Toss gently.
Arrange on a serving plate. Just before serving, very lightly dust with anchovy powder. A tiny pinch per serving is enough.
notes: Fermentation enhances flavor depth and acts as a natural preservative.
This recipe utilizes lemon peels, reducing food waste and embracing a zero-waste approach.
The anchovy provides a unique umami counterpoint to the sweetness, a sustainable use of a small amount of preserved fish.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato and Olive Risotto with Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: A creamy, vibrant Tomato and Olive Risotto is served in a shallow, matte white porcelain bowl. The risotto presents a rich orange-red hue from crushed tomatoes, punctuated by dark, glossy halves of Kalamata olives and delicate white threads of Parmesan. Its texture is fluid and al dente, not dry. A light dusting of freshly grated Parmesan and a scattering of bright green basil leaves garnish the surface, adding fresh aroma and color contrast. The bowl sits centrally on a light wooden table, typical of a modern bistro. A silver fork and spoon rest on a white cotton napkin beside it. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a warm restaurant ambiance, with natural, even lighting highlighting the dish's inviting appeal. The entire bowl is visible with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a 'primo piatto' (first course) or main dish.
Accompany with crusty bread like ciabatta.
Pair with a light, dry white wine, such as Pinot Grigio.

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.quantity: 80 g, freshly grated, plus extra for serving

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Stir in Arborio rice. Toast rice for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine, if using. Stir until fully absorbed.
Stir in crushed tomatoes.
Begin adding warm broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly.
Wait for broth to be nearly absorbed before adding the next ladleful.
Continue adding broth and stirring for 18-20 minutes. Risotto should be creamy and al dente.
Stir in halved Kalamata olives.
Remove from heat. Stir in cold butter and half of the grated Parmesan cheese.
Cover and let rest for 2 minutes (mantecare).
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust broth quantity for desired risotto consistency. It should be creamy and flow freely, not be stiff.
Use good quality Arborio rice and freshly grated Parmesan for the best flavor and texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Sausage Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy Chicken and Sausage Risotto is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple light wooden table. The risotto forms a natural, fluid pool, not mounded, displaying a golden hue. Visible within are browned, irregular chunks of chicken, crumbled Italian sausage, and bright red diced tomatoes. Vibrant green fresh basil leaves and a dusting of grated Parmesan cheese generously top the dish. The plating is clean with moderate negative space. A polished silver fork and spoon rest beside the plate, with a folded light grey cotton napkin. Soft, natural lighting highlights the fresh ingredients and appealing textures. The background suggests a casual restaurant atmosphere, minimally blurred.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately after resting.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the creamy sauce.

ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 2 cm cubes

instructions: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Add crumbled sausage. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Remove sausage with a slotted spoon; set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add chicken cubes. Cook until browned on all sides and cooked through. Remove chicken; set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and carrot to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and chopped savory. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes to toast the rice until edges become translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until wine is fully absorbed.
