Stir in the smoked cod roe. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and black pepper as needed. Fish roe can be salty, so season carefully.
Gently fold in the cooked cod chunks. Do not overmix to keep the fish pieces intact.
Serve immediately, garnished with finely chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheddar and Gherkin Croquettes with Poached Eggs
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table in a modern bistro style. Three golden-brown, oblong cheddar and gherkin croquettes, each about 7 cm long, are arranged neatly. They boast a crisp, textured breadcrumb crust. A single, perfectly poached egg, with a bright white and visible, trembling yolk, rests atop one croquette. The interior of the croquettes, subtly visible, shows creamy, cheesy, gherkin-flecked potato. Vibrant green, finely chopped chives are scattered over the egg and croquettes, adding a fresh color contrast. The plating is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. A simple cotton napkin and traditional flatware complete the approachable yet refined restaurant presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: A simple green salad
instructions: Boil peeled and cubed potatoes in salted water until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well. Mash thoroughly until smooth. Set aside.

In a saucepan, melt 50g butter over medium heat. Add 50g plain flour and cook, stirring constantly, for 1-2 minutes to form a roux. Gradually whisk in warm milk until a thick, smooth béchamel sauce forms. Season with salt, pepper, and Dijon mustard if using.

In a large bowl, combine mashed potatoes, béchamel sauce, grated cheddar, and finely diced gherkins. Mix well. Adjust seasoning. Let the mixture cool completely in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour, or until firm.
Divide the chilled mixture into 12 equal portions. Shape each portion into an oval or cylindrical croquette, about 6-7 cm long.

Set up a dredging station: one bowl with 100g plain flour, one bowl with 2 beaten eggs, and one bowl with breadcrumbs. Roll each croquette first in flour, then dip in beaten egg, then roll in breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan or deep fryer to 170°C. Fry croquettes in batches for 3-4 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crispy. Drain on paper towels. Keep warm.

Fill a wide, shallow pan with water. Add white vinegar. Bring to a gentle simmer. Carefully crack each of the remaining 4 eggs into separate small bowls. Gently slide eggs into simmering water. Poach for 3-4 minutes for a runny yolk. Remove with a slotted spoon.
Place three hot croquettes on each plate. Top each serving with one poached egg. Garnish with chopped fresh chives. Serve immediately.
notes: The gherkins provide a tangy counterpoint to the rich cheddar and potato.
Ensure croquette mixture is well chilled for easier shaping and to prevent them from falling apart during frying.

recipes.recipe_name: Grilled Halloumi with Roasted Apricots and Arugula
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant single serving is presented on a clean white round porcelain plate, centered on a light wooden table surface. At the heart, golden-brown grilled halloumi planks, approximately 1 cm thick and 5 cm long, are arranged slightly overlapping on a bed of fresh, dark green arugula leaves. The halloumi exhibits distinct char marks from grilling. Around the halloumi, several roasted apricot halves, their cut sides revealing soft, warm orange flesh with slightly caramelized edges, are artfully placed. Crumbled white feta cheese is scattered generously over the halloumi and apricots, adding contrasting texture and color. A glistening, dark balsamic glaze is drizzled in a controlled, fluid pattern across the entire dish. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. Standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin rest beside the plate, all under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Combine balsamic vinegar and honey in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 10-15 minutes until thickened to a syrupy consistency. Set aside.

Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve apricots and remove pits. Toss apricot halves with 15ml olive oil. Arrange cut-side up on a baking sheet. Roast for 10-15 minutes until slightly softened and caramelized at the edges.

Slice halloumi into 1 cm thick planks. Heat a grill pan or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. Brush halloumi with remaining 45ml olive oil. Grill halloumi for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and grill marks appear. Cook in batches if necessary.

Divide arugula among 4 plates. Arrange grilled halloumi planks over the arugula. Place roasted apricot halves around the halloumi. Crumble feta cheese generously over the dish. Drizzle with balsamic glaze. Garnish with fresh mint leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Grilled Lamb Chops with Apricot-Mint Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly grilled lamb loin chop, with caramelized brown grill marks and a juicy medium-rare interior, rests on a bed of vibrant green arugula. A bright apricot-mint salsa is spooned generously over and beside the lamb, featuring small cubes of orange apricots, finely chopped fresh mint, and tiny flecks of red onion. This adds a fresh, textural pop of color. Crumbled white feta cheese is scattered artfully over the lamb and salsa, providing creamy, salty contrast. The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, set on a simple light wooden table, with a cotton napkin beside. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. Natural, even lighting highlights the fresh ingredients and inviting textures. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a refined individual portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of couscous or roasted potatoes.
Offer warm pita bread for scooping up the salsa.

ingredients.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil
ingredients.quantity: 75 ml (30 ml for salsa, 15 ml for lamb, 30 ml for arugula)

instructions: Pat lamb chops dry. Season generously with salt, pepper, garlic powder, and dried oregano. Drizzle with 15 ml olive oil. Let sit at room temperature for 15 minutes.

Prepare apricot-mint salsa: Dice fresh apricots into small cubes (approx. 0.5 cm). Finely chop fresh mint leaves. Combine diced apricots, chopped mint, finely diced red onion, lime juice, and 30 ml olive oil in a small bowl. Season with salt and pepper. Stir well.
Preheat a grill pan or outdoor grill to medium-high heat.
Place lamb chops on the hot grill. Grill for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness (internal temperature 63°C for medium-rare).
Remove lamb chops from grill. Rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine arugula and 30 ml olive oil. Toss gently.
Divide arugula among 4 plates. Place 1 lamb chop on top of the arugula on each plate.
Spoon a generous amount of apricot-mint salsa over and beside each lamb chop.
Crumble feta cheese over the lamb chops and salsa. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust grilling time based on lamb thickness and desired doneness.
Fresh, firm apricots are best for the salsa to maintain texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Corn & Bell Pepper Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken is presented on a cream-colored, handcrafted ceramic plate. The chicken is cut into thick, succulent pieces, displaying a golden-brown crust from searing. It rests on a generous, creamy dollop of savory yogurt. Alongside the chicken, a vibrant mound of golden fermented corn kernels, interspersed with finely diced red bell pepper and flecks of green basil, adds a pop of natural color and texture. Bright red julienne strips of quick-pickled bell pepper are neatly arranged, providing a sharp visual contrast. The plating emphasizes natural shapes and negative space. The dish sits on a light bamboo surface, complemented by an undyed linen napkin and soft natural light. The background is clean and minimal, allowing the ingredients to shine.
instructions: Prepare Chicken Brine: Dissolve 30g salt in 1 litre cold water. Submerge chicken breasts. Brine for 30 minutes. Remove chicken, pat very dry.

Prepare Fermented Corn & Bell Pepper Relish: Dice 50g bell pepper trimmings and 20g basil stems very finely. Combine with corn kernels. Dissolve 10g salt in 200ml water to make brine. Pack corn mixture into a clean jar. Pour brine over, ensuring vegetables are submerged. Seal loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until tangy. Refrigerate.

Prepare Quick-Pickled Bell Peppers: Cut remaining bell pepper into thin julienne strips. In a small saucepan, combine white wine vinegar, 40ml water, and sugar. Bring to a boil, stirring to dissolve sugar. Remove from heat. Place bell pepper strips in a heatproof jar. Pour hot brine over peppers. Let cool completely. Refrigerate.

Prepare Savory Yogurt: Strain yogurt through a cheesecloth-lined sieve for 30 minutes to thicken slightly. Finely chop 10g fresh basil leaves. Stir into strained yogurt with a pinch of salt and pepper.

Cook Chicken: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add brined chicken breasts. Sear 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest chicken 5 minutes.

Plate Dish: Spoon savory yogurt onto the centre of each plate. Slice rested chicken breasts into thick pieces. Arrange chicken on top of the yogurt. Spoon fermented corn relish alongside chicken. Place quick-pickled bell pepper strips next to the relish. Garnish with a few fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Apple and Bell Pepper Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, single-serving rice bowl is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The bowl, centered on a simple wooden table, holds a base of fluffy, off-white basmati rice. Neatly arranged on top is a generous portion of the bell pepper and black bean mixture. This mixture showcases rich red, yellow, and orange bell pepper cubes (2 cm) alongside dark black beans, coated in a reddish-brown, glossy sauce. Beside the main mixture, a neat pile of fresh, crisp mixed salad greens provides a bright green contrast. Small, bright white apple cubes (1 cm) are scattered over the top, adding a fresh texture. Bright green chopped fresh coriander is sprinkled over the dish. A vibrant green lime wedge rests on the bowl's rim. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. A cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The background suggests a modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Rinse rice. Cook rice with water or broth according to package directions. Set aside.
Dice bell peppers into 2 cm cubes. Dice red onion into 1.5 cm cubes. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced bell peppers and red onion. Sauté 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, cumin, and smoked paprika. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes (undrained), rinsed black beans, and hot sauce. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened. Season with salt and pepper.
Dice apple into 1 cm cubes.
To serve, divide cooked rice among 4 bowls. Top each with the bell pepper-bean mixture.
Arrange fresh salad greens on one side of the bowl. Sprinkle diced apple over the top.
Garnish with fresh chopped coriander and a lime wedge. Serve hot with extra hot sauce on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Carrot & Pomelo Tartlets with Sweet Goat Cheese and Spiced Lobster Bits
recipes.visual_description: Four individual tartlets are casually arranged on a well-used, light wooden dining table. Each tartlet, nestled in its simple ceramic plate with natural imperfections, features a golden-brown, rustic pastry shell. The filling, a vibrant orange from the carrot and pomelo, peeks out, topped with a generous, artfully swirled dollop of creamy white goat cheese. A scattering of glossy, golden-brown spiced lobster bits provides a contrasting texture and visual intrigue on top of the cream. The overall presentation is natural and unpretentious, with components touching as if freshly plated for a family meal. The scene is illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting, casting soft shadows. A simple, colorful, patterned cloth, reminiscent of Ethiopian textiles, is casually draped beneath the plates, adding a subtle cultural nod without overwhelming the food. Nearby, a rustic, unglazed ceramic cup or bowl might sit, hinting at a comfortable, lived-in atmosphere. The focus remains on the comforting, homemade appeal of the tartlets themselves.

ingredients.name: For the Sweet Goat Cheese Cream
For the Spiced Lobster Bits
ingredients.quantity: 100 grams cooked lobster meat, finely diced

instructions: Prepare tartlet shells: Combine flour, butter, and icing sugar in a food processor. Pulse until crumbly. Add egg yolk and cold water. Pulse until dough forms. Wrap dough in cling film. Chill 30 minutes.
Roll dough on a lightly floured surface. Cut out four circles. Press into 10 cm tartlet molds. Prick bottoms with a fork. Chill 15 minutes.

Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Line tartlet shells with parchment paper. Fill with pie weights or dried beans. Bake blind 15 minutes. Remove weights and parchment. Bake 5-7 minutes more until lightly golden. Cool completely.
Make carrot and pomelo filling: Place diced carrots in a small saucepan. Add 2 tablespoons water. Cook until very tender. Drain any excess water. Mash or blend carrots until smooth.

In a separate saucepan, whisk pomelo juice, zest, sugar, white port, and cornstarch. Heat over medium, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens. Remove from heat. Stir in pureed carrots. Mix well. Cool completely.
Prepare sweet goat cheese cream: In a bowl, combine goat cheese, cream cheese, and icing sugar. Beat with an electric mixer until smooth and creamy. Set aside.

Make spiced lobster bits: In a small non-stick pan, combine diced lobster meat, sugar, white port, and crushed grains of paradise. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring, until liquid evaporates and lobster is coated and slightly caramelized. Spread on parchment paper. Let cool and harden. Chop into small, crunchy bits.
Assemble tartlets: Spoon carrot and pomelo filling into cooled tartlet shells. Top each with a generous dollop of sweet goat cheese cream. Swirl cream gently with a spoon for a homely touch.
Sprinkle spiced lobster bits over each tartlet just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken, Broccoli, and Rice Bake with Cheesy Potato Topping
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of the creamy chicken, broccoli, and rice bake is served on a sturdy, off-white ceramic dinner plate. The top layer of mashed potatoes is golden-brown with slightly crisped peaks, revealing a hint of melted, bubbling cheddar cheese. The potatoes are naturally scooped, showing a soft, yielding texture. Beneath the topping, the creamy filling is visible, featuring tender, irregular chunks of white chicken, vibrant green broccoli florets, and soft, pearly rice grains intertwined in a rich, savory sauce. The dish is presented on a well-used, rustic wooden dining table, with natural, warm kitchen light illuminating the scene. A simple, folded linen napkin and a plain water glass are subtly placed nearby, enhancing the homely, comforting atmosphere. No fanned meat, just hearty, inviting food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad.
Accompany with crusty bread for scooping.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Boil potato chunks in salted water until very tender. Drain well. Mash with 30g butter, a splash of milk, salt, and pepper until smooth. Set aside.
Cook rice according to package instructions. Set aside.

Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add diced chicken. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 20g butter to the skillet. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk and chicken broth. Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens and begins to simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in 100g grated cheese until melted and smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper.
Add cooked chicken, broccoli florets, and cooked rice to the cheese sauce in the skillet. Stir gently to combine. Pour mixture into a 2.5-liter baking dish.
Evenly spread mashed potatoes over the chicken and rice mixture.
Sprinkle remaining 50g grated cheese and paprika over the mashed potatoes.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and the filling is bubbly.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley or chives.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust seasoning to taste throughout the cooking process.

recipes.recipe_name: Framboise & Lemon Verbena Petit Fours
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine identical, exquisitely crafted petit fours are artfully arranged on a pristine white French porcelain rectangular platter. The arrangement is organic and flowing, creating elegant negative space. Each petit four features a delicate, pale cream-colored lemon verbena crémeux dome, crowned with a vibrant, translucent framboise gelée disc. Beneath the crémeux, a thin, light-golden rice flour dacquoise base, subtly studded with white sesame, provides a refined foundation. A thin, dark black sesame tuile shard is precisely positioned beside each petit four, adding architectural height and contrasting color. A single fresh, ruby-red raspberry and a tiny, bright green micro mint leaf are placed with precision on each gelée disc, offering fresh color and natural elegance. The platter rests on a polished, light grey veined Carrara marble surface. A precisely folded white linen napkin sits to the side. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the textures and dimensionality of each component. The background is ultra-minimalist, emphasizing the pristine presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served traditionally on an elegant French porcelain platter, reflecting the European origins of petit fours in a modern Australian context.
instructions: For the White Sesame Dacquoise:
Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Toast white sesame seeds lightly. Crush finely.
Whip egg whites to soft peaks. Gradually add caster sugar, whip to stiff, glossy meringue.
Sift icing sugar, ground almonds, and rice flour together. Fold gently into meringue.
Fold in crushed white sesame seeds.
Spread batter thinly onto prepared baking sheet. Bake 12-15 minutes, until lightly golden and firm. Cool completely. Cut into 3cm diameter discs.
For the Lemon Verbena Crémeux:
Bloom 1g gelatin in cold water.
Combine lemon juice, zest, lemon verbena leaves, and 40g caster sugar in a saucepan. Heat gently until sugar dissolves. Steep 10 minutes. Strain out verbena leaves.
Whisk egg yolks into lemon mixture. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin. Let cool to 40°C.
Whisk in cold, diced unsalted butter until smooth and emulsified. Chill until firm.
For the Framboise Gelée:
Bloom 1.5g gelatin in cold water.
Gently warm raspberry puree with 15g caster sugar until sugar dissolves. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin and framboise eau de vie.
Pour into a shallow dish to a depth of 0.5cm. Chill until firm. Cut into 2.5cm diameter discs.
For the Black Sesame Tuile:
Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking sheet with silicone mat or parchment.
Melt 20g unsalted butter. Let cool slightly.
Whisk icing sugar, 20g egg white, and all-purpose flour until smooth.
Stir in melted butter and black sesame seeds.
Spread very thin, small oval or irregular shapes onto prepared baking sheet. Bake 5-7 minutes, until crisp and edges are golden. Cool on a rack.
Assembly:
Pipe a dome of lemon verbena crémeux onto each dacquoise disc.
Place a framboise gelée disc on top of each crémeux dome.
Garnish each petit four with one fresh raspberry and one micro mint leaf.
Arrange 6-9 assembled petit fours artistically on a serving platter. Place black sesame tuile shards beside each petit four.
notes: Ensure all components are chilled for clean assembly.
Work quickly when assembling to maintain the integrity of the delicate elements.

recipes.recipe_name: Sous Vide Chicken Breast, Carrot Purée, Crispy Rice, Onion Consommé
recipes.visual_description: The dish is a study in sophisticated minimalism, presented on a pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, delicate pattern along the rim. The background is an ultra-minimalist, dark wooden table with dramatic professional lighting creating soft shadows that emphasize the dish. A precisely folded white linen napkin sits beside the plate. A single, perfectly seared chicken breast, its skin a deep, inviting golden-brown, is the focal point, positioned slightly off-center. Its form is natural and untouched. Adjacent to the chicken, a small, elegant quenelle of vibrant orange carrot purée, incredibly smooth and glossy, provides a contrasting color and texture. Scattered around the main elements are irregular, airy shards of crispy, puffed Arborio rice, a delicate off-white, offering a sharp textural counterpoint. A small, clear, amber-hued pool of onion consommé gently surrounds a portion of the chicken, reflecting the ambient light. A single, fresh chervil sprig, its delicate green leaves, is meticulously placed atop the chicken, adding a final touch of color and elegance. Each component is positioned with architectural precision, allowing abundant negative space on the plate to enhance the visual impact of the perfectly executed elements.
instructions: Prepare Onion Consommé: Combine sliced shallots, chicken stock, bay leaf, and peppercorns in a saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 20 minutes. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth. Discard solids. Season consommé with salt. Keep warm.

Prepare Chicken: Season chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper. Place each breast in a separate vacuum-sealable bag with a sprig of thyme. Vacuum seal bags. Cook in a sous vide bath at 63°C for 1.5 hours.

Prepare Carrot Purée: In a saucepan, combine chopped carrots and 100ml chicken stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until carrots are very tender (about 15-20 minutes). Drain most liquid, reserving a tablespoon. Transfer carrots to a high-speed blender. Add 30g butter and reserved liquid. Blend until exceptionally smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Season with salt and white pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare Crispy Rice: Rinse Arborio rice. In a small pot, combine rice and 500ml water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until rice is very soft and overcooked (about 30 minutes). Drain excess water. Spread cooked rice very thinly onto a silicone mat or parchment paper. Dehydrate in an oven at 80°C for 3-4 hours, or until completely dry and brittle. Break dried rice into irregular small pieces. Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 180°C. Fry dried rice pieces in batches until puffed and crispy (a few seconds). Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt.

Finish Chicken: After sous vide, remove chicken from bags. Pat very dry. Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 4-5 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip and cook for 1-2 minutes on the flesh side to ensure even cooking and internal temperature of 75°C. Add remaining 5g butter to the pan in the last minute, basting chicken. Rest chicken for 5 minutes.

Plate: Spoon a small, elegant swirl or quenelle of carrot purée slightly off-center on each plate. Place one rested chicken breast (skin-side up) next to the purée. Arrange a few irregular pieces of crispy rice artfully around the chicken. Pour a small pool of warm onion consommé beside the chicken. Garnish with a few small chervil leaves or microgreens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Lamb Shanks with Herbed Parmesan Crust
recipes.visual_description: A single braised lamb shank, rich brown and falling-off-the-bone tender, rests prominently on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. The shank is partially submerged in a glossy, dark reddish-brown red wine reduction sauce, showcasing its depth and richness. Sliced braised mushrooms are visible within the sauce. A vibrant sprinkle of golden-brown herbed parmesan breadcrumbs generously tops the lamb, adding a contrasting texture and bright color. A small sprig of fresh rosemary and thyme is placed beside the shank as a garnish. The plate is set on a simple light wooden table. A folded cotton napkin is placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and deep colors. The entire plate is in view, with moderate negative space, creating a professional yet approachable presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Season lamb shanks generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear lamb shanks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove lamb from pot.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 3 minutes.
Add tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Simmer for 5 minutes, reducing wine by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef stock, thyme sprigs, rosemary sprigs, and bay leaf.
Return lamb shanks to the pot. Ensure shanks are mostly submerged. If not, add more stock.
Bring liquid to a simmer. Cover the pot tightly.
Transfer pot to the preheated oven. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until lamb is fork-tender.

While lamb braises, prepare the herbed parmesan crust. In a bowl, combine panko breadcrumbs, grated parmesan cheese, melted butter, and 5g chopped fresh thyme leaves and 5g chopped fresh rosemary leaves. Mix well.
Remove lamb from oven. Carefully remove shanks from the sauce. Set aside.
Strain the braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan. Discard solids. Skim off any excess fat.
Bring strained sauce to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Reduce until slightly thickened to desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper.
Return lamb shanks to the sauce or plate individually.
Serve shanks with a generous spoonful of sauce. Top each shank with a sprinkle of herbed parmesan crust. Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: The braising liquid can be prepared a day ahead and refrigerated. Skim off solidified fat before reheating.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Chicken and Mushroom Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Tuscan Chicken and Mushroom Tagliatelle is presented in a shallow white porcelain bowl. Golden tagliatelle pasta forms a generous base. Tender, golden-brown chicken breast chunks, approximately 2cm thick, are nestled throughout. Earthy, thickly sliced sautéed mushrooms and vibrant halved cherry tomatoes are evenly distributed, coated in a light, glossy rustic tomato sauce. Freshly grated Parmesan cheese and bright green chopped basil leaves are scattered over the dish, providing contrast and freshness. The composition is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space. The bowl rests on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights colors and textures, with a softly blurred casual bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a light-bodied Italian red wine like Chianti.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Rest for 5 minutes. Cut into 2cm thick chunks.
Slice mushrooms thickly. Dice onion. Mince garlic. Halve cherry tomatoes.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the same pan. Sauté diced onion 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Sauté 5-7 minutes until browned and tender.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer 2 minutes until wine reduces slightly.
Add halved cherry tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes soften and sauce thickens slightly.
While sauce simmers, cook tagliatelle according to package instructions in a large pot of salted boiling water until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 60ml pasta water.
Add cooked tagliatelle to the sauce. Add chicken chunks. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water a little at a time until desired consistency.
Finely chop fresh basil. Grate Parmesan cheese.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh basil and grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Parmesan with Creamy Polenta
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown pan-fried chicken cutlet, approximately 1.5 cm thick, is presented whole, topped with melted fresh mozzarella slices and grated parmesan. It rests atop a generous bed of creamy, flowing yellow polenta. A vibrant red fresh tomato and basil sauce, with visible diced tomatoes and minced garlic, is spooned generously over the chicken, spilling slightly onto the polenta. Fresh basil leaves, roughly torn, are scattered for color and aroma. The dish is served on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table. A folded cotton napkin sits beside the plate. The composition features moderate negative space, highlighting the dish's rich colors and varied textures under natural, even lighting. Traditional flatware accompanies the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread for dipping into the sauce.
Pair with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Prepare chicken: Pound each chicken breast to 1.5 cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.

Set up breading station: Place flour in one shallow dish, beaten eggs in a second, and breadcrumbs in a third. Dredge each chicken piece in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg, then coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere.

Pan-fry chicken: Heat 30ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry chicken 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Work in batches if necessary. Drain cooked chicken on paper towels.

Make tomato sauce: In a saucepan, heat remaining 30ml olive oil over medium heat. Sauté diced onion and minced garlic until fragrant, about 3-4 minutes. Add crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat and cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Stir in half of the chopped fresh basil. Season with salt and pepper.

Cook polenta: Bring chicken broth to a boil in a medium pot. Slowly whisk in polenta. Reduce heat to low, stir constantly for 5-7 minutes until creamy and thick. Stir in butter and 50g grated parmesan. Season with salt and pepper.

Assemble and bake: Place cooked chicken cutlets in a baking dish. Top each piece with sliced fresh mozzarella and 15g grated parmesan. Bake in the preheated oven for 5-7 minutes, until cheese is melted and bubbly.

Serve: Ladle creamy polenta onto individual plates. Top with a baked chicken cutlet. Spoon generous amount of tomato basil sauce over chicken and polenta. Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves, roughly torn.
notes: Ensure chicken breasts are pounded to an even thickness for uniform cooking.
For extra flavor, lightly toast breadcrumbs before coating chicken.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Fermented Garlic Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Roasted Chicken with Fermented Garlic Pasta is presented on a handcrafted, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The pasta, featuring rigatoni tossed with vibrant green seasonal greens and finely chopped herbs, forms a natural, organic mound in the center. Its texture is al dente, coated in a light, glossy sauce. Beside the pasta, two or three roasted chicken thighs, cut into thick, golden-brown chunks, are placed simply, showcasing their crispy skin and tender interior. A few fresh herb leaves are scattered lightly as a natural garnish. The composition emphasizes clean lines and ample white space, highlighting the natural colors and textures of the ingredients. The setting is a light-colored, natural wood table. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone and a minimalist, clean background with soft, diffused natural lighting complete the eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Place chicken skin-side up on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes until skin is crispy and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add rigatoni. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
Reserve 250ml of pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add minced fermented garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chopped rosemary and thyme. Cook for 30 seconds. Add chopped seasonal greens. Cook until wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Add cooked rigatoni to the pan with the greens. Gradually add reserved pasta water, tossing constantly, until a light sauce forms and coats the pasta.
Slice rested chicken thighs into thick chunks. Do not fan out.
Serve pasta onto plates. Arrange chicken chunks alongside or on top of the pasta. Drizzle with fresh lemon juice. Grate lemon zest over each serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Sirloin with Roasted Potatoes and Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared beef sirloin steak, cooked to a medium-rare, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. The steak displays a deep, even brown crust from searing. Beside it, a generous pile of roasted potato wedges, golden and slightly crisp on the exterior with a fluffy interior, are artfully arranged. Thinly sliced, deeply caramelized onions, rich amber in color, are nestled against the potatoes. Sautéed cremini mushroom slices, earthy brown and tender, are scattered around the base of the steak and potatoes. A light drizzle of pan sauce, glossy and dark, coats the beef. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley. The entire plate is visible on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors against a subtly blurred, inviting bistro background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and cut potatoes into 2cm thick wedges. Toss with 30ml olive oil, salt, pepper, and rosemary. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast potatoes for 30-35 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender-crisp.
While potatoes roast, thinly slice onions. Melt 20g butter and 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add onions.
Cook onions slowly for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and soft. Season with salt.
Slice mushrooms. In a separate pan, melt 20g butter over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms.
Sauté mushrooms for 7-10 minutes until golden brown and tender. Season with salt and pepper.
Pat beef sirloin steaks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed skillet over high heat until smoking.
Carefully place steaks in the hot pan. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or adjust for desired doneness.
Add remaining 20g butter, crushed garlic, and thyme sprigs to the pan during the last 2 minutes of cooking. Tilt pan and baste steaks with melted butter.
Remove steaks from pan and rest on a cutting board for 5-10 minutes.
Deglaze the skillet with red wine (if using) and beef broth, scraping up browned bits. Simmer for 3-5 minutes until slightly reduced to form a pan sauce.
Plate each steak centrally. Arrange roasted potato wedges, caramelized onions, and sautéed mushrooms around the beef. Drizzle with pan sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure beef is rested properly after cooking to retain juices.
Adjust cooking time for steak based on desired doneness.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Ginger Chili Chicken with Fragrant Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a single generous portion. Central are several succulent, pan-seared chicken chunks, approximately 3-4 cm, with a golden-brown crust. Beside the chicken, a neat mound of fluffy, fragrant jasmine rice is perfectly shaped. Finely chopped fresh coriander leaves are generously sprinkled over both chicken and rice, providing a vibrant green contrast. Thin, bright red slices of bird's eye chili are scattered over the chicken. Golden julienned ginger strands glisten on the chicken. A fresh lemon wedge sits alongside. The presentation is clean, organized, and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table. Elegant wooden chopsticks are placed to the right, and a small white rice bowl is positioned slightly behind, completing a modern bistro setting with an authentic Asian touch. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chopsticks and a small individual rice bowl.
instructions: Rinse jasmine rice thoroughly. Cook rice with 450 ml chicken stock according to package instructions until fluffy. Keep warm.
Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Finely mince garlic. Peel and julienne ginger. Thinly slice red chilies.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large wok or pan over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear chicken until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil to the pan. Add minced garlic, julienned ginger, and sliced chilies. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return chicken to the pan. Add soy sauce, fish sauce, and sesame oil. Toss to coat chicken evenly.
Remove from heat. Squeeze juice from one lemon over chicken. Grate zest from half a lemon into the pan.
Chop fresh coriander. Stir half of the coriander into the chicken mixture.
Serve chicken mixture immediately over fragrant jasmine rice. Garnish with remaining fresh coriander and lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Cherry Mochi Bites
recipes.visual_description: The Fermented Cherry Mochi Bites are presented as individual, irregularly shaped, soft white spheres, each dusted lightly with fine white cornstarch, suggesting a natural, unrefined quality. Each mochi is plump, revealing a subtle translucency. They are arranged artfully on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone, allowing ample negative space around each piece. Some mochi are gently broken open to reveal the vibrant, deep ruby-red of the lacto-fermented cherries, contrasting beautifully with the rich, dark brown chunks of chopped chocolate and the creamy, irregular pieces of macadamia nuts within. The texture is soft and yielding. The plate rests on a light, naturally textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige hue is folded loosely nearby. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the subtle textures of the mochi and the organic shapes of the ingredients. A few small, edible green leaves, perhaps from a cherry stem or a simple herb, are scattered sparingly on the plate, serving as a zero-waste garnish. The overall composition is clean, minimalist, and celebrates the raw beauty of each ingredient.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a wholesome, ingredient-focused snack.
Offer with a small glass of the leftover cherry fermentation brine, diluted, as a refreshing probiotic drink.

ingredients.name: cornstarch or potato starch, for dusting

instructions: Wash cherries. Pit them. Place pitted cherries in a clean glass jar.
Dissolve salt in filtered water to make a brine. Pour brine over cherries, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight if needed.

Cover jar loosely or use an airlock. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days. Check for small bubbles. Taste after 3 days; they should be pleasantly tart. Once fermented, store in refrigerator.
Roughly chop macadamia nuts. Finely chop dark chocolate. In a small bowl, combine chopped macadamia nuts and dark chocolate. Set aside.
In a microwave-safe bowl, combine glutinous rice flour, icing sugar, and water. Whisk until smooth.
Cover bowl loosely with cling film or a plate. Microwave on high for 1 minute. Stir well with a wet spatula.
Microwave again for 1 minute. Stir. Repeat once more for a total of 3 minutes cooking. The dough should be translucent and sticky.
Dust a clean surface generously with cornstarch. Scrape hot mochi dough onto the dusted surface.
Carefully flatten the dough into a rectangle using a cornstarch-dusted rolling pin or hands. Aim for 3-4 mm thickness.
Cut the mochi dough into 8 equal squares (approximately 6x6 cm).
Place a small amount of chocolate-macadamia filling in the center of each mochi square. Top with 1-2 fermented cherries.
Gently bring the corners of the mochi square together, pinching to seal the edges and form a ball. Dust with more cornstarch as needed to prevent sticking.
Place sealed mochi seam-side down on a plate.
notes: Adjust sweetness of mochi or filling based on tartness of fermented cherries.
The fermentation brine can be used in smoothies or dressings.
traditional_techniques: Traditional mochi preparation techniques adapted for modern kitchen

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pan Rosemary Garlic Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty One-Pan Rosemary Garlic Chicken and Potatoes is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with a slightly rustic edge. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned baked chicken thigh sits prominently at the center, its skin slightly crinkled from roasting. Around the chicken, generous chunks of roasted potatoes are scattered, some showing their fluffy interior, others with crispy, golden-brown edges. Interspersed are bright orange carrot chunks, softened and caramelized at the edges, and tender, translucent onion wedges. A light dusting of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the dish, adding a fresh contrast. The components are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, conveying a comforting, homemade feel. The plate sits on a well-worn, light-colored wooden kitchen table, subtly showing natural grain and minor imperfections. In the background, out of focus, a simple, folded checkered cloth napkin and a standard fork are casually placed, suggesting a relaxed family meal. Warm, soft light illuminates the dish from the side, highlighting the textures and natural colors of the roasted ingredients. The overall presentation is homely, inviting, and unpretentious, emphasizing satisfying portions and simple, delicious food.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut potatoes and carrots into 2.5 cm chunks. Cut onion into 2 cm wedges. Mince garlic.

In a large bowl, combine potato chunks, carrot chunks, and onion wedges. Add 30 ml olive oil, half of the minced garlic, half of the rosemary, half of the thyme, 2.5 ml salt, and 1.25 ml black pepper. Toss to coat vegetables evenly.
Spread seasoned vegetables in a single layer on a large baking sheet.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season chicken thighs all over with remaining salt, pepper, rosemary, and thyme.
Rub remaining 30 ml olive oil and minced garlic onto the chicken thighs.
Place chicken thighs skin-side up among the vegetables on the baking sheet.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Flip vegetables and continue baking for another 20-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and vegetables are tender and lightly browned.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Black Bean & Seaweed Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, savory bowl of black beans and vegetables rests on a simple, well-used wooden dining table. The cooked short-grain rice forms a base in an everyday ceramic bowl, slightly off-white with natural imperfections. A generous portion of the dark, glossy black bean and vegetable mixture is spooned over the rice. The black beans are plump and intact, mixed with vibrant orange diced carrots and earthy brown sliced shiitake mushrooms. A light sheen from the savory sauce coats the ingredients. Freshly sliced green scallions are sprinkled over the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. A scattering of toasted white sesame seeds provides subtle texture. The overall presentation is natural and unpretentious, reflecting a comforting home-cooked meal. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests casually beside the bowl on a simple cloth napkin. A small dish of vibrant red kimchi sits nearby as an accompaniment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of kimchi.
Offer pickled radishes or other banchan.
Provide a small bowl of gochujang for optional added spice.
instructions: Soak dried black beans overnight. Rinse thoroughly.
In a large pot, combine soaked beans, kombu, and 1 liter water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer 60-90 minutes until beans are tender. Remove kombu. Drain beans, reserving cooking liquid.
Heat cooking oil in a large pot or deep skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced carrot and sliced shiitake mushrooms. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in cooked black beans. Pour in 500ml reserved bean cooking liquid. Add soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, and brown sugar. Bring to a simmer.
Cook 10-15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and vegetables to tenderize.
Mix cornstarch with 20ml water to create a slurry. Stir slurry into the simmering mixture. Cook 1-2 minutes until sauce thickens.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot over cooked short-grain rice. Garnish with sliced scallions and toasted sesame seeds.
notes: Adjust sweetness and saltiness of the sauce to your preference.
For extra umami, a dash of mushroom seasoning can be added.

recipes.recipe_name: Honey-Lemon Spiced Fruit Salad
recipes.visual_description: A homely fruit salad is presented in a simple, off-white ceramic bowl, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The bowl is generously filled with natural portions of fruit. Firm ripe pears are cut into uniform 1.5 cm cubes, their pale yellow flesh contrasting with the deep, glossy purple-black of whole, plump blackberries. A light, golden honey-lemon dressing subtly coats the fruit, reflecting the warm, cozy kitchen lighting. A few fresh green mint leaves are casually placed on top as a functional garnish. The overall arrangement is natural and inviting, with some fruits gently overlapping. A plain cloth napkin and a simple dessert spoon rest beside the bowl, completing the relaxed, lived-in family kitchen scene.
instructions: Wash and dry all fruit.
Peel, core, and dice pears into 1.5 cm cubes.
Place diced pears in a large mixing bowl.
Gently add fresh blackberries to the bowl.
Zest the lemon directly over the fruit.
Squeeze lemon juice into a small bowl.
Add honey and ground cinnamon to the lemon juice.
Whisk dressing ingredients until combined.
Pour dressing over the fruit.
Gently toss fruit to coat evenly.
Divide fruit salad among four serving bowls.
Garnish each serving with a few fresh mint leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Black Bean and Wakame Patties with Sesame-Ginger Glaze
recipes.visual_description: Two golden-brown, pan-fried black bean and wakame patties are the focal point, stacked slightly off-center on a pristine white round porcelain plate. The patties, approximately 2cm thick, exhibit a crisp exterior and are generously coated with a glistening, dark amber sesame-ginger glaze. Finely sliced bright green green onions are scattered artfully over the patties, accented by a sprinkle of toasted white sesame seeds. Beside the patties, a small, neat mound of julienned quick-pickled cucumber offers a vibrant green and white contrast. The plate is positioned on a simple light wooden table. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests beside the plate on a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and rich colors of the dish. The background features a blurred, casual restaurant ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice.
Offer small dishes of quick-pickled vegetables on the side.
instructions: Rehydrate wakame. Place dried wakame in a bowl. Cover with warm water for 10 minutes. Drain well. Squeeze out excess water. Roughly chop.

Prepare aromatics. Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a pan over medium heat. Add diced red onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Remove from heat.

Make patty mixture. In a large bowl, mash drained black beans with a fork until mostly smooth but still some texture. Add chopped wakame, sautéed onion mixture, panko breadcrumbs, 15ml soy sauce, and 5ml toasted sesame oil. Mix well to combine.
Form patties. Divide mixture into 4 equal portions. Form each portion into a firm, round patty, about 2 cm thick.
Cook patties. Heat remaining 15ml vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Carefully place patties in the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and heated through.

Prepare glaze. While patties cook, combine remaining 15ml soy sauce, 10ml toasted sesame oil, rice vinegar, and maple syrup in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened.
Glaze and serve. Brush or drizzle cooked patties generously with the sesame-ginger glaze. Garnish with sliced green onions and toasted white sesame seeds. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pan Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of One-Pan Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken and Potatoes is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate with a subtle, natural glaze. The plate, perhaps in an off-white or light grey, sits on a well-worn wooden dining table. The centerpiece is a golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, its skin crispy and slightly darkened from the oven. Alongside it are several rustic potato wedges, their edges crisped and interiors tender, showing some of the potato skin. Scattered amongst the chicken and potatoes are softened, caramelized lemon slices and a few fragrant sprigs of roasted rosemary and thyme. The arrangement is natural and casual, with components touching and slightly overlapping, reflecting a homely, comforting meal. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen. A simple cloth napkin and a standard fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate. The overall scene is unfussy, highlighting the expertly cooked, hearty comfort food.

ingredients.name: Small potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or new potatoes)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Cut potatoes into 2-3 cm wedges. Do not peel.
Slice lemon into thin rounds.
Smash garlic cloves with the side of a knife.
In a large bowl, combine chicken, potato wedges, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Toss well to coat.
Add lemon slices, smashed garlic, rosemary sprigs, and thyme sprigs to the bowl. Toss gently to distribute.
Spread the chicken and potato mixture in a single layer on a large baking sheet. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Roast for 40-50 minutes, or until chicken is golden brown and cooked through.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) with a meat thermometer.
Serve immediately directly from the baking sheet or transfer to a large platter.
notes: This recipe offers minimal cleanup, making it perfect for weeknight dinners.
Ensure chicken reaches a safe internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Turkey and Mushroom Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: The Creamy Turkey and Mushroom Tagliatelle is presented in a deep, pristine white porcelain bowl. Long, golden-yellow tagliatelle strands are gently twirled, forming a nest in the center. Interspersed throughout the pasta are tender, seared turkey chunks, showcasing their golden-brown edges. Earthy brown, sliced cremini mushrooms add visual depth and texture. Finely diced carrots and onions provide subtle pops of orange and white, embedded within the rich, creamy sauce. The sauce coats the pasta beautifully, appearing glossy and inviting. A generous sprinkling of vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley garnishes the top, along with a coarse grind of black pepper. The dish is framed by a simple, light wooden table and a folded cotton napkin. A single fork rests beside the bowl.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.

Add turkey cubes. Season with salt and pepper. Sear turkey until golden brown and cooked through, approximately 8-10 minutes. Internal temperature should reach 75°C. Remove turkey from skillet and set aside.
Add sliced mushrooms to the same skillet. Sauté until browned and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Remove mushrooms and set aside with turkey.
Add diced onion and carrots to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
If using, pour in white wine. Deglaze the skillet, scraping up any browned bits. Simmer until wine is mostly evaporated.
Pour in chicken stock and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return turkey and mushrooms to the skillet. Stir to combine. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 5 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Meanwhile, cook tagliatelle according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 100 ml of pasta water.
Add cooked tagliatelle directly to the sauce. Toss to coat pasta evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water as needed.
Stir in half of the chopped fresh parsley.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh parsley and a grind of black pepper.
notes: Adjust sauce consistency by adding a splash of reserved pasta water if needed.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy White Beans and Charred Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy White Beans and Charred Broccoli is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, seared chicken thigh, its exterior beautifully caramelized, rests beside a generous mound of creamy white cannellini beans. The beans are rich and slightly viscous, studded with finely diced onion and flecks of green oregano. Alongside, vibrant green broccoli florets, expertly charred with crispy edges, are arranged artfully. A few fresh oregano leaves and a bright yellow lemon wedge provide a pop of color and freshness. The dish is set on a simple light wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin and standard flatware to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and inviting colors, creating an approachable, refined bistro aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the creamy sauce.

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.quantity: 1, half for juice, half for wedges

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.

Toss broccoli florets with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Arrange in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast in a preheated oven at 200°C for 15-20 minutes, or until tender-crisp and lightly charred.

In the same skillet used for chicken (add a little more oil if needed), reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook 1 minute until fragrant.

Stir in rinsed cannellini beans, chicken stock, heavy cream, and chopped oregano. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Squeeze in juice from half a lemon.

Divide creamy white beans among four plates. Place a seared chicken thigh on top of or alongside the beans. Arrange charred broccoli florets next to the chicken. Garnish with fresh oregano leaves and a lemon wedge. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pot Chicken, Tomato & Carrot Basmati Rice
recipes.special_requests: Canned crushed tomatoes, not fresh tomatoes. Basmati rice.
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a rustic, shallow ceramic bowl, showcasing a generous, mounded portion of One-Pot Chicken, Tomato & Carrot Basmati Rice. Golden-brown chicken chunks, seared and tender, are nestled among the fluffy, reddish-orange basmati rice, which has absorbed the rich tomato flavor. Vibrant orange carrot rounds and small diced onions are visible throughout the rice, adding color and texture. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley provides a final touch of green. The overall plating is natural and inviting, with components slightly overlapping, suggesting a hearty, homemade meal. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, accompanied by a simple, casually placed cloth napkin. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting appeal.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, peeled and sliced into 0.5 cm rounds

instructions: Pat chicken chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks in batches until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add carrot rounds and minced garlic. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in basmati rice. Toast for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Return seared chicken chunks to the pot. Stir gently to combine.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly. Simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove pot from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo (Mexican Chicken and Rice)
recipes.special_requests: Canned crushed tomatoes, not fresh tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Golden-brown chicken chunks, approximately 4-5 cm, are nestled among vibrant red-orange long-grain rice. The rice is tender, with distinct grains, interspersed with bright orange 1 cm diced carrots and green cilantro. The chicken shows a perfectly seared crust. The dish is slightly mounded, allowing moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple wooden table. A folded cotton napkin is beside the plate. The dish is accompanied by a small rustic bowl of salsa roja, warm corn tortillas, and a lime wedge. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors. Traditional flatware is arranged. The background is minimal, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Offer lime wedges for squeezing
Provide a side of salsa roja or pickled jalapeños

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs
ingredients.quantity: 900 g (boneless, skinless, cut into 4-5 cm chunks)

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper.
Add chicken to the pot. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd. Cook in batches if necessary. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and carrots to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in uncooked rice. Toast rice for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until lightly golden.
Add crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, cumin, smoked paprika, and oregano. Stir well. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken chunks to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed.
Remove pot from heat. Let it rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Fluff rice with a fork. Stir in half of the fresh cilantro.
Serve hot. Garnish with remaining fresh cilantro and lime wedges.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust salt and pepper to taste before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish-Style Chicken and Saffron Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish-Style Chicken and Saffron Rice is presented on a white porcelain dinner plate. A vibrant mound of golden-orange saffron rice, with distinct grains, forms the base. Small cubes of red and yellow bell peppers, thin slices of red chili, and browned slices of cremini mushrooms are mixed throughout, adding color and texture. A single, whole bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh, with deeply golden, crispy skin, rests prominently on top. The chicken is cooked to perfection. The dish is garnished with fresh, bright green chopped parsley and a yellow lemon wedge. Moderate negative space highlights the dish. The setting features a simple wooden table surface with a cotton napkin beside the plate, under natural, even lighting, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30 mL olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken, skin-side down, until golden and crispy. About 5-7 minutes.
Flip chicken. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast for 20-25 minutes. Internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 30 mL olive oil to the same pan.
Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, diced bell peppers, and sliced chili. Cook for 5-7 minutes until vegetables soften slightly.
Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté until mushrooms release their liquid and brown, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in rice, saffron, and smoked paprika. Toast for 2 minutes.
Pour in hot chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover pan. Cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not stir excessively.
Remove from heat. Let rice rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice with a fork. Adjust seasoning.
Serve rice onto plates. Top each portion with a roasted chicken thigh.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet Suprême Rôti, Consommé de Tomate Clarifié, Purée d'Ail Doux, et Poivron Rouge Confit
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly roasted chicken suprême, its skin a deep, glossy golden-brown, rests as the centerpiece on an elegant, pristine white bone china plate. The chicken is presented whole, showcasing its succulent form. Adjacent to the chicken, a small, artfully placed quenelle of creamy, pale beige roasted garlic purée adds a soft, luxurious texture. Scattered delicately near the purée are a few irregular, tender pieces of vibrant red confit bell pepper, their rich color providing a subtle contrast. A clear, ruby-red pool of clarified tomato consommé elegantly surrounds the chicken, its transparency hinting at deep, pure flavor. The plate features abundant negative space, emphasizing the minimalist composition. A single, delicate sprig of fresh thyme or a tiny cluster of micro-greens provides the only garnish, adding a hint of fresh green. The setting is a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that creates soft shadows, enhancing the dish's architectural precision and sophisticated simplicity. A pristine white linen napkin, folded precisely, and elegant silver flatware complete the ultra-minimalist, high-end presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a sophisticated main course in a multi-course French fine-dining experience.
Accompany with a glass of crisp, dry white Burgundy wine.
instructions: Prepare Tomato Consommé: Roughly chop tomatoes. Blend until smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve, then through a cheesecloth-lined sieve. Collect clear juice.
Season juice with salt, pepper, and a pinch of sugar. Chill juice over ice until very cold.
Bring juice slowly to a bare simmer over low heat. Do not stir. Skim any impurities. Let it gently simmer for 20 minutes.
Carefully ladle clear consommé through a clean cheesecloth-lined sieve. Keep warm.
Prepare Confit Garlic Purée: Separate garlic cloves. Peel.
Place cloves in a small saucepan. Cover with olive oil. Add 2 thyme sprigs. Cook over very low heat for 45-60 minutes, until garlic is very tender and golden. Do not brown.
Drain garlic, reserving oil. Blend garlic with a splash of reserved oil and a knob of butter until silky smooth. Season with salt. Keep warm.
Prepare Confit Red Bell Pepper: Core and deseed red bell peppers. Cut into 2 cm irregular pieces.
Place in a small saucepan. Cover with olive oil. Add 1 thyme sprig. Cook over very low heat for 30-40 minutes, until very tender.
Drain, reserving oil. Season with a pinch of salt. Keep warm.
Cook Chicken Suprêmes: Pat chicken suprêmes dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat neutral oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 5-7 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy.
Flip chicken. Add shallot and 1 thyme sprig to pan.
Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C. Roast for 10-15 minutes, until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Assemble and Serve: Spoon a small, artistic smear or quenelle of garlic purée onto one side of a warm, deep plate.
Arrange a few pieces of confit red bell pepper beside the purée.
Carefully place one roasted chicken suprême on the plate, slightly overlapping the other elements.
Pour a small pool of warm tomato consommé around the chicken.
Garnish with a single tiny sprig of fresh thyme or a micro-green. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Pork & Mushroom Crostini
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion features three golden-brown crostini, each approximately 8 cm long, arranged neatly on a clean white porcelain rectangular plate. The baguette slices are lightly toasted, revealing a crisp texture. Each crostini is generously spread with a creamy, pale yellow cheddar-mustard mixture. Piled on top is a savory blend of shredded smoked pork and pan-seared sliced cremini mushrooms, with finely diced yellow onion visible throughout. The pork is tender, and the mushrooms are deeply browned. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley garnishes each crostini, adding a fresh contrast. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. The dish is set on a simple wooden table surface, illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a warm, casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
If smoked pork is raw, slow cook or braise until fork-tender. Shred the cooked smoked pork into fine strands. If pre-cooked, simply shred or finely dice.
Slice the baguette into 1.5 cm thick rounds.
Brush both sides of bread slices lightly with olive oil.
Place bread slices on a baking sheet. Toast in the oven for 5-7 minutes, until golden and crisp. Set aside.
Finely dice the yellow onion. Thinly slice the cremini mushrooms.
Heat 15 ml of olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion and sliced mushrooms to the pan. Sauté for 8-10 minutes, until tender and lightly browned.
Add shredded smoked pork to the pan with onions and mushrooms. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring to combine and heat through. Season with salt and black pepper. Remove from heat.
For the spread, finely grate the sharp cheddar cheese.
In a small bowl, combine grated cheddar cheese, Dijon mustard, and mayonnaise. Stir until well mixed and creamy.
Spread a generous layer of the cheddar-mustard mixture onto each toasted baguette slice.
Top each crostini with a spoonful of the smoked pork and mushroom mixture.
Finely chop fresh parsley. Garnish each crostini with chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Scallops, Smoked Pork Lardons, Lemon-Mustard Emulsion
recipes.visual_description: A single individual starter portion is elegantly presented on a pristine white bone china plate with a wide rim. Three perfectly seared, golden-brown scallops are artfully arranged in a flowing, organic cluster slightly off-center. Each scallop exhibits a deep, caramelized crust and a translucent, tender interior. A small, creamy pool of pale yellow lemon-mustard emulsion is precisely placed adjacent to the scallops, forming a delicate counterpoint. Scattered over and around the scallops are small, dark golden, crisp smoked pork lardons, providing textural contrast and visual depth. A few vibrant green microgreens or finely chopped chives are sparsely and intentionally placed for a pop of color. Abundant negative space surrounds the central composition, emphasizing the minimalist and sophisticated presentation. The plate rests on a premium grey veined marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, is positioned to the side. The scene is illuminated by dramatic professional lighting, casting subtle shadows that highlight the textures and forms of the dish. The background is ultra-minimalist and out of focus, drawing all attention to the food.
instructions: Render smoked pork belly: Cut smoked pork belly into small lardons. Place lardons in a cold pan. Cook over medium-low heat until crisp. Remove lardons. Reserve rendered fat.
Prepare lemon-mustard emulsion: In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, 15ml fresh lemon juice, and a pinch of lemon zest. Whisk until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Prepare scallops: Pat scallops very dry with paper towels. Season both sides with salt and pepper.

Sear scallops: Heat olive oil and 15g butter in a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until shimmering. Add scallops in a single layer. Do not overcrowd the pan. Sear for 1.5-2 minutes per side until deeply golden-brown and caramelized. Scallops should be translucent in the center. Add remaining butter to the pan during the last 30 seconds. Spoon butter over scallops.

Plate: Place 3 seared scallops per plate. Spoon a small amount of lemon-mustard emulsion next to or under each scallop. Scatter crispy smoked pork lardons over and around the scallops. Garnish with microgreens or chives if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Medallion, Dark Beer Jus, Tomato Confit
recipes.visual_description: The single seared beef medallion, approximately 50g and perfectly medium-rare, rests slightly off-center on a pristine white bone china plate. Its exterior boasts a deep, rich brown crust from precision searing. Adjacent to the beef, a glossy, dark amber dark beer jus forms a fluid, organic pool, reflecting the ambient light. Two vibrant red, subtly wrinkled confit tomato halves, their skins slightly burst, are artfully placed near the beef. A delicate, golden-brown mustard seed crisp, thin and brittle, leans elegantly against the medallion, providing textural contrast. The composition emphasizes abundant negative space, highlighting each element's refined execution. The plate sits on a polished white Carrara marble surface, accompanied by a precisely folded white linen napkin and elegant, minimalist flatware, bathed in dramatic professional lighting with deep shadows.
instructions: Cut beef tenderloin into four 50g medallions. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Place in small oven-safe dish. Add 20ml olive oil, thyme sprig, pinch salt. Bake at 120°C for 45 minutes until tender and slightly shriveled.

Finely mince shallot and garlic. Sauté in a small pot with a touch of olive oil until soft. Deglaze with dark beer. Reduce by half. Add beef stock. Simmer until reduced to a glossy, coating consistency. Strain through fine-mesh sieve. Whisk in 10g cold butter. Keep warm.
Lightly toast mustard seeds in a dry pan. Spread thinly on a silicone mat. Press with parchment paper. Bake at 150°C until crisp and flat. Break into small shards.
Heat 10ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat. Sear beef medallions 2 minutes per side for medium-rare. Rest beef 3 minutes.

Place one beef medallion slightly off-center on a white plate. Spoon a pool of dark beer jus next to the beef. Arrange two confit tomato halves near the beef. Lean one mustard seed crisp against the beef. Serve immediately.
notes: For medium-rare beef, target an internal temperature of 55-60°C. Always ensure beef reaches a safe minimum internal temperature of 63°C (145°F) and rests for 3 minutes.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Macaroni with Spinach and Tomato
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Baked Macaroni with Spinach and Tomato is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain gratin dish. The top boasts a golden-brown, bubbly crust of melted cheddar cheese and toasted breadcrumbs, offering a crispy texture contrast. Peeking from beneath the crust are creamy, perfectly cooked macaroni noodles coated in a rich, velvety cheese sauce. Vibrant green wilted spinach and small diced red tomatoes are interspersed throughout the pasta, adding pops of color and freshness. A delicate sprig of fresh oregano rests on the golden crust as a garnish. The dish is centered on a simple, light-colored wooden table, illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting. A folded white cotton napkin and standard silver fork are placed neatly beside the dish, creating a clean, inviting modern bistro aesthetic. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, hot from the oven.
A side of crisp green salad with a light vinaigrette complements the richness of the dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Grease a 2-liter baking dish.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add chopped spinach and diced tomatoes to the skillet. Cook until spinach wilts and tomatoes soften, about 3-4 minutes.
Stir in dried oregano. Remove from heat. Set aside.
In a separate saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Whisk in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk until smooth. Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens, about 5-7 minutes. Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg (if using).
Remove béchamel from heat. Stir in 150g of grated cheddar cheese until melted and smooth. This creates the cheese sauce.
Combine cooked macaroni, vegetable mixture, and cheese sauce in a large bowl. Stir until well combined.
Pour mixture into the prepared baking dish. Sprinkle remaining 50g grated cheddar cheese and breadcrumbs evenly over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until bubbly and the topping is golden brown.
notes: For an extra kick, a pinch of cayenne pepper can be added to the cheese sauce.
Any good melting cheese can be substituted for cheddar, such as Gruyère or Fontina.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Tagliatelle with Bel Paese, Spinach, and Tomato
recipes.visual_description: The baked tagliatelle is presented in a clean, white porcelain individual serving bowl. The dish features golden-brown, bubbling melted Bel Paese cheese on top, contrasting with vibrant red tomato sauce and deep green wilted spinach. Long strands of tagliatelle noodles are intertwined within the rich sauce. Cubes of Bel Paese are partially melted, creating creamy pockets throughout. A few fresh oregano leaves are scattered on top as a garnish. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. The background is a subtly blurred modern bistro setting, clean and unobtrusive.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty artisan bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a light red Italian wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook tagliatelle in salted water until al dente. Drain well.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add fresh spinach to the sauce. Cook until wilted, about 2-3 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Add cooked tagliatelle to the sauce. Gently toss to coat.
Fold in cubed Bel Paese cheese.
Transfer the mixture to a 2.5-liter baking dish.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until bubbling and the cheese is melted and lightly golden.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Cooking the pasta al dente is crucial as it will continue to cook in the oven.
Bel Paese cheese melts beautifully, creating a creamy texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Medallion, Dark Beer Jus, Mustard Tuile
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly seared beef tenderloin medallion, cooked to a tender medium-rare, rests elegantly on a pristine white bone china plate. The beef exhibits a deep, caramelized crust contrasting with its rosy interior. Beside it, a small, glossy pool of rich, dark beer jus gleams, reflecting ambient light. A delicate, golden-brown mustard seed tuile shard stands upright, leaning subtly against the beef, offering intricate texture. A few vibrant green microgreens or precisely cut chive batons provide a precise, high-contrast garnish. The plate features expansive negative space, emphasizing the minimalist composition. The setting is a premium grey-veined marble surface, with a crisp white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing depth and sophistication.
instructions: Prepare Dark Beer Jus: In a small saucepan, combine dark beer, diced shallot, smashed garlic, and thyme sprig. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce liquid by half. Add beef stock. Continue to simmer until liquid reduces to a syrupy consistency, about 100ml. Strain jus through a fine-mesh sieve, discarding solids. Return strained jus to clean saucepan. Keep warm over low heat.
