The plate sits on a simple wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish. The background is softly blurred, showing hints of a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet.
Add diced onion. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Stir in heavy cream and lemon zest. Simmer 3-5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in lemon juice, chopped parsley, and chopped dill.
Return chicken to the skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Lomo Saltado
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lomo Saltado presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features 3cm chunks of seared beef sirloin with a deep brown crust. These are mixed with thick, glossy wedges of purple red onion and bright red Roma tomatoes. Golden, thick-cut potato batons are scattered through the beef mixture, all coated in a dark, shimmering sauce. A neat, molded dome of fluffy white rice sits on the side of the plate. Fresh green cilantro leaves garnish the top. The scene is set on a light wooden bistro table with a white cotton napkin and a small side bowl of spicy green aji sauce. The lighting is natural and even.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Aji Verde (green chili sauce)
Accompany with Inca Kola or a glass of red wine
Traditionally eaten with both rice and potatoes in the same meal

ingredients.name: Red onions, cut into thick wedges
Roma tomatoes, cut into thick wedges

instructions: Season beef chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Sear beef in batches until browned and medium-rare.
Remove beef from wok and set aside.
Add remaining oil to the wok.
Stir-fry onion wedges for 2 minutes until slightly charred but crisp.
Add garlic and aji amarillo paste. Stir for 30 seconds.
Return beef to the wok.
Pour in soy sauce and red wine vinegar. Toss quickly.
Add tomato wedges. Stir for 30 seconds to warm through.
Fold in the cooked potato fries and half the cilantro.
Remove from heat immediately.
Serve with white rice.
notes: Ensure the wok is extremely hot before adding beef to achieve a smoky flavor.
Do not overcook the tomatoes; they should be warm but hold their shape.
The potatoes should be added at the very last second to maintain some crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Almond and Onion Soup with Poached Egg
recipes.visual_description: The Creamy Almond and Onion Soup is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, showcasing its comforting, creamy texture. The soup has a warm, inviting beige-yellow hue, hinting at the caramelized onions and blended almonds. A perfectly poached egg, with its tender white exterior and visible soft yolk underneath, rests gently in the center of the soup. Around the egg, a scattering of vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley adds a fresh contrast and aroma. The soup is fluid, allowing the egg to nestle naturally within. The bowl sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table, suggesting a homely family kitchen setting. A simple, slightly crumpled cloth napkin is casually placed nearby. The scene is lit with warm, natural light, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere for a comforting meal.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onions. Cook for 15-20 minutes until very soft and deeply caramelized, stirring occasionally.
Add blanched almonds and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low and cook for 10 minutes.
Carefully transfer the soup mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. Return the soup to the pot.

In a small bowl, whisk kudzu powder with 60 ml cold water to form a slurry. Stir the kudzu slurry into the simmering soup. Cook, stirring constantly, until the soup thickens slightly, about 3-5 minutes.
Stir in coconut vinegar and verjus. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Keep warm over low heat.

Meanwhile, bring a separate pot of water to a gentle simmer. Carefully crack each egg into a small bowl or ramekin. Gently slide each egg into the simmering water. Poach for 3-4 minutes until whites are set and yolks are still runny. Remove with a slotted spoon.
Ladle hot soup into four individual bowls. Gently place one poached egg in the center of each bowl.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Sausage & Artichoke Tortilla Pizzas
recipes.visual_description: Four individual Sausage & Artichoke Tortilla Pizzas are arranged casually on a rustic wooden serving board. Each pizza features a golden-baked flour tortilla base, generously spread with creamy white ricotta. Toppings are piled naturally: crumbled, browned sausage pieces, vibrant red and yellow diced bell pepper, tender green artichoke heart chunks, and golden-toasted pine nuts. A light sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley or basil adds a pop of color. The edges of the tortillas are slightly crispy and browned. The presentation is simple and inviting, as if prepared for a casual family meal. The wooden board sits on a well-used wooden dining table, with warm, natural kitchen lighting illuminating the scene. A simple ceramic plate or two, and a casually placed cloth napkin complete the homely setting. No overcrowding; appropriate negative space highlights the comfort food appeal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add ground sausage. Cook, breaking it apart, until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat. Set aside.
In the same skillet, add diced bell pepper and minced garlic. Sauté for 3-5 minutes until bell pepper softens slightly.
In a small dry pan, toast pine nuts over medium heat for 2-3 minutes until golden. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
In a bowl, combine ricotta cheese with dried oregano, salt, and black pepper. Mix well.
Place tortillas on a large baking sheet.
Spread an even layer of seasoned ricotta over each tortilla.
Distribute cooked sausage, sautéed bell pepper, and chopped artichoke hearts evenly over the ricotta.
Sprinkle toasted pine nuts over the toppings.
Bake for 8-12 minutes, or until the tortilla edges are golden and crispy, and the toppings are heated through.
Remove from oven. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or basil.
Slice each tortilla pizza into quarters. Serve immediately. Ensure sausage reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature during cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken Thighs with Lemon-Herb Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, robust portion is centered on a clean white porcelain plate, set on a simple wooden table. The focal point is a golden-skinned, bone-in chicken thigh, richly browned and crispy. Adjacent is a generous pile of roasted potato wedges, golden-crusted with soft interiors, speckled with herbs. Blistered cherry tomatoes and caramelized lemon slices are interspersed. Fresh green rosemary, thyme, and chopped parsley add vibrant color. A glistening pan sauce, made from chicken drippings and lemon, subtly pools around the dish. The composition is clean, balanced, and inviting, with moderate negative space. A white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even lighting enhances the warm, earthy tones and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the pan sauce.
Pair with a dry white wine or a light-bodied red wine.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (small, firm, e.g., baby potatoes or Yukon Gold)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Cut potatoes into 2 cm wedges or halves if small.

In a large roasting pan or oven-safe skillet, toss potatoes with 30 ml olive oil, half the rosemary, half the thyme, and 2 crushed garlic cloves. Season with salt and pepper. Spread in a single layer.
Heat a separate oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add remaining 30 ml olive oil.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy.
Flip chicken. Add remaining rosemary, thyme, and 2 sliced garlic cloves to the skillet around the chicken. Add lemon slices (from half a lemon) and cherry tomatoes.
Carefully transfer chicken skillet to the oven, alongside the potato pan if using two pans. If using one large pan, arrange chicken skin-side up over the potatoes.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender and golden.
Remove chicken and potatoes from oven. Let chicken rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
While chicken rests, place the chicken skillet (with pan drippings) on the stovetop over medium heat. Add chicken stock. Scrape up any browned bits. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced.
Squeeze juice from the remaining half lemon into the pan sauce. Stir.
Plate chicken thighs with roasted potatoes. Drizzle with pan sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken is thoroughly patted dry for crispy skin.
Do not overcrowd the roasting pan for even cooking of potatoes.
Adjust roasting time based on oven performance and chicken size.
traditional_techniques: Roasting for even cooking and flavor development

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken Thighs with Potato Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, presented whole with its deeply golden, crisp skin facing upwards, anchors one side of a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Beside it rests a precisely cut rectangular portion of potato gratin, its creamy layers visible, topped with a rich, caramelized golden-brown crust. A glossy, dark amber pan sauce is artfully drizzled over the chicken and pooled delicately around its base. A fresh, vibrant green sprig of thyme is placed thoughtfully on the chicken for garnish. The plate, with moderate negative space, sits on a simple, rustic wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are placed beside the dish, creating a refined, approachable bistro aesthetic under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Crusty baguette for soaking up sauce
Simple green salad with a light vinaigrette
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Peel potatoes. Using a mandoline or sharp knife, slice potatoes into very thin (2mm) rounds.

Rub a 20x20 cm baking dish with butter. Arrange a layer of potato slices in the dish, slightly overlapping. Season with salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg. Sprinkle with minced garlic and a few thyme leaves.
Pour a little heavy cream over the potatoes. Repeat layering until all potatoes are used, finishing with a layer of cream. Ensure top layer is well covered.
Bake gratin for 45-50 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and top is golden brown and bubbling. A knife inserted should meet no resistance.
While gratin bakes, pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy.

Flip chicken thighs. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven (180°C / 350°F) alongside the gratin. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet; set aside to rest.
Drain excess fat from the skillet, leaving about 1 tablespoon. Add diced shallot to the skillet. Sauté over medium heat for 2-3 minutes until softened.
Deglaze skillet with chicken stock, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half, about 5-7 minutes, until slightly thickened.
Stir in chopped fresh thyme and parsley. Whisk in 20g of butter until melted and sauce is glossy. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Cut gratin into 4 equal square or rectangular portions. Place one portion of gratin on each plate. Place a roasted chicken thigh beside the gratin. Spoon a generous amount of pan sauce over and around the chicken. Garnish with a small fresh thyme sprig. Serve immediately.
notes: For the gratin, using a mandoline ensures uniform thin slices for even cooking and a beautiful layered texture.
Do not overcrowd the gratin dish; ensure cream covers the top layer to prevent drying out.
Resting the chicken after roasting ensures juicy meat.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Chicken Skin Crackers with Fermented Vegetable Dip
recipes.visual_description: A minimalistic and clean presentation. Golden-brown crispy chicken skin pieces, irregularly shaped, are arranged naturally on a light, textured, handcrafted ceramic plate in an off-white tone. The chicken skins are not fanned, but casually overlapping. Adjacent to them, a small, round ceramic bowl holds the vibrant, creamy fermented vegetable dip. The dip is a natural pale green or mixed vegetable color, reflecting its fresh ingredients. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space. The setting is a light-colored reclaimed wood or bamboo surface. A simple, undyed linen napkin in a natural beige is subtly placed. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures of the chicken skin and the dip. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of natural plant greenery, emphasizing the eco-conscious theme.

ingredients.name: Mixed vegetable scraps (e.g., carrot peels, radish greens, broccoli stems, outer cabbage leaves)

instructions: Clean chicken skin. Pat dry thoroughly.
Cut chicken skin into 5cm pieces. Place in a cold frying pan.
Render chicken skin over medium-low heat. Cook slowly until deeply golden and crisp. This takes 15-20 minutes.
Remove crispy skins. Place on paper towel to drain excess fat. Season with salt.
Wash vegetable scraps. Roughly chop into 2-3cm pieces.
Combine water and salt in a clean jar. Stir until salt dissolves.
Add chopped vegetable scraps and peeled garlic clove to the jar. Ensure vegetables are fully submerged.
Seal jar tightly. Allow to ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days. Taste daily for desired tang.
Once fermented, drain vegetables. Reserve a small amount of brine.
Blend fermented vegetables with herb stems and olive oil until smooth. Add reserved brine if needed for consistency. Season with black pepper.
Serve crispy chicken skin crackers alongside the fermented vegetable dip.
notes: Utilize chicken skin, often discarded, for a flavorful snack.
Use diverse vegetable scraps for the dip to reduce food waste.
Fermentation enhances flavor and extends shelf life.
The rendered chicken fat (schmaltz) can be saved for cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Rice and Vegetable Fritters
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of two to three golden-brown Cheesy Rice and Vegetable Fritters rests casually on a simple, round white ceramic plate. The fritters, roughly 7cm in diameter, have a slightly irregular, rustic shape with visible flecks of green from the finely diced broccoli and orange from the small cubed carrots peeking through the crispy, textured breadcrumb coating. They are stacked slightly or casually overlap, showing their soft, cheesy interior where a small fritter is broken open. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley garnishes the top of the fritters and around the plate's edge. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting, creating a comfortable, inviting atmosphere. A casually folded cloth napkin is nearby, enhancing the homely feel.
instructions: Cook rice: Combine rice and chicken stock in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15-20 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Let cool.
Prepare vegetables: Steam broccoli florets and diced carrot until tender-crisp. Dice cooked broccoli and carrot into small cubes.
Combine ingredients: In a large bowl, mix cooled rice, diced broccoli, diced carrot, grated cheddar cheese, egg, flour, salt, pepper, and garlic powder. Mix thoroughly until well combined.
Form fritters: Shape the mixture into 8-10 small, flat patties (approximately 6-7 cm in diameter).
Coat fritters: Gently press each patty into the breadcrumbs, coating both sides evenly.

Pan-fry: Heat 2-3 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat. Fry fritters in batches for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and heated through. Add more oil as needed.
Serve: Transfer cooked fritters to a plate. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Onion Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Fermented Tomato & Onion Rice Bowl is presented in a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic bowl on a light-colored, reclaimed wood surface. The rice is a warm, earthy brown, studded with vibrant red diced fresh tomatoes and translucent, slightly pink fermented onion slices. The texture is soft and cohesive. A delicate scattering of crispy, deep green kale leaves rests on top, providing a contrasting texture and color. The composition is minimalistic, with ample white space around the bowl, highlighting the dish's natural beauty. A simple, undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is folded neatly beside the bowl. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene from the side, emphasizing the ingredients' natural colors and textures. The background is clean and uncluttered, with subtle hints of lush green plants, reinforcing the sustainable theme.
instructions: Prepare fermented tomatoes: Dice 2 tomatoes into 1 cm cubes. Place in a clean jar.
Prepare fermented onions: Thinly slice half a red onion. Place in a separate clean jar.
Make fermentation brine: Dissolve 15g non-iodized sea salt in 500ml filtered water. Pour over tomatoes and onions in jars. Ensure vegetables are submerged. Seal jars loosely.
Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Burp daily. Refrigerate when desired tang is reached.
Cook rice: Rinse 200g brown rice. Combine with 400ml vegetable broth in a pot. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover. Simmer 40 minutes until liquid is absorbed.
Prepare fresh vegetables: Dice remaining 2 tomatoes into 1 cm cubes. Dice white onion into small cubes. Mince garlic.
Sauté aromatics: Heat 20ml olive oil in a pan. Add diced white onion and minced garlic. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add fresh tomatoes: Stir in diced fresh tomatoes. Cook 3 minutes until slightly softened.
Combine: Add cooked rice to the pan with sautéed vegetables. Stir well.
Finish rice: Stir in fermented tomatoes and fermented onions. Add nutritional yeast and black pepper. Mix gently.
Crisp greens: Separate outer leaves of seasonal greens. Toss with a drizzle of olive oil. Bake or air fry until crispy.
Serve: Spoon rice mixture into bowls. Top with crispy greens.
notes: Use any leftover vegetable scraps (peels, ends) to make homemade vegetable broth for the rice.
Adjust fermentation time for desired tanginess. Warmer temperatures accelerate fermentation.
This recipe embraces a zero-waste approach by utilizing fermentation and vegetable off-cuts.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken Thighs with Herbs and Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of roasted chicken thigh, skin golden-brown and slightly crisped, rests on an everyday ceramic plate. It is surrounded by rustic, thick-cut roasted potato wedges, their skins slightly blistered and interiors soft. Bright orange carrot chunks, caramelized and tender, and soft, sweet onion wedges are interspersed among the potatoes. Whole roasted garlic cloves peek through. The natural colors of the vegetables and chicken are vibrant against the simple white plate. The arrangement is casual and natural, as if served directly from the roasting pan to the table. A few fresh rosemary sprigs are scattered for aroma. The scene is set on a well-used wooden dining table with a simple cloth napkin and standard flatware, bathed in warm, inviting kitchen light, evoking a comfortable family meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Wash and scrub potatoes. Cut potatoes into 3 cm thick chunks.
Peel carrots. Cut carrots into 2 cm thick rounds or batons.
Peel onion. Cut onion into thick wedges.
Smash garlic cloves with the side of a knife; leave skins on.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
In a large roasting pan or bowl, combine chicken thighs, potato chunks, carrot rounds, onion wedges, and smashed garlic.
Drizzle with olive oil. Add salt, black pepper, chopped rosemary leaves, and thyme leaves.
Toss all ingredients to coat evenly.
Arrange chicken and vegetables in a single layer in the roasting pan. Ensure chicken skin faces up.
Roast for 40-50 minutes. Chicken is done when its internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Vegetables should be tender and lightly browned.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Spanish Chicken and Potato Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rustic Spanish Chicken and Potato Stew is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, seared chicken thigh sits prominently, surrounded by tender, rustic chunks of potato. Interspersed are vibrant red bell pepper strips, softened onion pieces, and bright red tomato quarters, all coated in a rich, savory, reddish-brown broth. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley adds a final pop of color and freshness. The textures are varied: crispy chicken skin, soft potatoes, and tender vegetables. The dish exudes warmth and comfort. The plate is placed on a simple wooden surface with natural, even lighting. A cotton napkin, a rustic bread roll, and a glass of red wine are subtly placed alongside, enhancing the casual, authentic Spanish bistro feel.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a dry Spanish red wine.

ingredients.name: Smoked paprika (Pimentón de la Vera dulce)

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy. Flip. Sear other side. Remove chicken.
Dice onions into medium pieces. Slice red bell pepper into strips. Mince garlic.
Add onions and bell pepper to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze with white wine. Scrape up browned bits. Reduce slightly.
Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Cut potatoes into 3-4 cm chunks. Quarter tomatoes.
Add potatoes and seared chicken to the pot. Nestle chicken among potatoes.
Add quartered tomatoes.
If using saffron, steep in a tablespoon of hot stock, then add to pot.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover.
Cook 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature and potatoes are tender. Stir occasionally.
Uncover for the last 10 minutes to thicken sauce slightly.
Taste. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Indian Chicken and Potato Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Aloo Murgh is presented in a shallow white porcelain bowl. A mound of fluffy, steamed long-grain basmati rice occupies one side. Beside it, the curry features large 4cm chunks of moist chicken and 3cm cubes of tender potato. The sauce is a rich, deep orange-brown with visible textures of sautéed onions. Two bright green chilies, slit lengthwise, are nestled among the chicken pieces. Freshly chopped green coriander is scattered across the curry for contrast. The bowl rests on a rustic dark wood surface. A small side dish of pickled vegetables and a copper spoon accompany the meal. Natural light emphasizes the glossy sauce and soft textures of the rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of lime wedges
Accompany with mango chutney
Traditional copper serving spoon
Serve with warm garlic naan
instructions: Wash rice until water runs clear. Soak in water for 20 minutes.
Boil 600ml water. Add soaked rice. Simmer 12 minutes until tender. Drain.
Heat oil in a heavy-based pot over medium heat. Add cumin seeds.
Add diced onions. Sauté until deep golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste and slit chilies. Cook for 1 minute.
Cut chicken into 4cm chunks. Add to pot. Sear until browned.
Add turmeric, garam masala, and 3cm potato cubes. Season with salt.
Pour in 200ml water. Cover with a tight lid. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Garnish with chopped coriander. Serve hot with rice.
notes: Ensure onions are well-browned for a deep sauce color
Use waxy potatoes so they do not break apart during the simmer
Soaking the basmati rice ensures long, separate grains

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Supreme, Truffled Pomme Purée, Chanterelles, Jus Lié
recipes.visual_description: A perfectly pan-seared chicken supreme, golden-skinned and moist, rests elegantly as the centerpiece on a pristine white, modern designer plate. Adjacent, a velvety, glossy truffled pomme purée is artfully swiped across the plate, showcasing its smooth texture. Golden-brown sautéed chanterelle mushrooms are carefully arranged beside the chicken, adding earthy contrast. A rich, amber jus lié, precisely spooned, encircles the elements, providing depth and sheen. The composition is minimalist with abundant negative space, highlighting the pristine execution of each component. Colors are sophisticated: golden-brown chicken, creamy white purée, deep amber jus, and earthy chanterelles, subtly garnished with finely minced chives. The scene is set on a premium white Carrara marble surface with a crisp white linen napkin, under dramatic professional lighting, emphasizing luxurious simplicity.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Pat chicken supremes dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in an oven-safe, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken supremes skin-side down. Sear 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crisp. Do not move chicken during searing.
Flip chicken. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast 12-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from oven. Rest chicken on a wire rack for 5 minutes.
For the Pomme Purée: Peel and dice potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Place in a pot, cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook 15-20 minutes until very tender. Drain thoroughly.

Pass hot potatoes through a ricer or fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot. Heat 100ml heavy cream and 50g butter until just simmering. Gradually whisk hot cream mixture into potatoes until smooth and glossy. Stir in truffle paste or oil. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Keep warm.

For the Chanterelles: Clean mushrooms gently with a brush or damp cloth. Heat 20g butter in a pan over medium-high heat. Add chanterelles. Sauté 3-5 minutes until golden and tender. Season with salt and pepper.

For the Jus Lié: In the same pan used for chicken (after removing chicken), drain excess fat. Add finely minced shallot and garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Deglaze with chicken stock, scraping up any browned bits. Add thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half, about 8-10 minutes, until slightly thickened. Strain jus through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Return jus to clean pan. Stir in remaining 100ml heavy cream and 30g butter. Whisk until incorporated and glossy. Season with salt and pepper.

To plate: Spoon a generous dollop of truffled pomme purée onto one side of each plate. Using the back of a spoon, artfully swipe the purée across the plate. Place one chicken supreme elegantly beside the purée. Arrange sautéed chanterelle mushrooms next to the chicken. Spoon a precise pool of jus lié around the chicken and purée. Garnish with finely minced fresh chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Supreme with Silky Pomme Purée and Thyme-Chanterelle Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken supreme, with golden-crisp skin and tender white meat, is the centerpiece on a pristine white bone china plate. It rests elegantly beside a perfectly formed quenelle of silky, ivory-hued pomme purée. Scattered around the chicken and purée are vibrant, golden-orange sautéed chanterelle mushrooms, some whole, some halved, showcasing their delicate ruffles. A rich, glossy, dark brown thyme-infused chicken jus is artfully spooned around the components, creating a flowing, organic composition. A few delicate green micro-herbs, like chervil or micro-thyme, are precisely placed on top of the chicken and purée, adding a subtle color contrast. The entire plate is visible, with abundant negative space. It sits on a premium white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a precisely folded white linen napkin and modern, elegant flatware. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting textures against an ultra-minimalist background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).

For the Pomme Purée: Peel and cut potatoes into uniform large chunks. Place in a pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain thoroughly. Pass potatoes through a ricer or fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot. Heat cream and 100g butter until melted. Gradually whisk hot cream mixture into potatoes until smooth and silky. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

For the Chicken Supreme: Pat chicken supremes dry. Season skin generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear until skin is golden brown and crispy, about 6-8 minutes. Flip chicken. Add 2 sprigs of thyme, 20g butter, and 2 crushed garlic cloves to the pan. Baste chicken with butter. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F), about 10-15 minutes. Rest chicken on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

For the Chanterelles: Clean chanterelle mushrooms. Halve larger mushrooms. Finely dice shallots. Heat remaining 30g butter in a separate pan over medium-high heat. Add chanterelles. Sauté until tender and lightly golden, about 5-7 minutes. Add diced shallots and remaining thyme sprigs. Cook for 2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

For the Thyme-Chanterelle Jus: Deglaze the chicken pan with chicken stock. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce stock by half over medium heat. Strain the jus through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Whisk in a knob of butter for gloss. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

To plate: Place a spoonful of silky pomme purée towards one side of a warm plate. Create a gentle swoosh or quenelle. Carefully place one rested chicken supreme next to the purée. Arrange sautéed chanterelles artfully around the chicken and purée. Spoon a generous amount of Thyme-Chanterelle Jus around the elements. Garnish with micro-herbs.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rustic Roasted Chicken and Potatoes rests on an everyday cream-colored ceramic plate. Two golden-brown roasted chicken drumsticks, with crispy, crackled skin, are positioned naturally beside a generous pile of thick-cut, golden-brown roasted potato wedges. The potatoes show a slightly crispy exterior and tender interior, some edges lightly charred. Scattered among the potatoes and chicken are a few wilted rosemary and thyme sprigs and roasted garlic cloves. The arrangement is casual and unpretentious, reflecting home cooking. The plate is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple cloth napkin and standard flatware nearby. Warm, inviting kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a comfortable family kitchen setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and pat dry chicken pieces. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Wash potatoes. Cut into thick wedges, about 2-3 cm thick.
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges, olive oil, smashed garlic, rosemary, and thyme. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange chicken pieces and potato wedges in a single layer on a large baking tray. Ensure chicken skin faces up.
Roast for 30 minutes. Flip potatoes once during cooking.
Continue roasting for another 20-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden-brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Potato Puree and Quick-Pickled Cabbage Slaw
recipes.visual_description: A single seared chicken thigh, its surface golden-brown with a delicate crust, rests alongside a smooth, creamy mound of potato puree. The chicken retains its natural shape, showcasing its succulence. Adjacent to the chicken, a vibrant pile of quick-pickled cabbage and carrot slaw adds a burst of color and crisp texture. The slaw, a mix of shredded white cabbage, bright orange julienned carrots, and subtle apple pieces, is lightly glossy from the pickling liquid. The plate, a simple handcrafted ceramic in a natural cream tone, provides ample negative space, highlighting each component. A scattering of fresh, finely chopped dill or chives provides a final verdant touch. The presentation emphasizes clean lines and the natural beauty of each ingredient against a light, uncluttered background of a natural wood or stone surface.
instructions: Prepare Quick-Pickled Slaw: Thinly slice cabbage and carrots. Julienne apple. Combine in a bowl.
Make Pickling Brine: In a saucepan, combine vinegar, water, sugar, 10g salt, peppercorns, and bay leaf. Bring to a boil. Stir until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat.
Pickle Vegetables: Pour hot brine over cabbage mixture. Ensure vegetables are submerged. Let cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or longer for more intense flavor.
Prepare Potatoes: Peel potatoes. Cut into 2-3 cm cubes. Place in a pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Cook Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear Chicken: Place chicken thighs in the hot skillet. Sear for 5-7 minutes until golden brown. Flip chicken.
Finish Chicken: Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F). Roast for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
Make Potato Puree: Drain cooked potatoes well. Return to the hot pot over low heat for 1 minute to dry. Add milk and butter. Mash until smooth. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Plate Dish: Place a generous mound of creamy potato puree off-center on each plate. Arrange a seared chicken thigh next to the puree. Drain quick-pickled slaw. Place a small mound of slaw next to the chicken.
Garnish: Sprinkle fresh dill or chives over the slaw and puree. Serve immediately.
notes: To reduce waste, potato peels can be roasted until crispy for a snack or used to flavor vegetable stock.
Leftover chicken trimmings or bones can be simmered with vegetable scraps for a quick broth.

recipes.recipe_name: Goat Cheese Agnolotti with Brown Butter Sage Sauce and Candied Walnuts
recipes.visual_description: A Michelin-starred plate showcases precisely cooked goat cheese agnolotti. Each delicate, plump pasta parcel, approximately 3cm by 2cm, is perfectly al dente with a creamy, pale yellow interior visible on some. They are artfully arranged in a fluid, organic cluster on one side of a pristine, circular bone china plate, leaving abundant negative space. The agnolotti are glistening with a rich, golden-brown butter sauce, infused with the aroma of crisped, dark green sage leaves. A scattering of irregularly broken, golden-brown candied walnut pieces provides textural contrast and a subtle sheen. A few vibrant green microgreens are delicately placed atop the pasta, adding a touch of fresh color. The plate sits on a smooth, grey-veined marble surface, accompanied by a precisely folded white linen napkin and elegant silver flatware. Dramatic, directional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the dish's refined textures and warm tones.
instructions: Pile flour on a clean surface. Make a well in the center.
Crack eggs into the well. Add salt.
Gradually incorporate flour into eggs with a fork.
Knead dough for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Wrap in cling film. Rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Combine goat cheese, ricotta, Parmesan, lemon zest, and nutmeg in a bowl.
Season with salt and pepper. Mix well.
Transfer filling to a piping bag.
Combine sugar and water in a small saucepan. Heat over medium until sugar dissolves.
Add walnuts. Stir constantly until water evaporates and sugar crystallizes, coating walnuts.
Continue cooking, stirring, until sugar melts and coats walnuts golden brown.
Spread walnuts on parchment paper. Cool completely. Break into small pieces.
Divide pasta dough into 2-3 portions.
Roll one portion through a pasta machine, starting from the widest setting.
Gradually reduce settings until dough is thin (setting 6 or 7 on most machines).
Lay pasta sheet on a lightly floured surface.
Pipe small mounds of filling (approximately 5g each) in a line down the center of the sheet, spaced 2 cm apart.
Fold one side of the pasta over the filling. Gently press around each mound to remove air.
Cut agnolotti using a fluted pasta wheel, creating small square or rectangular pillows.
Repeat with remaining dough and filling.
Place formed agnolotti on a semolina-dusted tray.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Carefully add agnolotti. Cook for 2-3 minutes until al dente and floating.
Reserve 100ml pasta cooking water. Drain agnolotti.
Melt butter in a large sauté pan over medium heat.
Add sage leaves. Cook until butter turns golden brown and smells nutty. Sage leaves will crisp.
Season with salt.
Add cooked agnolotti to the pan with brown butter sauce.
Add a splash of reserved pasta water. Gently toss to coat.
Divide agnolotti evenly among 4 warm plates. Arrange them artfully.
Spoon remaining sauce over pasta.
Sprinkle generously with candied walnuts.
Garnish with microgreens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Root Vegetable Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Beef and Root Vegetable Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with natural imperfections. Tender, dark brown beef chunks are nestled among vibrant orange carrot chunks, pale yellow potato chunks, and flecks of green celery. The rich, glossy, dark brown gravy coats all ingredients, creating a cohesive, appetizing appearance. A scattering of bright green chopped fresh parsley provides a fresh contrast on top. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple metal spoon rests beside the bowl on a casually placed beige cloth napkin. The setting evokes a warm, cozy home kitchen with natural, soft lighting and a slightly blurred, unobtrusive background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm, crusty bread for dipping.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 3 medium, peeled and cut into 2 cm chunks

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 4 medium, peeled and cut into 2-3 cm chunks

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry with paper towels. In a large bowl, toss beef with flour, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove seared beef and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrot chunks, and celery slices to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until vegetables soften, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste to the pot. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Pour in beef broth and Worcestershire sauce. Scrape the bottom of the pot to loosen any browned bits.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add potato chunks, dried thyme, and bay leaves. Stir to combine.
Bring the stew to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and cook for 2 to 2.5 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove bay leaves before serving. Skim any excess fat from the surface if desired. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Ladle hot stew into individual serving bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure beef is cooked until very tender, easily pulled apart with a fork.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A comforting, golden-brown Creamy Chicken and Potato Bake is presented in a well-loved, rustic ceramic baking dish, slightly off-center on a warm, worn wooden kitchen table. The dish features tender, cubed chicken breast chunks and soft potato cubes, generously coated in a creamy, savory sauce, with vibrant green peas interspersed throughout. A thick, bubbly layer of golden-brown melted cheddar cheese forms a crisp crust over the top. The sauce peeks through in places, showing its rich, creamy texture. The overall appearance is hearty and inviting, with natural, modest portions. The setting is a homely family kitchen, bathed in warm, soft light from an overhead fixture. A simple, everyday ceramic plate with minor imperfections is placed nearby, ready for serving. A casually folded cloth napkin and basic flatware rest beside the dish. The background is minimal, hinting at a lived-in kitchen atmosphere with a natural, unpretentious feel, emphasizing the dish as the centerpiece of a satisfying home-cooked meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 2 cm cubes. Place in a pot of salted cold water. Bring to a boil. Cook 8-10 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain thoroughly.
Dice chicken breasts into 2-3 cm cubes. Season with salt and black pepper.
Heat an oven-safe baking dish or large skillet over medium heat. Melt butter. Add diced chicken. Sear for 3-4 minutes until lightly browned on all sides. Remove chicken from dish.
Add chopped onion to the same dish. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.
Stir in flour. Cook 1 minute. Gradually whisk in chicken broth until smooth. Remove dish from heat.
Stir mayonnaise into the sauce until well combined. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Add seared chicken, drained potatoes, and frozen peas to the dish. Pour the creamy sauce over. Stir gently to coat all ingredients.
Sprinkle grated cheddar cheese evenly over the top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until bubbly and the cheese topping is golden brown. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Let the bake rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Lemon-Garlic Potatoes and Creamy Cucumber Salad
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple light wooden table. A single pan-seared chicken thigh, boasting a rich golden-brown crust and tender interior, is positioned as the main focal point. Adjacent to the chicken are several golden-brown roasted potato wedges, their edges slightly crisped and interiors fluffy. Beside the potatoes, a generous portion of creamy cucumber salad is neatly mounded. The salad showcases vibrant green diced cucumber and bright red or yellow diced bell pepper, coated in a luscious, pale yellow dressing. A light sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese adorns the chicken and potatoes, adding a subtle texture and color contrast. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting includes a simple set of silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin placed to the side. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the fresh ingredients.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel potatoes. Cut into wedges. Toss with 15ml olive oil, 1 minced garlic clove, half of lemon slices, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes, until golden and tender.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt, pepper, and oregano.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs presentation side down for 6-8 minutes until golden brown and crispy.

Flip chicken. Add remaining 2 minced garlic cloves to the pan. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Cook for 10-15 minutes, until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
For the salad: Dice cucumber, bell pepper, and onion finely. Combine in a medium bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk mayonnaise, sour cream, and juice from half a lemon. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour dressing over vegetables. Gently mix until coated.
To serve: Place roasted potatoes on a white plate. Arrange a chicken thigh next to potatoes. Spoon creamy cucumber salad beside chicken and potatoes. Garnish with grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken & Cheese Bites
recipes.visual_description: Multiple golden-brown Spicy Chicken & Cheese Bites are presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, centrally placed on a light wooden table surface. Each bite is irregularly shaped, approximately 4-5 cm in diameter, showcasing a crispy, textured exterior. The interior, revealed slightly in one or two bites, shows finely diced white chicken, vibrant red specks of minced chili, and pockets of melted, pale yellow cheese. A small cluster of fresh green cilantro leaves garnishes the bites, adding a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is organic, with 4-5 bites artfully clustered, allowing for moderate negative space around them. A folded light grey cotton napkin rests to the left of the plate. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the dish from above, highlighting its inviting textures. The background is subtly blurred, suggesting a casual, contemporary bistro setting.
instructions: Boil chicken breast until cooked through. Shred chicken finely.
Rehydrate dried chilies in hot water for 15 minutes. Drain. Mince finely.
Grate cheddar cheese.
Finely dice onion and mince garlic. Sauté in a pan with a little oil until softened. Cool.
In a large bowl, combine shredded chicken, minced chilies, grated cheese, sautéed onion and garlic, egg, and breadcrumbs.
Season mixture with salt and black pepper. Mix thoroughly.
Form mixture into small, uniform bites, approximately 4-5 cm in diameter.
Heat neutral oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Pan-fry bites for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy.
notes: Serve hot with lime wedges or a simple chili aioli.

recipes.recipe_name: Chickpea 'Meatballs' with Creamy Lemon Dill Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with a slightly uneven rim, placed on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. A single portion of four to five golden-brown chickpea 'meatballs' are casually arranged in the center, some touching. Each 'meatball' is spherical, roughly 3-4 cm in diameter, with a slightly textured, crisp exterior. A generous pool of creamy, pale yellow lemon dill sauce flows around and over the 'meatballs,' its surface subtly speckled with finely chopped green dill. Alongside, a small mound of vibrant, diced red and yellow bell peppers and crisp, diced cucumber adds a pop of color and fresh texture. The vegetables are lightly sautéed, retaining their shape. A simple, folded cloth napkin in a neutral tone rests casually beside the plate. The scene is lit by warm, inviting kitchen light, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere. The plate is not overcrowded, allowing for negative space, and the overall presentation is natural and unpretentious.
instructions: Toast bread until crisp. Blend into breadcrumbs.
Mash chickpeas in a bowl. Leave some texture.
Add half of diced onion, half of minced garlic, breadcrumbs, egg, half of chopped dill, lemon zest, 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper to mashed chickpeas.
Mix well. Form into 8-10 'meatballs' (approx. 3-4 cm diameter).
Heat a large frying pan over medium heat with 15ml olive oil.
Cook 'meatballs' for 8-10 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and firm. Set aside.
In the same pan, add butter. Sauté remaining diced onion and minced garlic for 2-3 minutes until softened.
Stir in cashew milk and lemon juice. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring, until sauce slightly thickens.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining chopped dill. Season with salt and pepper.
While sauce simmers, quickly sauté diced bell pepper and cucumber in a separate small pan with a drizzle of olive oil for 2-3 minutes until slightly tender-crisp. Season lightly.
Divide 'meatballs' between two plates.
Spoon creamy lemon dill sauce generously over 'meatballs'.
Serve with sautéed bell pepper and cucumber on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Carota e Mozzarella Polpette al Forno
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of baked carrot and mozzarella patties is presented on a rustic, off-white ceramic dinner plate, set on a well-used wooden dining table. Three golden-brown, round patties, approximately 7 cm in diameter, are casually arranged on a vibrant red bed of simple tomato sauce, allowing the sauce to pool naturally around them. Each patty features melted, slightly bubbling mozzarella on top, with some cheese oozing down the sides. The patties show a textured, slightly crispy exterior from baking, revealing hints of grated orange carrot within. A scattering of fresh, finely chopped green parsley adds a pop of color. The plate fills the frame adequately, leaving some negative space. A simple silver fork and knife are placed beside the plate on a casually draped, light-colored linen napkin. Warm, soft lighting from above casts gentle shadows, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar
instructions: Grate carrots. Finely dice onion and mince garlic. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan.
Sauté onion and garlic until softened, about 3 minutes. Add grated carrots. Cook until tender, about 8-10 minutes. Let cool.
In a bowl, combine cooled carrots, 100 g breadcrumbs, egg, grated Parmesan, salt, and black pepper. Mix well.
Dice 150 g mozzarella into small cubes. Form carrot mixture into 12 small patties, about 7 cm wide. Press a few mozzarella cubes into the center of each patty.
In a separate saucepan, combine crushed tomatoes, remaining 15 ml olive oil, dried oregano, salt, and pepper. Simmer sauce for 15 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Arrange patties on a baking tray lined with parchment paper.
Bake for 20 minutes, until golden. Remove from oven. Top each patty with remaining 50 g shredded mozzarella.
Return to oven. Bake until cheese is melted and bubbly, about 5-7 minutes.
Serve patties hot over the tomato sauce, garnished with fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure patties are golden brown and firm to the touch when cooked through.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Apples and Rosemary
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, comforting roasted chicken dish is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate with an off-white glaze. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned roasted chicken thigh rests centrally. Around it, tender, caramelized chunks of roasted potato and soft, browned apple wedges are naturally arranged, some slightly overlapping. Charred onion pieces and fresh rosemary flecks are scattered among the components, adding color. The chicken shows rendered fat and an irregular shape from roasting. Potatoes have a golden crust and fluffy interior. Apples are softened and caramelized at edges, retaining shape. The overall impression is warmth with natural textures and earthy tones. The dish sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, with a simple fork, knife, and casual cloth napkin. Warm, inviting kitchen light illuminates the scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the roasting pan or on individual plates.

ingredients.name: Apples (firm, tart variety like Honeycrisp or Granny Smith)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Pat chicken pieces dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Core apples and cut into 2 cm thick wedges. Cut potatoes into 3 cm chunks. Cut onion into 2 cm wedges.
In a large roasting pan or baking dish, combine potato chunks, onion wedges, and apple wedges.
Strip rosemary leaves from sprigs and roughly chop. Mince garlic.
Add olive oil, chopped rosemary, and minced garlic to the vegetables and apples. Toss to coat evenly.
Nestle chicken pieces among the vegetables and apples in the roasting pan.
Pour chicken broth into the bottom of the pan, if using.
Roast for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are tender and browned.
Baste chicken and vegetables occasionally during roasting.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Garlic Herb Pan Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, whole and golden-brown with a savory crust, rests centrally on a modest white ceramic plate. The chicken is glistening with the rich garlic herb pan sauce spooned generously over it. Freshly chopped green parsley and thyme leaves are scattered over the chicken and around the plate, adding vibrant color and natural texture. The glossy sauce pools slightly at the base of the chicken. The plate sits on a well-worn, natural wooden kitchen table. A simple, everyday fork and knife are placed casually beside the plate. The scene is bathed in warm, natural kitchen light, evoking a cozy, homely atmosphere. The background is softly blurred, showing hints of a lived-in kitchen setting.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Place chicken breasts in the hot skillet. Sear for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and a crust forms. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary.

Flip chicken. Reduce heat to medium. Cook for another 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Use a meat thermometer to check. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside on a plate; tent with foil.
Reduce heat to low. Add minced garlic to the skillet. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in butter, chopped parsley, and thyme. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Spoon sauce over the chicken. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Marsala with Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: Golden pan-seared chicken breast, whole or in two thick pieces, positioned on a pristine white round plate. Earthy brown sautéed cremini mushroom slices are artfully scattered around. A rich, glossy Marsala wine sauce, deep amber, pools around the chicken, lightly coating it. Vibrant green fresh chopped Italian parsley garnishes the dish. Presented on a light wooden table with a crisp white linen napkin and silver flatware. A subtle glass of red wine in the background. Natural, even lighting highlights textures: crisp chicken surface, tender mushrooms, smooth shimmering sauce. Balanced composition with negative space, focusing on the refined single serving.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of simple buttered pasta or creamy polenta.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a dry red wine, such as a Chianti or Merlot.

ingredients.name: Unsalted butter, cold, cut into cubes

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Pound each breast to an even 1.5 cm thickness. Season with salt and pepper.
Dredge chicken breasts lightly in flour, shaking off excess.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add sliced cremini mushrooms to the same skillet. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened and browned. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with Marsala wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Simmer 2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Reduce heat to low. Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Allow chicken to warm through in the sauce.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in cold butter until melted and incorporated (mantecare).
Stir in fresh chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve immediately.
notes: Use a good quality dry Marsala wine for best flavor, not cooking Marsala.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Root Vegetables and Herb Stem Pesto
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken thigh, with crisp, golden-brown skin, rests prominently on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy tone. Beside it, a vibrant scattering of lacto-fermented root vegetable batons – orange carrots, pale parsnips, and white daikon radish – adds pops of natural color and varied textures. A rich, emerald-green dollop of herb stem pesto garnishes the plate, hinting at fresh, bright flavors. The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample white space around the ingredients, emphasizing their natural beauty and simple presentation. The setting features a light, reclaimed wood surface, an undyed linen napkin, and soft, natural light from the side, creating an eco-conscious, inviting atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Mixed root vegetables (carrots, parsnips, daikon radish)

instructions: Clean a 1-liter glass jar. Pack root vegetable batons tightly into the jar. Dissolve sea salt in filtered water to create brine. Pour brine over vegetables, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight or small plate to keep vegetables under brine. Seal jar loosely or use an airlock. Ferment at room temperature (18-24°C) for 5-7 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Burp jar daily if not using an airlock. Refrigerate after fermentation.
Pat chicken thighs very dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden brown and crispy.

Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F). Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) at the thickest part. Rest chicken 5 minutes before serving.

Combine herb stems, walnuts/sunflower seeds, garlic, olive oil, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt in a food processor. Process until smooth, scraping down sides as needed. Adjust seasoning if necessary.
Arrange rested chicken thighs on plates. Serve alongside a generous portion of fermented root vegetables. Spoon or drizzle herb stem pesto over chicken and vegetables.

recipes.recipe_name: Apple and Onion Pork Chops
recipes.visual_description: A single, hearty portion of Apple and Onion Pork Chops rests on a simple, round ceramic plate, centrally placed on a well-used wooden dining table. A thick, seared pork chop, displaying a rich golden-brown crust, is nestled amidst a generous spoonful of braised apple wedges and translucent, softened onion half-moons. The apples, slightly collapsed but still chunky, show their natural light yellow and reddish hues. The onions are a soft, caramelized amber. A glossy, reduced pan sauce coats the ingredients, catching the warm, cozy light from overhead kitchen fixtures. A few fresh thyme sprigs are casually placed over the dish as a functional garnish. A plain cloth napkin and simple metal fork and knife rest beside the plate. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a comforting, homely presentation with natural portions.
instructions: Pat pork chops dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Slice apples into 1 cm thick wedges. Slice onion into 0.5 cm thick half-moons.
Heat olive oil and 15 g butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear pork chops for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chops from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 g butter to the skillet. Reduce heat to medium.
Add sliced onion to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in apple wedges and thyme sprigs. Cook for 2-3 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth and apple cider vinegar. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared pork chops to the skillet. Nestle them into the apple and onion mixture.
Cover the skillet. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until pork reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove pork chops from skillet. Tent with foil to rest for 5 minutes.
Increase heat to medium-high. Simmer sauce, apples, and onions uncovered for 5-7 minutes. Reduce liquid until slightly thickened.
Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste. Discard thyme sprigs.
Serve pork chops immediately with the braised apples and onions.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Apples and Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single bone-in pork chop, golden-brown and pan-seared, rests on an everyday off-white ceramic plate. Adjacent to the chop are tender, lightly caramelized apple wedges and soft, translucent onion slices, some slightly overlapping the pork. A modest drizzle of the rich pan sauce lightly coats the pork and surrounding ingredients. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley. The plate is placed on a well-used, rustic wooden dining table. A simple metal fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate. A plain, folded linen napkin sits nearby. The scene is illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting, creating a relaxed, lived-in family dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with mashed potatoes or creamy polenta.
Accompany with steamed green beans or roasted root vegetables.

ingredients.name: Large firm apple (e.g., Honeycrisp, Fuji), cored and cut into 8 wedges

instructions: Pat pork chops dry. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Sear pork chops for 4-5 minutes per side until deeply golden brown. Reduce heat if browning too quickly.
Transfer chops to a plate. Set aside.
Add butter to the same skillet. Reduce heat to medium.
Add onion slices and apple wedges to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until softened and lightly caramelized.
Stir in fresh thyme sprigs. Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Return pork chops to the skillet with the apple and onion mixture. Ensure chops are nestled in the sauce.
Cover skillet and cook for 5-7 minutes, or until pork reaches an internal temperature of 63°C (145°F).
Remove from heat. Let chops rest in the skillet for 5 minutes.
Remove thyme sprigs. Taste pan sauce and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve pork chops with apples and onions, drizzled with pan sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best results, use thick-cut pork chops to prevent drying out.
Adjust cooking time based on the thickness of your pork chops and desired doneness.

recipes.recipe_name: Mini Banana Financiers with Dark Chocolate Glaze
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine uniformly baked mini banana financiers are presented on a pristine white French porcelain rectangular serving platter. Each financier features a golden-brown exterior with crisp edges and a moist, tender crumb. A smooth, glossy dark chocolate glaze elegantly tops each petit four, slightly pooling at the base. A delicate, very thin slice of fresh banana or a light dusting of cocoa powder garnishes each. The arrangement is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space, highlighting the rich colors of the baked pastry and dark chocolate. The scene is set on a simple light wooden surface, illuminated by natural, even light, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as part of a mignardise selection.
Offer with coffee or tea after a meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Lightly grease financier molds.

Brown butter: Melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Cook until butter solids turn golden brown and butter smells nutty. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve into a heatproof bowl. Let cool slightly.
Combine dry ingredients: In a medium bowl, whisk together powdered sugar, almond flour, all-purpose flour, and salt.
Add wet ingredients: Add egg whites and mashed banana to the dry ingredients. Mix with a whisk until just combined.
Incorporate butter: Gradually whisk the slightly cooled brown butter into the batter until smooth. Do not overmix.
Fill molds: Pour the batter into the prepared financier molds, filling each about two-thirds full.
Bake financiers: Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until the edges are golden brown and the centers are set. A toothpick inserted into the center should come out clean.
Cool: Carefully remove financiers from molds immediately. Place them on a wire rack to cool completely.

Prepare glaze: Finely chop the dark chocolate. Place it in a heatproof bowl. Heat the heavy cream in a small saucepan until it simmers. Pour the hot cream over the chopped chocolate. Let stand for 1 minute, then whisk until smooth and glossy.
Glaze financiers: Once financiers are completely cool, dip the top of each into the warm chocolate glaze. Allow excess glaze to drip off.
Set: Place glazed financiers back on the wire rack for the glaze to set. This can be expedited by refrigerating for a few minutes.
notes: Ensure the butter is properly browned for a rich, nutty flavor (beurre noisette).
Do not overmix the batter to maintain a tender crumb.
Financier molds are typically rectangular or oval, but can be adapted to other small molds.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Cottage Cheese Bites
recipes.visual_description: Homely family kitchen setting. Natural warm light from kitchen window. A well-used wooden dining table. Everyday ceramic platter, possibly with slight imperfections. Six to nine uniform miniature "Sweet Cottage Cheese Bites" are arranged organically on the platter. Each bite is baked in a mini muffin liner, forming a small, round tartlet. They have a visible light golden-brown graham cracker crust base. The filling is creamy, off-white, with a smooth, slightly domed top, indicating a soft, set texture. Some bites are lightly dusted with white powdered sugar. A few have a single small, vibrant red berry placed centrally on top. The arrangement is casual, inviting, and slightly asymmetrical, as if just placed for family. A casually folded plain linen napkin rests nearby. The overall impression is comforting, homemade, and unpretentious.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a 12-cup mini muffin tin with paper liners.
Crush graham crackers finely. Melt butter. Mix crushed crackers and melted butter.
Press about 15g of cracker mixture into bottom of each muffin liner. Bake 5 minutes. Remove from oven.
In a blender or food processor, combine cottage cheese, granulated sugar, egg, heavy cream, vanilla extract, and salt. Blend until completely smooth.
Pour cottage cheese mixture evenly over pre-baked crusts. Fill each liner about two-thirds full.
Bake 18-22 minutes, or until edges are set and centers are slightly jiggly.
Turn off oven. Leave bites in oven with door ajar for 15 minutes. This helps prevent cracking.
Remove from oven. Let cool completely in tin on a wire rack.
Chill in refrigerator for at least 2 hours before serving. This is crucial for proper setting.
Dust with powdered sugar and top with a small berry, if desired.
notes: For best results, ensure cottage cheese is blended completely smooth for a creamy texture.
Chilling is crucial for proper setting and enhanced flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Gourmet Bratwurst Tartine
recipes.visual_description: A single Gourmet Bratwurst Tartine rests centrally on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A thick, golden-crusted slice of rustic sourdough bread forms the base. It is topped with a substantial mound of tender, pale green braised sauerkraut, flecked with darker caraway seeds. Arranged artfully atop the sauerkraut are several thick, perfectly seared bratwurst medallions, their skins browned and glistening. A generous dollop of rich, deep amber caramelized onions cascades over the bratwurst. A golden-brown, bubbling layer of melted Gruyère cheese covers the toppings, creating inviting texture. A sprinkle of bright green chopped parsley adds a fresh contrast. The plate features moderate negative space, highlighting the dish's robust presentation. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple wooden table, a folded cotton napkin, and standard European flatware.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crisp German lager
Offer a side of gherkin pickles
Enjoy with a simple green salad dressed with a vinaigrette

ingredients.name: Rustic bread slices (e.g., sourdough or rye)

instructions: Slice yellow onion thinly. Melt butter in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add sliced yellow onions. Cook slowly for 30-40 minutes until deep golden brown and sweet. Season with salt. Set aside.

Finely dice red onion. In a pot, heat a small amount of vegetable oil over medium heat. Sauté diced red onion until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add drained sauerkraut, caraway seeds, and broth. Grate in apple if using. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook for 20-25 minutes until tender and flavors meld. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Heat remaining vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add bratwurst sausages. Sear until browned on all sides, about 8-10 minutes. Reduce heat to medium-low. Add 50ml water, cover the skillet, and steam for 5-7 minutes until bratwursts are cooked through (internal temperature 70°C). Remove from pan. Let rest briefly. Slice each bratwurst into 2cm thick medallions.
Lightly toast bread slices. Spread a thin layer of Dijon mustard evenly on each toasted bread slice.

Assemble tartines: Place a generous layer of braised sauerkraut on each mustard-coated bread slice. Arrange the sliced bratwurst medallions on top of the sauerkraut. Spoon caramelized onions over the bratwurst.

Sprinkle grated Gruyère cheese generously over each tartine. Place tartines under a preheated hot grill (broiler) for 2-4 minutes, or until the cheese is bubbly and golden brown. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
Carefully transfer the Gourmet Bratwurst Tartines to individual plates. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: For best flavor, caramelize onions slowly until very deep brown. This process cannot be rushed.
Adjust sauerkraut acidity with a pinch of sugar or a splash of apple cider vinegar if desired, depending on its tartness.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Paprika Chicken with Roasted Potatoes and Chili-Lime Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Smoked Paprika Chicken with Roasted Potatoes and Chili-Lime Broccoli is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh is positioned as the focal point. Alongside, roasted potato chunks, with their slightly browned, rustic edges, are casually arranged. Bright green broccoli florets, tender-crisp and lightly charred, are scattered amongst the potatoes, with visible flecks of red chili and a subtle sheen from the lime and olive oil. A rich, savory pan sauce pools slightly at the base of the chicken and potatoes. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The dish is set on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and vibrant colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with a vinaigrette.
Offer crusty bread to sop up the pan juices.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or Desiree), medium

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Cut potatoes into 2.5 cm chunks. Toss with 30ml olive oil, half the smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast potatoes for 20 minutes.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Rub with remaining smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.
After 20 minutes, add chicken thighs to the baking tray with the potatoes. Roast for another 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and skin is crispy.
While chicken roasts, prepare broccoli. In a bowl, toss broccoli florets with 15ml olive oil. Finely slice red chili.
When chicken is nearly done, add broccoli to the tray. Squeeze lime juice over broccoli and sprinkle with sliced chili. Toss lightly.
Roast broccoli for 8-10 minutes, until tender-crisp.
Remove tray from oven. Carefully pour chicken stock onto the tray, scraping up any browned bits.
Arrange chicken, potatoes, and broccoli on plates. Spoon pan juices over. Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato Gnocchi with Mushroom and Cherry Tomato Ragù
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Potato Gnocchi with Mushroom and Cherry Tomato Ragù is presented in a clean, white porcelain pasta bowl. The gnocchi are plump and golden, lightly coated in a rustic, vibrant ragù. Sliced cremini mushrooms are tender and earthy brown. Halved cherry tomatoes burst with rich red and orange hues. Diced shallots and minced garlic are integrated seamlessly into the sauce. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered generously on top, providing a pop of color and freshness. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese adds a delicate white finish. The dish is arranged naturally, allowing ingredients to show their textures. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface, beside a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, unfocused bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty ciabatta bread to sop up the delicious ragù.
Pair with a medium-bodied Italian red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
Finish the meal with a strong espresso.
instructions: Boil unpeeled potatoes in salted water until very tender, about 25-30 minutes. Drain well. Peel hot potatoes. Pass them through a potato ricer or mash thoroughly until smooth. Spread mashed potatoes on a clean surface to cool slightly.

Form a well in the center of the potatoes. Add egg and 200g flour. Gently mix with a fork, then knead lightly until dough forms. Do not overmix. Dough should be soft. If sticky, add a little more flour, 15g at a time.

Divide dough into 4 portions. Roll each portion into a 2 cm thick rope. Cut ropes into 2 cm pieces. Roll each gnocchi piece over a fork or gnocchi board to create ridges. Place gnocchi on a lightly floured baking sheet. Repeat with remaining dough.
Slice mushrooms. Dice shallot. Mince garlic. Halve cherry tomatoes.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced shallot. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Sauté until golden brown and tender, about 8-10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Let wine reduce by half. Add halved cherry tomatoes and vegetable broth. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, until tomatoes soften and sauce thickens slightly.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add gnocchi in batches. Cook until they float to the surface, about 2-3 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon.
Add cooked gnocchi directly to the mushroom and tomato ragù. Toss gently to coat. Cook for 1-2 minutes to allow gnocchi to absorb some sauce.
Remove from heat. Stir in half of the grated Parmesan cheese. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh basil leaves and remaining grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Do not overwork the gnocchi dough; it will make them tough. Knead just enough to combine ingredients.
Ensure potatoes are very dry after cooking for best gnocchi texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Tuscan Chicken Pasta is artfully plated on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy fettuccine, intertwined with golden-brown chicken chunks and vibrant green spinach, forms a neat mound in the center. Interspersed are deep red sun-dried tomato slices and earthy brown mushroom slices. The chicken chunks are irregularly shaped, about 2 cm, displaying a seared crust. A light drizzle of the creamy sauce coats the pasta, showing its rich texture. A sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and finely chopped fresh basil leaves garnish the top, adding contrasting color and freshness. The arrangement is organic, allowing ingredients to show naturally. The plate is positioned on a simple light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and classic silver fork and spoon are placed beside the plate, with a small Italian-style bread roll. Natural, soft lighting highlights the textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine, like a Chianti Classico.

ingredients.name: Sun-dried tomatoes, oil-packed, drained and sliced

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Let rest. Cut into 2 cm chunks.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and browned.
Stir in sun-dried tomatoes and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Add heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir until cheese is melted and sauce slightly thickens.
While sauce simmers, cook fettuccine according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Drain, reserving 120 ml pasta water.
Add fresh spinach to the sauce. Cook until wilted, about 1-2 minutes.
Add cooked pasta and chicken chunks to the sauce. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water as needed.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
notes: For extra richness, add a knob of butter at the end.
Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Spaghetti Carbonara
