Preheat oven to 180°C. Lightly flour a surface. Roll dough to 3mm thickness. Cut out four circles larger than tartlet molds. Press dough into four 10cm tartlet molds. Trim edges. Prick bottoms with a fork. Line with parchment paper. Fill with baking beans or rice. Bake blind for 15 minutes. Remove parchment and beans. Bake an additional 5-7 minutes until edges are firm. Cool completely on a wire rack.

Place chopped chocolate in a heatproof bowl. Heat milk and butter in a small saucepan until butter melts and milk is hot, but not boiling. Pour hot milk mixture over chocolate. Let sit for 1 minute. Whisk until smooth and glossy.
Pour ganache into cooled tart shells. Fill about two-thirds full. Chill in refrigerator for at least 30 minutes, or until set.

Whisk egg yolks, sugar, and cornstarch in a bowl until pale. Heat milk in a saucepan until simmering. Gradually whisk hot milk into egg mixture. Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until thick and bubbling (about 1-2 minutes). Remove from heat. Stir in butter and rose water. Pour into a shallow dish. Cover surface with plastic wrap to prevent a skin. Chill completely.
Once pastry cream is cold, whisk it briefly to smooth. In a separate bowl, whip cold heavy cream to soft peaks. Gently fold whipped cream into pastry cream until combined and light.
Spoon or pipe rose cream onto the set chocolate ganache in each tartlet. Arrange strawberry halves or quarters on top of the rose cream. Lightly dust with cocoa powder just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Ragoût with Creamy Potato Puree
recipes.visual_description: A small, elegant starter portion is presented on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table. A perfectly smooth, creamy mound of pale yellow potato puree forms the base. Nestled slightly off-center atop the puree is a rich, dark brown braised beef ragoût. The ragoût features tender, succulent beef chunks (approx. 2-3 cm cubes), glistening quartered mushrooms, and finely diced caramelized onions, all coated in a thick, savory, glossy sauce. A vibrant green sprig of fresh thyme or finely chopped parsley garnishes the ragoût, providing a fresh color contrast. The arrangement is clean and professional, with moderate negative space. The setting includes standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin beside the plate, illuminated by natural, even lighting that highlights the dish's textures and colors, creating an inviting bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a starter course before a main meal.
Pair with a glass of dry red wine.
instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and quartered mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are tender and liquid evaporates, about 7-8 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Deglaze the pot with red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer until wine is reduced by half.
Return beef to the pot. Add beef broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until beef is very tender.
While beef simmers, prepare potato puree. Peel and cut potatoes into equal-sized chunks.
Place potatoes in a saucepan. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes thoroughly. Return to the hot saucepan to dry for 1 minute.
Mash potatoes until smooth. Add butter and warm cream/milk. Season with salt and pepper. Whisk until creamy and lump-free.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf from the beef ragoût. Taste and adjust seasoning.
To serve, place a mound of creamy potato puree on each plate. Spoon a generous portion of beef ragoût over the puree.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: The ragoût can be made a day in advance and reheated gently. Flavors often deepen overnight.
For best results, use good quality beef broth and red wine.

recipes.recipe_name: Chocolate Strawberry Rose Tartlets
recipes.visual_description: A single Chocolate Strawberry Rose Tartlet sits on a simple, slightly worn wooden kitchen table. The tartlet, roughly 10 cm in diameter, has a rustic, dark cocoa crust with slightly uneven edges, indicating a homemade touch. Inside, a smooth, rich chocolate ganache forms the base layer, topped by a pale pink, creamy rose pastry cream that fills the shell generously. Fresh, vibrant red strawberry halves are arranged casually on the cream, some slightly overlapping, showcasing their natural shape. A faint dusting of cocoa powder lightly coats a few strawberries and the edge of the cream. The lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a cozy kitchen atmosphere. The tartlet is placed on an everyday white ceramic plate, possibly with minor imperfections, alongside a simple fork. The background is softly blurred, showing hints of a lived-in kitchen with natural light.

ingredients.name: fresh strawberries, hulled and halved or quartered

instructions: Combine flour, cocoa powder, powdered sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Add cold butter. Rub with fingertips until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add egg yolk. Mix until dough just comes together. Add milk if too dry.
Form into a disc. Wrap in plastic. Chill 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180°C.
Roll dough on lightly floured surface to 3 mm thick.
Cut out 4 circles using tartlet molds as guide.
Press dough into 4 individual 10 cm tartlet molds. Trim edges.
Prick bottoms with a fork. Line with parchment paper. Fill with pie weights or dried beans.
Bake 15 minutes. Remove weights and parchment. Bake 5-7 more minutes until firm.
Cool completely on a wire rack.
Place chopped chocolate in a heatproof bowl.
Heat milk in a small saucepan until simmering. Do not boil.
Pour hot milk over chocolate. Let sit 2 minutes.
Stir gently until smooth and glossy.
Stir in butter until melted and combined.
Let cool slightly at room temperature until it thickens to a spreadable consistency.
Whisk egg yolks, sugar, and cornstarch in a bowl until pale.
Heat milk in a saucepan over medium heat until simmering.
Gradually whisk hot milk into egg yolk mixture.
Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until thick and bubbling (about 1-2 minutes).
Remove from heat. Stir in butter and rose water.
Pour into a clean bowl. Cover surface with plastic wrap to prevent a skin.
Chill completely in the refrigerator (at least 2 hours).
Spoon or pipe chocolate ganache into cooled tart shells, filling about half way.
Spoon or pipe rose pastry cream over ganache, filling to the top.
Arrange fresh strawberry halves or quarters on top of the rose cream.
Dust lightly with cocoa powder, if desired.
Serve immediately or chill until serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Chocolate Rose and Strawberry Layer Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of chocolate rose and strawberry layer cake is centered on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The cake slice reveals distinct layers: dark chocolate sponge, a pale pink, fluffy rose buttercream, and bright red, thinly sliced fresh strawberries. The top of the cake slice is generously frosted with the same pink buttercream and adorned with a few vibrant red, halved fresh strawberries. Textures contrast moist cake, creamy frosting, and juicy fruit. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, with a casually placed off-white cloth napkin nearby. Natural, warm light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy family kitchen setting. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space around the slice.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour two 15cm round cake pans.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, cocoa powder, caster sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
Add egg, milk, vegetable oil, and vanilla extract to dry ingredients. Beat until smooth.
Stir in boiling water until batter is thin and combined.
Divide batter evenly between prepared pans.
Bake 25-30 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool cakes in pans for 10 minutes. Invert onto wire racks to cool completely.
For the buttercream: Beat softened butter in a bowl until creamy.
Gradually add icing sugar, beating until combined. Add 30ml milk and rosewater.
Beat until light and fluffy. Add pink food coloring if desired.
For strawberries: Wash and hull strawberries. Slice half of them thinly for filling. Halve or quarter the remaining for decoration.
Assemble cake: Place one cooled cake layer on a serving plate. Spread a thin layer of rose buttercream.
Arrange thinly sliced strawberries evenly over the buttercream layer.
Top with the second cake layer. Frost the top and sides of the entire cake with remaining buttercream.
Arrange fresh strawberry halves and quarters decoratively on top of the cake.
notes: Adjust rosewater to your preference for a stronger or lighter floral note.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Amaranth & Cheese Curd Loaf
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, golden-brown Savory Amaranth & Cheese Curd Loaf slice rests centrally on a rustic ceramic plate, showcasing its comforting, home-cooked appeal. The loaf is baked firm, with a lightly browned exterior. Small, vibrant red currants are visible within the slice, offering bursts of color against the creamy cheese curd and subtle amaranth. Diced onion and flecks of green parsley are integrated, providing texture. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple, rumpled cloth napkin placed casually. Warm, natural kitchen lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its wholesome character. Everyday stainless steel fork and knife are ready for use. The background suggests a lived-in family kitchen, with a hint of natural clutter.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Heat a non-stick pan. Add diced onion and a splash of vegetable broth. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute more. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, combine cheese curd, eggs, amaranth flour, sautéed onion and garlic, chopped parsley, salt, and pepper.
Gently fold in the red currants. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Press the mixture into a 20x10 cm loaf pan. Do not grease the pan. Line with parchment paper if necessary to prevent sticking.
Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until golden brown and firm to the touch. A toothpick inserted into the center should come out clean.
Let the loaf cool in the pan for 10 minutes before carefully inverting it onto a serving plate.
Slice into 2 cm thick portions. Serve warm.
notes: This recipe is designed without any added sugar, butter, or oil, relying on the natural moisture and fats of the ingredients, and non-stick cooking methods.
Ensure your loaf pan is truly non-stick or line it with parchment paper to prevent sticking without oil.

recipes.recipe_name: Tart Red Currant and Cheese Curd Amaranth Loaf Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generously thick slice of the Tart Red Currant and Cheese Curd Amaranth Loaf Cake rests on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The slice, cleanly cut, reveals a dense, moist crumb with visible vibrant red currants, some slightly burst. The cake's natural, light golden-brown hue from the amaranth flour is evident. In the background, the remaining loaf cake sits on a rustic wooden cutting board, showcasing its unadorned, simple home-baked appearance. The setting is a cozy, lived-in kitchen table made of light-colored, well-used wood. A casually folded, plain linen napkin is placed beside the plate. Lighting is soft, warm, and natural, from a nearby window, casting gentle shadows. The overall impression is comforting, unpretentious home baking, inviting and naturally appealing.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a 20 cm x 10 cm loaf pan with baking paper.
Whisk amaranth flour, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl. Set aside.
In a separate bowl, whisk eggs until light. Add oil and vanilla extract. Whisk until combined.
Add cheese curd to the wet ingredients. Mix well to break up curd.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Gently fold in red currants.
Pour batter into the prepared loaf pan. Smooth the top.
Bake for 45-55 minutes. A wooden skewer inserted into the center should come out clean.
Cool cake in the pan for 10 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
notes: This cake is intentionally made without added sugar or butter. Its sweetness comes solely from the natural sugars in the red currants, resulting in a distinctly tart flavor profile.
The cheese curd provides moisture and a subtle tang, complementing the currants.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Black Bean and Seaweed Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single, homely portion of Savory Black Bean and Seaweed Rice Bowl is presented in a simple, deep ceramic bowl. Fluffy white jasmine rice forms the base, topped generously with the vibrant stir-fry. Dark, glossy black beans are mixed with bright green broccoli florets, orange diced carrots, red diced bell peppers, and sliced brown mushrooms. Rehydrated dark green seaweed pieces are interspersed, adding texture. All ingredients are coated in a rich, savory, glossy brown sauce. A sprinkle of thinly sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds garnishes the top. The components touch and overlap naturally, creating an inviting, unarranged look. The bowl rests on a well-used wooden dining table with a casual cloth napkin. Warm, soft lighting mimics natural kitchen light. Dark wooden chopsticks rest across the bowl's rim, completing the authentic, homely Asian scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chopsticks.
Offer a small side dish of pickled daikon or kimchi for an authentic Asian accompaniment.

ingredients.name: Dried black beans
ingredients.quantity: 200 g (or 2 x 400g cans cooked black beans)

instructions: If using dried black beans, soak overnight. Cook until tender, then drain. If using canned, drain and rinse well.
Rehydrate wakame seaweed in warm water for 10 minutes. Drain, squeeze out excess water. Chop into small pieces.
Cook jasmine rice according to package directions. Keep warm.
Prepare vegetables: Dice carrot and red bell pepper into 1 cm cubes. Cut broccoli into small florets. Slice mushrooms. Dice onion into small pieces. Mince garlic and grate ginger.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, and maple syrup. In a separate small bowl, mix cornstarch with 60 ml water to create a slurry.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add diced onion, minced garlic, and grated ginger. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced carrot and broccoli florets to the wok. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until slightly tender-crisp.
Add diced red bell pepper and sliced mushrooms. Continue to stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Add drained black beans and chopped rehydrated seaweed to the wok. Stir well.
Pour the prepared sauce over the ingredients. Stir to coat everything evenly.
Stir the cornstarch slurry again, then pour into the wok. Stir continuously for 1-2 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the vegetables and beans.
Remove from heat. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

To serve, scoop a portion of cooked jasmine rice into individual ceramic bowls. Spoon a generous amount of the black bean and seaweed stir-fry over the rice. Garnish with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds.
Serve immediately. Enjoy as a hearty, comforting main course.
notes: Adjust the amount of maple syrup or brown sugar to your sweetness preference.
For extra spice, add a teaspoon of gochujang or chili garlic sauce to the sauce mixture.

recipes.recipe_name: Korean Black Bean Chicken with Seaweed Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Korean Black Bean Chicken with Seaweed Rice is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate with a slightly rustic edge, centered on a well-worn wooden dining table. Diced chicken pieces and cubed vegetables (potato, zucchini, onion) are coated in a rich, glossy dark brown black bean sauce, piled naturally on one side of the plate. Adjacent to it, a mound of fluffy white rice is topped with thinly shredded roasted seaweed (gim). The chicken and vegetables show natural variations in color and texture, with the sauce providing a deep, inviting sheen. A light sprinkle of vibrant green sliced spring onions garnishes the top of the chicken. The arrangement is casual and comforting, allowing components to naturally touch. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests beside the plate, and a small, white ceramic bowl of bright red kimchi sits slightly behind, adding a pop of complementary color and cultural context. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of kimchi.
Serve with danmuji (pickled yellow radish).
instructions: Dice chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or wok over medium-high heat.
Add black bean paste. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Remove paste from pot and set aside.
Add diced chicken to the pot. Cook until browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Add diced onion, cubed potato, and cubed zucchini to the pot. Stir-fry for 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return cooked black bean paste to the pot. Stir to coat vegetables and chicken.
In a small bowl, whisk cornstarch with 50 ml water or stock to create a slurry.
Pour remaining 350 ml water or stock into the pot. Add soy sauce and sugar. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in cornstarch slurry. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in sesame oil. Remove from heat.
Serve chicken and sauce over hot white rice. Top with shredded roasted seaweed and sliced green onions.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Braised Beef with Creamy Polenta
recipes.visual_description: Three large, dark brown braised beef chunks rest in the center of a wide, clean white porcelain plate. The beef sits atop a bed of vibrant yellow, fluid polenta that spreads naturally without a ring. A rich, glossy deep red tomato sauce coats the beef, featuring whole purple Kalamata olives and softened onion bits. The beef displays a tender, shredded texture. Fresh green rosemary needles are scattered as a garnish. The plate is set on a dark wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin and a silver spoon. Natural side lighting creates soft shadows, highlighting the creamy texture of the polenta and the sheen of the braising liquid.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of robust Italian red wine
Provide crusty bread for the scarpetta tradition to clean the sauce
instructions: Pat beef dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy pot. Brown beef chunks on all sides. Remove beef.
Sauté onion and garlic until soft.
Add tomatoes and rosemary. Return beef to pot.
Pour in 400ml beef stock. Cover and simmer for 90 minutes.
Add olives. Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes to thicken sauce.
Check beef internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Boil water and remaining 400ml stock in a separate pan.
Whisk in cornmeal slowly. Reduce heat to low.
Stir cornmeal constantly for 20 minutes until creamy.
Stir in butter and Parmesan to finish the polenta.
notes: Use coarse cornmeal for a more traditional texture
Ensure the beef is fork-tender before removing from heat

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Braised Beef with Fermented Tomato and Root Vegetable Kimchi
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a single portion of slow-braised beef chunks, rich and tender, resting in a deep reddish-brown sauce. The beef exhibits a subtle seared crust on its exterior, contrasting with its moist interior. The sauce, glistening and slightly chunky from the fermented tomatoes, pools around the beef. Adjacent to the beef, a vibrant mound of root vegetable kimchi adds a burst of color with its crisp, diced orange carrots, white daikon, and pale green cabbage. A few fresh green herb leaves are artfully placed for a natural accent. The presentation is minimalistic, set on a handcrafted, cream-toned ceramic plate, allowing ample white space. The plate sits on a light, textured bamboo surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural lighting highlights the ingredients' organic textures. The background is clean and simple, with subtle natural elements.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomatoes (3-5 days prior): Dice tomatoes. Place in a clean jar. Add 20g coarse sea salt. Cover loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until tangy and bubbly. Refrigerate.

Prepare Root Vegetable Kimchi (3-7 days prior): Peel and dice root vegetables into 1 cm cubes. Shred napa cabbage. Combine vegetables. Add 15g coarse sea salt. Let sit 30 minutes. Drain excess liquid.

Grate ginger and 4 cloves garlic. Mix with sugar and chili flakes to form a paste. Combine paste with drained vegetables. Pack tightly into a clean jar. Cover loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-7 days. Refrigerate.
Cut beef chuck into 50g chunks. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Dice onions and remaining garlic. Add to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add fermented tomatoes (with their liquid) to the pot. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer 5 minutes.

Return seared beef to the pot. Add vegetable stock or water. Bring to a simmer. Cover. Reduce heat to low. Braise for 2-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove lid for the last 30 minutes of cooking. Allow sauce to reduce and thicken. Adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve braised beef chunks with generous sauce. Place a portion of root vegetable kimchi alongside. Garnish with fresh parsley or cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Red Currant and Cheese Curd Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single generous slice of the Rustic Red Currant and Cheese Curd Cake is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with a slightly uneven rim. The cake has a golden-brown crust with visible red currants dotted throughout and on top. The interior reveals a soft, slightly dense crumb, light yellow from the cheese curd and eggs, with bursts of red from the currants. A light dusting of powdered sugar unevenly covers the top. The slice is cut cleanly, showing the rustic, home-baked texture. The whole cake, slightly cooled, sits on a wooden cake stand in the background, showing its full, round shape. The plate rests on a well-worn wooden dining table, rich with natural grain. Beside the plate, a simple, folded linen napkin in a muted color. A plain, sturdy fork is placed to the right of the plate. The lighting is warm and soft, mimicking natural light filtering through a kitchen window, creating gentle shadows. The background is slightly blurred, showing hints of a homely kitchen, perhaps a ceramic jug or a simple fruit bowl, suggesting a lived-in family space.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 15cm round cake pan.
In a large bowl, cream softened butter and 100g granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time. Mix in vanilla extract.
Add well-drained cheese curd to the mixture. Beat until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whisk amaranth flour, baking powder, and salt.
Gradually fold dry ingredients into the wet mixture until just combined. Do not overmix.
Gently toss red currants with 20g granulated sugar.
Fold two-thirds of the sugared red currants into the cake batter.
Pour batter into the prepared cake pan. Spread evenly.
Scatter remaining red currants over the top of the batter.
Bake for 40-45 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool cake in the pan for 10 minutes. Then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
Dust with powdered sugar before serving, if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Red Currant and Cheese Curd Amaranth Cake
recipes.visual_description: A generous slice of Rustic Red Currant and Cheese Curd Amaranth Cake rests on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. The slice showcases a moist, golden-yellow crumb dotted with vibrant red currants. The cake's golden-brown top crust is softly dusted with powdered sugar. The overall presentation is unpretentious and homely. The plate sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, with the remaining whole cake, on a cooling rack, softly blurred in the background. A casually folded cloth napkin and a simple fork are nearby. Warm, inviting light from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, family kitchen atmosphere, emphasizing comfort and the natural appeal of this freshly baked dessert.

ingredients.name: Cheese curd (fine or pressed, not dry)

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 20cm round cake pan.
Whisk amaranth flour, baking powder, and salt in a medium bowl. Set aside.
In a large bowl, cream softened butter and granulated sugar until light and fluffy. Use an electric mixer.
Beat in eggs one at a time. Mix well after each addition.
Add cheese curd, vanilla extract, and lemon zest. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients. Mix on low speed until just combined. Do not overmix. A few lumps are fine.
Gently fold in red currants. Distribute evenly.
Pour batter into prepared cake pan. Smooth the top.
Bake for 45-55 minutes. A wooden skewer inserted into the center should come out clean.
Cool cake in pan for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Dust cooled cake generously with powdered sugar before serving.
notes: Ensure cheese curd is not too wet; if it is, gently press out excess moisture.
Amaranth flour can make cakes dense. Do not overmix the batter to keep it light.
Store cake at room temperature in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Roasted Bell Pepper Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken and Roasted Bell Pepper Rigatoni is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain pasta bowl. The rigatoni pasta is generously coated in a rich, rustic tomato sauce, showing its deep red hue. Interspersed throughout are golden-brown seared chicken chunks (3 cm), along with vibrant strips of roasted red and yellow bell peppers (1.5 cm wide), adding color and texture. A few fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered over the top, and a light dusting of finely grated white Parmesan cheese completes the dish. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a fork, knife, and a folded cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut bell peppers into 1.5 cm wide strips. Toss with 10 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly charred. Set aside.
Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 20 ml olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd. Cook in batches if necessary. Remove chicken and set aside. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer until wine is mostly reduced, about 3 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 15 minutes.
While sauce simmers, cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 125 ml pasta cooking water before draining.
Add seared chicken chunks and roasted bell peppers to the sauce. Simmer for 5-7 minutes to meld flavors. Stir in a splash of reserved pasta water if sauce is too thick.
Add drained rigatoni to the sauce. Toss to coat evenly.
Serve immediately in wide bowls. Garnish with fresh basil leaves and grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Roasting bell peppers enhances their sweetness and adds a smoky depth to the sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo y Arroz Estilo Paella
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant individual portion of Spanish Paella-style Chicken and Rice is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Golden-yellow Bomba rice, infused with saffron and paprika, forms the base, its distinct grains visible. Nestled within the rice are two succulent, bone-in chicken thighs, seared to a deep golden-brown, their skin slightly crisp. Scattered throughout the rice are small, tender cubes of vibrant red and green bell peppers, and softened pieces of diced tomato, adding bursts of color. A generous sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the dish, providing a fresh contrast. A quarter lemon wedge sits beside the paella, ready to be squeezed. The dish exhibits balanced color, varied textures, and a professional, yet approachable, presentation, honoring traditional Spanish aesthetics. The background features a simple wooden table and a neatly folded cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the paella pan at the table for a communal experience.
Offer with crusty bread for dipping into the flavorful rice.
Serve alongside a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Always provide lemon wedges for diners to squeeze over their portion.

ingredients.name: Ripe tomatoes, grated or finely diced
Red bell pepper, diced into 1 cm cubes
Green bell pepper, diced into 1 cm cubes
Saffron threads, steeped in 60ml hot water

instructions: Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large paella pan or wide, shallow pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken.
Add diced onion and bell peppers to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and grated tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until mixture thickens.
Add smoked paprika and sweet paprika. Stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rice. Stir to coat rice grains evenly with the sofrito. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in hot chicken broth and steeped saffron. Return chicken pieces to the pan, nestling them into the rice.

Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes. Do not stir the rice. Allow liquid to absorb and 'socarrat' to form. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat. Cover pan with foil or a clean kitchen towel. Let rest for 10 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley. Serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Encourage the formation of 'socarrat' – a crispy, caramelized crust at the bottom of the pan – by avoiding stirring the rice during simmering and listening for a crackling sound at the end.
Use a wide, shallow pan for best results, as this allows the rice to cook evenly and for the socarrat to develop.

recipes.recipe_name: Argentinian Spicy Beef Medallions with Caramelized Onions and Jalapeño Relish
recipes.visual_description: Presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Two thick, seared beef medallions, with a dark brown crust and tender pink interior, are centered. Adjacent, a mound of deeply golden, translucent caramelized onions. A vibrant, chunky relish, featuring bright green finely chopped pickled jalapeños and red hot sauce, is spooned over one beef medallion. Golden-brown roasted potato wedges with crispy exteriors are artfully arranged. A small fresh parsley sprig garnishes the relish. The plating is balanced and professional, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, white cotton napkin, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors against a minimal, blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Accompany with a glass of robust Argentinian Malbec wine.
Traditionally, this dish would be served with "papas fritas" (fries) or "papas asadas" (roasted potatoes).

ingredients.name: Beef tenderloin or sirloin
ingredients.quantity: 600 g, cut into 8 medallions (approx. 2.5 cm thick)

instructions: Prepare Potatoes: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss potato wedges with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 30-40 minutes until golden and tender.

Caramelize Onions: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add sliced onions and sugar. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 25-30 minutes until deeply golden brown and soft. Set aside.

Make Jalapeño Relish: In a small bowl, combine finely chopped pickled jalapeños, smoky hot sauce, minced garlic, red wine vinegar, and 30 ml olive oil. Stir in chopped fresh parsley. Season with salt to taste.
Cook Beef: Season beef medallions generously with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan or cast-iron skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Sear Beef: Place beef medallions in the hot pan. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. Remove beef from pan and let rest for 5 minutes.

Plate: Arrange two beef medallions on each plate. Place a mound of caramelized onions beside the beef. Spoon a generous amount of jalapeño relish over or next to the beef. Serve immediately with roasted potato wedges.
notes: Adjust the amount of hot sauce in the relish to suit your spice preference.
For optimal caramelization, cook onions slowly and do not rush the process.
traditional_techniques: Searing: High-heat cooking of beef to achieve a flavorful crust.
Caramelizing: Slow cooking of onions to develop deep sweetness and color.
Relish preparation: Similar in concept to creating a "chimichurri" style sauce, focusing on fresh ingredients and acidity.

recipes.recipe_name: Peanut Butter & Roasted Bell Pepper Entremet
recipes.visual_description: A single, precisely crafted mini entremet sits centered on a clean white porcelain plate. The entremet, approximately 6 cm in diameter and 4 cm tall, is enrobed in a smooth, glossy, golden-brown peanut glaze. Its surface is pristine and reflective. A subtle cross-section, if visible, hints at layers of creamy peanut butter mousse, a delicate roasted red bell pepper and caramelized onion crémeux (a soft, warm reddish-orange hue), a refreshing translucent green cucumber-lime gel insert, and a crisp, light golden dacquoise base. The edges of the entremet are sharp and clean. Garnish is minimal and elegant: a scattering of a few perfectly candied peanuts and a tiny, vibrant green micro-basil leaf or a whisper of lime zest for a fresh accent. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the pastry’s textures and colors, creating a professional and inviting presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.

For Dacquoise: Whisk egg whites until soft peaks form. Gradually add 10g caster sugar, whisk until stiff and glossy. Fold in ground peanuts and icing sugar. Pipe a 6 cm circle onto parchment. Bake 15-20 minutes until golden. Cool. Trim to fit mold base.

For Roasted Bell Pepper & Caramelized Onion Crémeux: Dice bell pepper and onion into small cubes. Sauté in olive oil over low heat until very soft and caramelized, about 15-20 minutes. Add 15g caster sugar; cook until dissolved. Blend mixture until smooth puree. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Bloom 0.5g gelatin in cold water.

Whisk egg yolk into the warm puree. Return to saucepan. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened (82°C). Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin. Stir in butter until melted and smooth. Pour into a small container. Chill until firm.

For Cucumber-Lime Gel: Juice cucumber. Combine cucumber juice, lime juice, and 5g caster sugar in a small saucepan. Whisk in agar-agar. Bring to a boil, simmer 1 minute. Pour into a flat dish (approx. 5x5 cm). Chill until set. Cut a 4 cm circle.

For Peanut Butter Mousse: Bloom 0.5g gelatin in cold water. Whisk egg yolk and 10g caster sugar in a bowl. Heat milk in a saucepan until simmering. Slowly pour hot milk into egg yolk mixture, whisking constantly. Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over low heat, stirring, until thickened (82°C). Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin and 30g peanut butter until smooth.
Whip 50ml cream to soft peaks. Fold whipped cream into the peanut butter mixture gently.

Assembly: Place the dacquoise base inside a 6-7 cm diameter entremet ring mold on a flat tray. Pipe a thin layer of peanut butter mousse over the dacquoise. Place the firm bell pepper-onion crémeux disc on top. Pipe more mousse around and over the crémeux. Gently press the cucumber-lime gel disc into the center. Top with remaining mousse, smoothing the surface. Freeze solid for at least 4 hours.

For Glaze: Bloom 0.5g gelatin in cold water. Melt white chocolate. Heat 20ml cream and glucose syrup until simmering. Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin. Pour hot cream mixture over melted white chocolate and 10g peanut butter. Emulsify with a whisk until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Let cool to 30-35°C.
Unmold frozen entremet. Place on a wire rack over a tray. Pour glaze evenly over the frozen entremet, ensuring full coverage. Let excess drip off. Transfer entremet to a serving plate.
Allow entremet to thaw in the refrigerator for 30-45 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Chicken & Cheese Croquettes
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of three Crispy Chicken & Cheese Croquettes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Each croquette is a uniform, golden-brown cylinder, approximately 6 cm long, with a distinctly crispy Panko breadcrumb crust. The exterior shows a rich, even color with visible texture from the breadcrumbs. One croquette is gently broken open to reveal its creamy, savory interior of finely shredded chicken, melted pale yellow American cheese, and flecks of green parsley, contrasting with the crisp shell. The croquettes are arranged neatly but organically in the center of the plate, leaving moderate negative space. A vibrant green sprig of fresh parsley is placed beside them, along with a bright yellow lemon wedge, ready for squeezing. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, unobtrusive background that suggests a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Poach chicken breast in lightly salted water until cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Shred chicken finely. Set aside.
Melt 30g butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Whisk in 30g flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in 250ml milk. Continue whisking until sauce thickens to a béchamel consistency. Remove from heat.
Add shredded chicken, 100g shredded American cheese, 2 minced garlic cloves, 15g finely chopped fresh parsley, salt, and pepper to the béchamel sauce. Mix thoroughly.
Transfer the mixture to a shallow dish. Cover tightly. Chill for at least 2 hours, or until firm enough to handle.
Prepare a breading station: Place 50g flour in the first dish. Whisk 2 eggs in the second dish. Place 150g Panko breadcrumbs in the third dish.
Form the chilled mixture into 12 small, uniform cylindrical or oval croquettes, approximately 30g each.
Roll each croquette first in flour, ensuring full coverage. Tap off excess.
Dip floured croquette into whisked egg, letting excess drip off.
Finally, coat croquette thoroughly in Panko breadcrumbs. Gently press crumbs to adhere firmly.
Heat 750ml vegetable oil in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 175°C.
Carefully fry croquettes in batches for 3-4 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Do not overcrowd the pot.
Remove fried croquettes with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels.
Serve immediately. Arrange 3 croquettes per plate. Garnish each plate with a fresh lemon wedge and additional fresh parsley sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Mustard Sauce and Tomato-Thyme Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of pan-seared chicken is centered on a clean, white porcelain plate. The chicken thigh, bone-in and skin-on, exhibits a beautiful golden-brown, crisp skin and tender, juicy meat. It rests beside a neatly mounded portion of vibrant tomato-thyme rice, flecked with red diced tomatoes and green thyme. A rich, creamy, and golden-beige mustard sauce is artfully spooned over and around the chicken, creating a luscious sheen. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley. The arrangement is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple, light wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A crisp white cotton napkin is folded beside the plate, accompanied by classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and warm colors of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty baguette for soaking up the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine, such as Sancerre or Sauvignon Blanc.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 8-10 minutes until golden and crispy. Flip and sear for another 3-5 minutes.
Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the same skillet. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with white wine, if using. Scrape up any browned bits. Cook until liquid is almost evaporated.
Stir in Dijon mustard. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in chicken stock and heavy cream. Bring to a simmer. Add 4 thyme sprigs. Return chicken to the skillet, skin-side up.
Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F). Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
While chicken bakes, prepare the rice. Melt butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add remaining diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes.
Add rice to the saucepan. Stir for 1 minute to coat grains. Add diced tomatoes and remaining 4 thyme sprigs. Pour in 400ml chicken stock.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Discard thyme sprigs from sauce and rice. Garnish chicken with fresh chopped parsley.
Serve chicken with creamy mustard sauce over a bed of tomato-thyme rice.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For extra flavor, reserve a tablespoon of chicken fat from searing to cook the rice onion.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Bacon & Mushroom Pasta Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Creamy Bacon & Mushroom Pasta Salad is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, mounded generously in the center. Al dente penne pasta, coated in a light, creamy mayonnaise-based dressing, forms the base. Interspersed throughout are golden-brown roasted potato cubes (2cm), crispy irregular chunks of pan-fried bacon, and tender, sautéed mushroom slices. Bright green, 1cm diced cucumber pieces and small cubes of sharp cheddar cheese add fresh color and texture. The salad is garnished with a generous sprinkle of roughly chopped fresh parsley and golden-brown, crispy 1.5cm bread croutons scattered on top. The overall presentation is inviting, with a balanced mix of colors and textures. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table, with a folded white cotton napkin and a silver fork beside it, under natural, even lighting. The background features a subtly blurred modern bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash and cut potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until golden and tender. Flip halfway through. Set aside to cool.
Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water to stop cooking. Drain thoroughly. Set aside.
Cut bacon into irregular 2 cm chunks. Cook in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels. Reserve 15 ml bacon fat in the skillet.
Slice mushrooms. Add to the skillet with reserved bacon fat. Sauté over medium-high heat for 5-7 minutes until browned and tender. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside to cool.
Cut bread slices into 1.5 cm cubes. Toss with remaining 15 ml olive oil. Bake on a separate baking sheet for 8-10 minutes, or until golden and crispy. Set aside.
Dice cucumber into 1 cm cubes. Cut cheddar cheese into 1 cm cubes.
In a large bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, white wine vinegar, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Add cooled pasta, roasted potatoes, crispy bacon, sautéed mushrooms, diced cucumber, and diced cheese to the dressing. Gently toss to combine all ingredients evenly.
Chop fresh parsley. Stir half of the parsley into the salad.
Cover the salad and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld. Serve chilled, garnished with remaining fresh parsley and crispy croutons.
notes: For best flavor, chill the salad for at least 30 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Decadent Chocolate Layer Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single, precisely cut wedge of decadent chocolate layer cake stands elegantly on a clean white round porcelain dinner plate. The slice reveals distinct, moist layers of deep dark chocolate cake interspersed with thick, smooth bands of rich chocolate buttercream frosting. A light dusting of unsweetened cocoa powder graces the top of the slice, and a few vibrant red fresh raspberries are artfully placed beside it, providing a striking color contrast. The plate rests on a simple light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by a crisp, folded off-white linen napkin. In the softly blurred background, the remaining whole, perfectly frosted cake sits on a modest white cake stand, hinting at the full dessert. Natural, even lighting highlights the cake's textures and rich brown hues, creating an inviting, professional bistro-style presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour two 18 cm round cake pans. Line bottoms with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, granulated sugar, 60g cocoa powder, baking soda, baking powder, and 3g salt.
In another bowl, whisk eggs, 120ml milk, vegetable oil, and 10ml vanilla extract.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Mix until just combined.
Stir in hot water. Batter will be thin.
Divide batter evenly between prepared pans. Bake 25-30 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool cakes in pans 10 minutes. Invert onto wire racks to cool completely.
For the buttercream, in a large bowl, beat softened butter until creamy.
Gradually add icing sugar and 40g cocoa powder. Beat until combined.
Pour in cooled melted chocolate, 60ml milk, 5ml vanilla extract, and a pinch of salt. Beat on medium-high speed until light and fluffy.
Level cooled cake layers if needed. Place one layer on a serving plate. Spread a generous layer of buttercream on top.
Place second cake layer on top. Apply a thin crumb coat of buttercream over the entire cake. Chill 15 minutes.
Apply remaining buttercream smoothly over the top and sides.
Dust top of cake with a small amount of cocoa powder. Arrange fresh raspberries artfully on top or around the base.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Butter Cake with Crème Fraîche Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single wedge of golden-yellow lemon butter cake, approximately 4cm thick at its widest point, is positioned slightly off-center on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The cake slice reveals a fine, even crumb. A thin, translucent sheen of pale white crème fraîche glaze cascades gently over the top and sides of the slice, pooling slightly at the base. A small cluster of vibrant mixed fresh berries, including bright red raspberries and deep blue blueberries, is artfully arranged beside the cake slice. A single small, fresh green mint sprig is tucked among the berries. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin is positioned neatly beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from the side, creating soft shadows that add depth. The background is a soft, blurred representation of a modern bistro setting, providing a warm, inviting atmosphere without distracting from the food.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour a 20cm round cake pan.
Cream softened butter and granulated sugar in a large bowl until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time. Scrape down bowl sides after each addition.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
Combine milk, lemon zest, lemon juice, and vanilla extract in a small bowl.
Add dry ingredients to wet ingredients in three additions, alternating with milk mixture in two additions. Begin and end with dry. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into the prepared pan. Smooth the top with a spatula.
Bake 30-35 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool cake in pan for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack. Cool completely.
Prepare glaze: Whisk powdered sugar, crème fraîche, and fresh lemon juice in a medium bowl until smooth.
Pour glaze evenly over the cooled cake. Allow glaze to set slightly.
Slice cake into 4 equal portions. Plate each slice for serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Blackberry & Vanilla Bean Loaf Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant slice of Blackberry & Vanilla Bean Loaf Cake is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, positioned slightly off-centre. The slice reveals distinct layers: a golden-brown, moist vanilla bean cake base, generously topped with a vibrant, deep purple blackberry compote, and finished with a smooth, creamy white cream cheese glaze. The compote is artfully drizzled over the glaze, showcasing its glossy texture and the rich color of the blackberries. Two plump, fresh blackberries and a small, verdant mint sprig are placed beside the slice as a fresh garnish. In the soft-focused background, the remaining whole loaf cake sits on a simple cake stand, hinting at its full form. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and natural, even lighting. The overall composition is clean, professional, and highlights the cake's refined texture and inviting colors with ample negative space.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour a 23x13 cm loaf tin.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
Cream softened butter and 200g granulated sugar in a large bowl until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time. Mix well after each addition.
Alternate adding dry ingredients and 120ml milk to butter mixture. Begin and end with dry ingredients. Mix until just combined.
Stir in vanilla bean paste. Pour batter into prepared loaf tin. Smooth top.
Bake 45-55 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean. Cool in tin for 10 minutes. Transfer to wire rack to cool completely.
Combine 200g blackberries, 50g granulated sugar, and lemon juice in a small saucepan.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until berries soften and sauce thickens slightly. Mash lightly if desired. Cool completely.
Beat softened cream cheese and icing sugar in a bowl until smooth.
Stir in melted butter and 30ml milk until smooth and pourable. Add more milk if needed for desired consistency.
Pour cream cheese glaze over cooled loaf cake. Let it drip down the sides.
Spoon cooled blackberry compote over the glazed cake. Create a swirl or drizzle pattern.
Garnish with fresh blackberries and mint sprigs before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Fig and Apple Millefoglie with Honey-Almond Cream
recipes.visual_description: A single, exquisitely crafted millefoglie stands tall on a pristine white porcelain dessert plate with a subtle gold rim, centered with abundant negative space. Three perfectly cut, crisp, golden-brown puff pastry layers are visible, showcasing their delicate lamination. Between each layer, a generous, smooth piping of pale ivory honey-almond diplomat cream provides a soft contrast. A vibrant, deep ruby-red fig and apple compote is precisely placed within the cream layers, offering a burst of color. The top pastry layer is lightly dusted with icing sugar, creating a subtle frosty sheen. A few precisely placed, golden-brown toasted slivered almonds are scattered artfully on the top layer, alongside a tiny sprig of fresh green microgreens, adding a delicate touch of color and texture. The presentation is architectural and minimalist, emphasizing the precision of each component. The plate rests on a polished white marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that creates soft shadows, highlighting the dessert's textures. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a crisp triangle, is positioned to the side, enhancing the haute patisserie shop aesthetic.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Place puff pastry on parchment. Pierce evenly with a fork (docking).
Place another sheet of parchment and a second baking tray on top to weigh down. This prevents excessive puffing.
Bake for 15 minutes. Remove top tray and parchment. Continue baking for 10-15 minutes until golden brown and crisp.
Remove from oven. Dust immediately with icing sugar. Return to oven for 2-3 minutes to caramelize. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
Cool completely on a wire rack. Once cool, trim edges. Cut pastry into 12 identical rectangles (approx. 8cm x 4cm) for 4 individual millefoglie.
Combine diced figs, apple, 30g honey, orange zest, cinnamon, lemon juice, and water in a small saucepan.
Cook over medium heat for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until fruit is soft and liquid has reduced to a syrupy consistency. Mash lightly with a fork for desired texture.
Remove from heat. Cool completely.
Heat milk in a saucepan until just simmering.
In a separate bowl, whisk egg yolks, granulated sugar, and cornstarch until pale and smooth.
Gradually pour hot milk into egg mixture, whisking constantly to temper.
Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until thickened and boiling for 1 minute.
Remove from heat. Stir in almond paste and 30g honey until dissolved. Stir in cold butter until melted and incorporated.
Transfer pastry cream to a clean bowl. Cover surface directly with plastic wrap to prevent a skin forming. Chill in refrigerator for at least 2 hours until very cold.
In a cold bowl, whip heavy cream to medium peaks.
Gently fold whipped cream into the chilled almond pastry cream until fully combined. This is your diplomat cream.
Transfer diplomat cream to a piping bag fitted with a plain round or star tip.
Place one pastry rectangle on a serving plate. Pipe a layer of diplomat cream evenly over the pastry.
Spoon a line of fig and apple compote down the center of the cream layer.
Carefully place a second pastry rectangle on top. Pipe another layer of diplomat cream.
Add another line of fig and apple compote.
Top with the third pastry rectangle.
Dust the top pastry layer lightly with icing sugar.
Arrange a few toasted slivered almonds on top. Add a small sprig of microgreens or mint leaves if desired.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure puff pastry is fully chilled before baking for best lamination and crispness.
Chilling the pastry cream thoroughly is crucial for a stable diplomat cream.
Assemble just before serving to maintain the crispness of the puff pastry.

recipes.recipe_name: Vanilla Tapioca Crémeux, Poached Pear, Strawberry Fluid Gel, Cocoa Soil
recipes.visual_description: The dessert is presented on an expensive bone china plate with subtle patterns, resting on a premium grey veined marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, sits elegantly. The composition is minimalist and organic, with abundant negative space. A dollop of creamy, off-white vanilla tapioca crémeux forms a soft base. Three to four thin, translucent slices of gently poached pear are artfully arranged over the crémeux, showcasing their delicate form and warm hue. Vibrant crimson dots and elegant streaks of strawberry fluid gel are strategically placed, providing contrasting color and acidity. A fine scattering of dark cocoa nib soil adds textural crunch and deep color. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows. A single, small, fresh strawberry half, glistening, serves as a precise garnish, adding a final touch of fresh color and natural form.
instructions: Prepare Poached Pears: Peel pears. Cut each pear into 4 wedges. Core wedges.
In a saucepan, combine 500ml water, 100g sugar, and cinnamon stick. Bring to a simmer.
Add pear wedges. Poach gently for 10-15 minutes until tender but still firm.
Remove pears from liquid. Cool completely. Slice each wedge into 2-3 thin pieces just before plating.
Prepare Vanilla Tapioca Crémeux: Rinse tapioca pearls. Drain.
In a saucepan, combine coconut milk, 50g sugar, vanilla bean seeds and pod, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Stir in tapioca pearls. Cook over low heat, stirring frequently, for 15-20 minutes until tapioca is translucent and liquid is thickened to a creamy consistency.
Remove vanilla pod. Cool slightly.
Prepare Strawberry Fluid Gel: Wash and hull strawberries. Roughly chop.
In a small saucepan, combine strawberries, 20g sugar, and 50ml water. Simmer for 5-7 minutes until soft.
Blend mixture until very smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve to remove seeds.
Return strained puree to a clean saucepan. Whisk in agar-agar powder. Bring to a boil, whisking constantly, for 1 minute.
Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until firm (at least 1 hour).
Once firm, cut gel into cubes. Blend until smooth and fluid. Transfer to a squeeze bottle or piping bag.
Prepare Cocoa Nib Soil: Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine flour, cocoa powder, 20g sugar, and a pinch of salt.
Cut in cold vegan butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Stir in cocoa nibs.
Spread mixture evenly on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 10-12 minutes, stirring once, until crisp. Cool completely.
Assemble and Plate: Place a generous spoonful of warm or room temperature vanilla tapioca crémeux slightly off-center on each plate.
Arrange 3-4 thin slices of poached pear elegantly on top of or next to the crémeux.
Dot the plate with small, artful drops or swirls of strawberry fluid gel.
Sprinkle a small amount of cocoa nib soil sparingly around the crémeux and pear for texture.
notes: Ensure tapioca crémeux is not too thick; it should be fluid and creamy.
Fluid gel must be perfectly smooth after blending.
Pears should be tender but hold their shape.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Lemon Herb Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Baked Lemon Herb Chicken and Potatoes rests on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The plate sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table, softly lit by warm kitchen light. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh, whole and un-sliced, is the focal point, positioned slightly off-center. Its skin shows the faint char of roasting and flecks of dried herbs. Beside the chicken are several thick-cut, roasted potato wedges, their edges caramelized and interiors soft, some still bearing their skin. Bright yellow lemon slices, slightly browned from baking, are tucked among the chicken and potatoes, adding a pop of color. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley provides a fresh contrast. The overall arrangement is natural and unforced, typical of a comforting home-cooked meal. A simple, folded cloth napkin and a plain water glass are visible in the soft-focus background, enhancing the homely, lived-in atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges, 30ml olive oil, half of the minced garlic, half of the rosemary, half of the thyme, 0.5 teaspoon salt, and 0.25 teaspoon black pepper. Toss to coat.
Spread potatoes in a single layer on a large baking tray.

Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. In the same bowl, toss chicken thighs with remaining 30ml olive oil, remaining minced garlic, remaining rosemary, remaining thyme, 0.5 teaspoon salt, and 0.25 teaspoon black pepper. Add lemon juice from one lemon.
Arrange chicken thighs skin-side up among the potatoes on the baking tray. Place lemon slices over and around the chicken.
Pour chicken broth into the tray, if using, to keep things moist.
Bake for 35-45 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Duck Breast with Cherry-Brandy-Cocoa Reduction, Sweet Potato Puree, and Sautéed Tatsoi
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared duck breast is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered for professional food photography. The duck breast features a perfectly rendered, golden-brown, crispy skin and a tender, moist interior, served as a whole piece. Beside it, a smooth, light orange sweet potato puree forms a refined quenelle. Vibrant green, lightly wilted tatsoi leaves are neatly arranged, adding a fresh contrast. A glossy, deep reddish-brown cherry-brandy-cocoa reduction is elegantly drizzled over the duck and pools subtly around the puree. The dish is garnished with a small sprig of fresh thyme, enhancing its natural color balance. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a white cotton napkin placed beside the plate, and standard European flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and rich colors of the dish, creating an inviting and sophisticated presentation with appropriate negative space.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Peel and dice sweet potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Boil in salted water until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain sweet potatoes. Return to pot. Add 50g butter and cream cheese. Mash until smooth. Whisk in egg white until light and fluffy. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Score duck breast skin in a crosshatch pattern. Season duck generously with salt and pepper.

Heat a cold, oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place duck breasts skin-side down. Cook for 8-10 minutes, rendering fat until skin is crispy and golden brown. Pour off excess fat as it accumulates.

Flip duck breasts. Cook meat-side down for 2-3 minutes. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 6-8 minutes for medium-rare, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F). For well-done, cook to 75°C (167°F).
Remove duck from oven. Let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
While duck rests, finely dice shallot and mince garlic. In the same skillet (pour off most duck fat, leave 15 ml), sauté shallot until translucent, about 2 minutes. Add garlic; cook 30 seconds.

Deglaze pan with brandy. Add chai tea bag. Simmer for 1 minute. Add cherries, diced peaches, cocoa powder, and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce sauce by half, about 8-10 minutes. Remove chai tea bag. Season sauce with salt and pepper.
Wash tatsoi. In a separate pan, melt remaining 30g butter with olive oil over medium heat. Add tatsoi and thyme sprigs. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until wilted. Season with salt and pepper.

To plate, spoon a generous quenelle of sweet potato puree onto each plate. Place a whole duck breast beside the puree. Arrange sautéed tatsoi next to the duck. Spoon the cherry-brandy-cocoa reduction over the duck and around the plate.

recipes.recipe_name: Coffee Chocolate Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Coffee Chocolate Risotto is presented in a shallow, clean white round bowl. The risotto is creamy, fluid, and has a rich, earthy brown hue, subtly flecked with darker chocolate. It is not mounded but allowed to spread naturally in the bowl. Resting on top are golden-brown seared cremini mushroom slices, their irregular shapes adding organic texture. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers parts of the risotto, providing a contrasting lighter color. Fresh green thyme leaves are delicately scattered over the top, offering a pop of vibrant color and freshness. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware, under soft, even natural lighting, suggesting a relaxed modern bistro setting.
instructions: Heat vegetable broth in a saucepan. Keep it at a gentle simmer.
Finely dice shallots. Mince garlic. Slice mushrooms thinly.
In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, melt 20 g butter with olive oil over medium heat.
Add diced shallots. Cook until translucent, about 3-4 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until rice grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in the strong brewed coffee. Stir until fully absorbed by the rice.
Add one ladleful of hot vegetable broth to the rice. Stir continuously until liquid is mostly absorbed.
Continue adding broth one ladleful at a time, stirring constantly, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.
While risotto cooks, melt the remaining 20 g butter in a separate pan over medium-high heat.
Add sliced mushrooms. Sear until golden brown and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
When the risotto is creamy and al dente (still has a slight bite), remove from heat.
Stir in grated dark chocolate, full-fat milk, and 60 g grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously to combine and create a creamy texture. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Divide risotto among four shallow bowls. Top each serving with seared mushrooms. Garnish with remaining grated Parmesan and fresh thyme leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: For a vegan version, use plant-based milk, vegan butter, and nutritional yeast instead of Parmesan cheese.
Ensure coffee is unsweetened and strong for the best flavor balance.

recipes.recipe_name: Kimchi Beef & Broccoli Bowl
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. A generous portion of vibrant green roasted broccoli florets forms a base on one side. Alongside, tender, dark brown beef chunks, coated in a glossy sauce, are piled naturally. A bright red, roughly chopped mound of kimchi provides a striking color contrast next to the beef. Creamy, pale green avocado slices are casually arranged, slightly overlapping. Crowning the bowl is a single fried egg, with a firm white and a rich, golden yolk. The components touch and overlap, creating a hearty, comforting, and natural appearance. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a home kitchen. A pair of simple metal chopsticks rests beside the bowl, with a plain cloth napkin casually placed nearby. The overall presentation is unpretentious and focuses on the wholesome, satisfying nature of the meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed rice.
Offer extra gochujang (Korean chili paste) for added heat.
instructions: Cut beef into 2.5cm chunks or thick slices.
In a bowl, combine soy sauce, 15ml sesame oil, minced garlic, grated ginger, rice vinegar, and optional honey. Add beef chunks. Toss to coat. Marinate for at least 15 minutes.

Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut broccoli into florets. Toss broccoli with 15ml cooking oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly charred. Alternatively, steam until tender-crisp.

Heat 15ml cooking oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Remove beef from marinade, reserving marinade. Sear beef in batches to avoid overcrowding, 2-3 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.
Pour reserved marinade into the skillet with the beef. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring, until sauce slightly thickens. Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 15ml sesame oil.
Heat a separate non-stick pan over medium heat. Add a small amount of cooking oil. Fry eggs sunny-side up or over easy, until whites are set and yolks are runny.

Divide roasted broccoli among 4 serving bowls. Add a portion of the cooked beef and its sauce to each bowl. Arrange a generous scoop of roughly chopped kimchi alongside the beef. Place sliced avocado next to the other components. Top each bowl with a freshly fried egg.
notes: This dish is packed with protein and healthy fats.
Adjust spice level by adding more or less kimchi, or a dash of gochujang to the beef marinade.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Tuscan Chicken Pasta is artfully plated on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy fettuccine, intertwined with golden-brown chicken chunks and vibrant green spinach, forms a neat mound in the center. Interspersed are deep red sun-dried tomato slices and earthy brown mushroom slices. The chicken chunks are irregularly shaped, about 2 cm, displaying a seared crust. A light drizzle of the creamy sauce coats the pasta, showing its rich texture. A sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and finely chopped fresh basil leaves garnish the top, adding contrasting color and freshness. The arrangement is organic, allowing ingredients to show naturally. The plate is positioned on a simple light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and classic silver fork and spoon are placed beside the plate, with a small Italian-style bread roll. Natural, soft lighting highlights the textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine, like a Chianti Classico.

ingredients.name: Sun-dried tomatoes, oil-packed, drained and sliced

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Let rest. Cut into 2 cm chunks.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and browned.
Stir in sun-dried tomatoes and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Add heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir until cheese is melted and sauce slightly thickens.
While sauce simmers, cook fettuccine according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Drain, reserving 120 ml pasta water.
Add fresh spinach to the sauce. Cook until wilted, about 1-2 minutes.
Add cooked pasta and chicken chunks to the sauce. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water as needed.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
notes: For extra richness, add a knob of butter at the end.
Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Cabbage with Mustard Cream, Roasted Potatoes, and Green Beans
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Braised Cabbage with Mustard Cream, Roasted Potatoes, and Green Beans is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. At the center, two tender braised green cabbage wedges, lightly caramelized, are arranged and coated in a rich, pale yellow mustard cream sauce pooling subtly around them. Golden-brown roasted potato halves are scattered around the cabbage. Vibrant green roasted whole green beans are nestled amongst the potatoes, showing slight char marks. The dish is garnished with fresh chopped parsley. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting creates a clean, professional bistro atmosphere in the background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Wash potatoes. Halve or quarter larger potatoes. Trim green beans.
Toss potatoes with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 15 minutes.

Add green beans to the baking sheet with potatoes. Toss with remaining 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Continue roasting for 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and golden and beans are tender-crisp.
While vegetables roast, prepare cabbage. Remove outer leaves from cabbage. Cut cabbage into 8 thick wedges through the core.
Chop onion finely. Mince garlic.
Heat butter in a large braising pan or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add cabbage wedges to the pan. Sear lightly on cut sides for 3-4 minutes per side.
Pour in white wine. Bring to a simmer. Cook until liquid reduces by half, about 3 minutes.
Add vegetable stock and Dijon mustard. Stir to combine. Season with salt and pepper.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover. Braise for 15-20 minutes, or until cabbage is tender. Check tenderness with a knife.

Remove cabbage from pan. Keep warm. Stir heavy cream into the braising liquid. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Chop fresh parsley.
To serve, place braised cabbage wedges on plates. Spoon mustard cream sauce over cabbage. Arrange roasted potatoes and green beans alongside. Garnish with chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Blueberry Crumble Cake
recipes.visual_description: A thick, generous slice of golden-brown blueberry crumble cake sits on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The cake's top is covered with a rustic, golden-brown streusel topping, showing irregular clumps and a slightly crumbly texture. Below the streusel, the light, tender cake crumb is visible, studded generously with plump, dark purple blueberries, some slightly burst, releasing their juices into the cake. The side of the slice reveals the layered texture of the cake and topping. The plate rests on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple, silver dessert fork is placed casually beside the slice. In the background, the rest of the round cake, still in its baking pan, is partially visible, showing its full, comforting form. Warm, natural light streams in, highlighting the cake's textures and colors without harsh shadows.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 20 cm round cake pan.
Make streusel: Combine 75 g flour, 50 g sugar, and cinnamon in a bowl. Cut in cold butter with fingers or a pastry blender until coarse crumbs form. Set aside.
Combine dry ingredients: In a large bowl, whisk together 200 g flour, 150 g sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Combine wet ingredients: In a separate bowl, whisk eggs, milk, melted butter, and vanilla extract.
Combine wet and dry: Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Fold in blueberries: Gently fold in 150 g of blueberries into the batter.
Assemble cake: Pour batter into prepared cake pan. Sprinkle remaining 50 g blueberries over the top of the batter.
Add streusel: Evenly sprinkle the prepared streusel topping over the blueberries and batter.
Bake: Bake for 40-50 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool: Let cake cool in pan for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Carrot Velouté, Broccoli Florets, Crisps
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant orange Roasted Carrot Velouté rests in a deep, pristine white ceramic bowl, occupying the bottom third. The velouté is exquisitely smooth, reflecting soft light. Artfully arranged slightly off-center are 3-4 small, blanched broccoli florets, their bright green contrasting against the orange. A few golden-brown, paper-thin broccoli stem crisps are delicately placed, some standing, others flat, adding architectural texture. A small cluster of fresh green microgreens crowns the florets. Abundant negative space surrounds the composition. The bowl sits on a polished white Carrara marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin, precisely folded, lies beside it. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the minimalist elegance.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel and roughly chop carrots. Peel and quarter onion. Peel garlic cloves.
Toss carrots, onion, and garlic with 15 ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Roast vegetables on a baking sheet for 25-30 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.
Separate broccoli florets from stems. Reserve florets. Peel broccoli stems; thinly slice them into rounds.
Toss sliced broccoli stems with remaining 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast broccoli stem crisps for 10-15 minutes, until golden and crisp. Monitor closely to prevent burning.
In a large pot, combine roasted carrots, onion, garlic, vegetable broth, and coconut milk.
Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes.
Carefully transfer mixture to a high-speed blender. Blend until silky smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate smoothness. Adjust seasoning.
Bring a small pot of salted water to a boil. Blanch broccoli florets for 1-2 minutes, until tender-crisp and bright green. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.
Ladle velouté into individual bowls. Artfully arrange blanched broccoli florets and roasted broccoli crisps on top. Garnish with microgreens. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe is plant-based and Keto-friendly.
Ensure velouté is strained for a truly smooth, luxurious texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Korean Beef and Kimchi Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: The Korean Beef and Kimchi Rice Bowl presents a vibrant, well-composed single portion in a wide white porcelain bowl. Fluffy white short-grain rice forms the base. Pan-seared beef strips, rich brown, are neatly arranged alongside bright green, tender-crisp blanched broccoli florets. Sautéed red kimchi, glossy and softened, contrasts beautifully.
