recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Pork Ragu with Pappardelle is artfully presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Broad pappardelle ribbons are tossed with a rich, deep reddish-brown ragu, showcasing tender, shredded pork chunks. The sauce, infused with finely diced caramelized onion and subtle chili heat, has a creamy, almost orange hue from the added cream and Dijon mustard, creating a luxurious sheen. The pasta is generously mounded, with the succulent pork nestled among the flowing ribbons. A light drizzle of the chili-mustard cream gently swirls over the top, accentuating its richness. The dish is garnished simply with a scattering of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley, adding a touch of freshness and color contrast. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space. It rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the textures, against a soft, blurred restaurant-style background, evoking a casual bistro ambiance.

ingredients.name: Red chili flakes (or fresh red chili, minced)

instructions: Dice pork shoulder into 2-3 cm cubes. Season pork generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Add pork cubes. Sear pork on all sides until deeply browned. Remove pork and set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add finely diced onion to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and chili flakes (or fresh minced chili). Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return seared pork to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes and chicken stock. Stir to combine. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 2-3 hours, or until the pork is very tender and easily shredded with a fork.
Remove pork from the pot. Shred the pork using two forks. Return shredded pork to the ragu sauce. Stir well.
Stir Dijon mustard and heavy cream into the ragu. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
While ragu finishes, cook pappardelle pasta according to package directions in a large pot of salted boiling water until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 60 ml of pasta water.
Add drained pasta to the ragu. Toss gently to coat. If sauce is too thick, add a splash of reserved pasta water.
Plate immediately. Garnish each serving with chopped fresh parsley or chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Korean Chicken Bites with Truffle Gochujang Glaze
recipes.visual_description: Crispy, deep golden-brown chicken chunks, coated in a glossy, vibrant red-orange gochujang glaze, are artfully arranged on a clean, simple white porcelain sharing platter. Each chicken piece, approximately 3-4 cm, is visibly crisp with an inviting sheen from the sauce. Beside the chicken, clusters of sautéed oyster mushrooms, tender and slightly browned with irregular, organic shapes, add an earthy contrast. The dish is generously garnished with bright green, thinly sliced scallions scattered over the chicken and a sprinkle of toasted white sesame seeds, providing textural and color accents. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space, showcasing the inviting textures and rich colors. The platter rests on a light wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin is placed subtly beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish without harsh shadows. The background is minimal, evoking a modern bistro setting, allowing the food to be the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served as anju, a traditional Korean drinking snack, ideal with soju or beer.
Presented on a central sharing platter for communal dining.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and black pepper.
Dredge chicken chunks thoroughly in corn starch. Shake off excess starch.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or wok to 170°C.
Fry chicken in batches for 5-6 minutes until lightly golden. Remove chicken from oil.
Increase oil temperature to 180°C.
Return all chicken to oil. Fry for 2-3 minutes until deep golden brown and crispy. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken. Drain on a wire rack.
While chicken fries, prepare sauce. In a small saucepan, combine gochujang, soy sauce, mirin, rice vinegar, minced garlic, grated ginger, honey, and sesame oil.
Bring sauce to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Remove from heat. Stir in white truffle oil.
In a separate pan, heat a small amount of oil. Sauté torn oyster mushrooms for 3-4 minutes until tender and slightly browned. Season with a pinch of salt.
Place fried chicken in a large bowl. Pour truffle gochujang glaze over chicken. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange glazed chicken bites on a casual sharing platter or individual plates.
Place sautéed oyster mushrooms beside or around the chicken.
Garnish with thinly sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
traditional_techniques: Double-frying chicken for superior crispiness, characteristic of Korean fried chicken.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Chicken with Mushroom & Bean Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy risotto forms the base, spread naturally on a round white porcelain plate. A golden-brown, glistening braised chicken thigh, skin-on, sits prominently atop the risotto. The chicken is a whole piece, showcasing its rich, caramelized surface. Surrounding the chicken, the risotto is studded with earthy sliced mushrooms and dark black beans, providing textural contrast. Warm tones of golden chicken and creamy, off-white risotto are punctuated by deep brown mushrooms, dark beans, and vibrant green chopped parsley scattered over the chicken and risotto. The chicken skin is crisp, the meat tender and falling off the bone. The risotto is fluid and creamy, with a slight bite from the al dente rice and a soft texture from the beans and mushrooms. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, soft overhead lighting highlights the dish. The background is a subtly blurred, warm-toned bistro interior, suggesting a relaxed, inviting atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Black beans, canned, rinsed and drained

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown and crisp, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms and minced garlic. Cook until mushrooms release their moisture and begin to brown, about 7-10 minutes.
Stir in chopped red chili. Deglaze the pot with beer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the pot. Cover the pot tightly. Transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.

While chicken braises, prepare the risotto. In a separate medium saucepan, heat remaining olive oil over medium heat. Add remaining finely diced onion (if using a second onion, or portioned from the first). Cook until translucent.
Add Arborio rice to the saucepan. Stir constantly for 1-2 minutes until the edges of the rice grains become translucent.

Pour in one ladle of hot chicken stock. Stir continuously until the stock is fully absorbed by the rice. Continue adding stock ladle by ladle, stirring constantly, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.
When the risotto is creamy and al dente (has a slight bite), stir in the drained black beans, grated Parmesan cheese, and butter. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Remove chicken from the oven. Let rest briefly before serving.
To plate, spoon a generous portion of creamy risotto onto a warm plate. Place one braised chicken thigh on top. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure risotto remains fluid; it should not be stiff. Allow chicken to rest briefly before serving to retain juices.

recipes.recipe_name: Honey-Garlic Chicken Croquettes with Apple-Ginger Compote
recipes.visual_description: A sophisticated sharing platter of golden-brown honey-glazed chicken and roasted garlic croquettes. Each croquette, approximately 4cm long, is impeccably crisp, coated in golden panko and glistening with a thin, translucent honey-ginger glaze. The croquettes are arranged organically, not in a rigid pattern, on a pristine white bone china sharing plate with subtle texture. Alongside, delicate, abstract smears of pale yellow apple-ginger compote provide a contrasting soft element. A scattering of finely toasted golden brioche crumbs adds textural contrast. The composition is highly minimalist, featuring abundant negative space. A few vibrant green, finely sliced chives are precisely placed as the sole garnish, enhancing color and freshness. The setting is a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that creates elegant shadows, with an ultra-minimalist background to emphasize the culinary artistry. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the thoughtful arrangement and pristine presentation.

ingredients.name: Apples (e.g., Fuji or Gala), peeled, cored, diced

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut tops off garlic heads. Drizzle with olive oil. Wrap in foil. Roast for 40-50 minutes until very soft. Squeeze out pulp.
Poach chicken breast in lightly salted water until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Cool completely. Shred or finely mince chicken.
In a bowl, combine shredded chicken, roasted garlic pulp, and mascarpone cheese. Season with salt and pepper. Mix thoroughly. Chill for 30 minutes.
Take small portions (approx. 20g) of the chilled chicken mixture. Shape into small cylinders, approximately 4cm long and 1.5cm in diameter. You should yield about 20 croquettes.
Set up a breading station: one shallow dish with flour, one with beaten egg, and one with panko breadcrumbs mixed with 2 finely minced fresh garlic cloves.
Roll each croquette first in flour, then in beaten egg, and finally in the panko mixture, ensuring a complete and even coating. Place breaded croquettes on a tray. Chill for at least 30 minutes.

For the Apple-Ginger Compote: In a small saucepan, combine diced apples, 10g finely minced ginger, 10g unsalted butter, and 20ml water. Simmer over medium-low heat for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until apples are soft and break down. Mash slightly for a rustic texture. Season with a pinch of salt. Keep warm.

For the Honey-Ginger Glaze: In a small saucepan, combine honey, light soy sauce, and 10g grated ginger. Bring to a gentle simmer over low heat. Cook for 5 minutes until slightly reduced and syrupy. Keep warm.
For the Toasted Brioche Crumb: Pulse brioche slices in a food processor to create fine crumbs. In a dry pan, toast brioche crumbs over medium heat until golden and crisp. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or fryer to 170°C. Carefully fry croquettes in batches for 3-4 minutes until golden brown and crisp. Drain on paper towels.
Gently toss the hot croquettes in the warm honey-ginger glaze until lightly coated.

On a minimalist sharing platter or individual plates, artfully arrange the glazed croquettes. Place small, organic dollops or smears of the apple-ginger compote alongside. Sprinkle toasted brioche crumb over and around the croquettes. Garnish sparingly with finely sliced fresh chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Dark Chocolate Lava Cake with Summer Berry & Mango Compote
recipes.visual_description: A single warm, dark chocolate lava cake, rich and deep brown, sits centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. Its exterior is subtly firm, hinting at a molten interior. Beside it, a golden-orange roasted peach half, tender and slightly caramelized, gleams gently. A vibrant quenelle of summer berry and mango compote, bursting with reds, yellows, and hints of purple from the fruits, rests alongside the peach. The compote showcases softened pieces of quartered strawberry, diced mango, and halved cherries, retaining their individual forms. A delicate dusting of white powdered sugar lightly graces a portion of the plate, providing a refined contrast. The plate, set on a simple wooden bistro table, is illuminated by soft, even natural light, highlighting the dessert's balanced colors and inviting textures. The overall presentation is clean, professional, and approachable, with adequate negative space.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Grease and lightly flour 4 (150ml capacity) ramekins.
Melt 200g dark chocolate and 150g unsalted butter in a double boiler. Stir until smooth. Remove from heat.
In a separate bowl, whisk 2 large eggs, 2 large egg yolks, and 80g granulated sugar until pale and thick.
Fold the melted chocolate mixture into the egg mixture. Gently fold in 40g all-purpose flour until just combined. Do not overmix.
Divide batter evenly among prepared ramekins. Bake for 12-14 minutes, until edges are set but the center is still molten.
While cakes bake, prepare compote: Combine 200g quartered strawberries, 1 diced large mango, 150g halved cherries, 30g granulated sugar, and 15ml lemon juice in a saucepan.
Cook compote over medium heat, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes, until fruits soften and sauce thickens slightly. Remove from heat. Cool slightly.
For roasted peaches: Preheat oven to 190°C. Place 2 peach halves, cut-side up, on a baking sheet.
Brush peaches with 10g melted butter. Sprinkle with 15g light brown sugar. Roast for 15-20 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.
Let lava cakes cool in ramekins for 1 minute. Carefully invert each cake onto a serving plate.
Place a roasted peach half next to each lava cake. Spoon a generous portion of compote beside the peach.
Lightly dust the plate with powdered sugar before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chocolate Hotteok with Mint Sugar
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown hotteok, round and slightly flattened, rests on a simple white ceramic plate with a subtle rim. The pan-fried dough has a crispy exterior, revealing a hint of dark, melted chocolate and chili filling oozing from a small crack. A generous sprinkling of bright green mint sugar crystals covers the top, adding a fresh contrast. The plate is placed on a warm-toned, well-worn wooden dining table, suggesting a homely kitchen setting. Beside the plate, a traditional Korean ceramic tea cup or a small glass of Sikhye, along with a pair of simple metal chopsticks, completes the authentic, casual presentation. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting textures and inviting warmth of the dessert.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot, fresh from the pan.
Often enjoyed with a glass of Sikhye (sweet rice punch) or Sujeonggwa (cinnamon punch).
Eaten by hand as a warm, comforting snack or dessert.
instructions: Combine flour, yeast, 10g granulated sugar, and salt in a large bowl.
Add warm water. Mix until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap. Let the dough rise in a warm place for 1 hour, or until doubled in size.
Chop the dark chocolate into small pieces.
In a small bowl, mix the chopped chocolate, brown sugar, and fine chili powder for the filling.
Finely chop the fresh mint leaves. In another small bowl, mix the chopped mint with 50g granulated sugar to create mint sugar.
Divide the risen dough into 4 equal pieces.
Flatten one dough piece into a disk. Place a spoonful of the chocolate-chili filling in the center.
Gather the edges of the dough over the filling. Pinch them firmly to seal completely, forming a ball.
Heat a lightly oiled non-stick pan over medium heat.
Place a dough ball, seam-side down, in the hot pan.
Cook for 30 seconds. Use a spatula or hotteok press to flatten the dough into a pancake.
Cook for 2-3 minutes per side, until golden brown and puffed.
Repeat with the remaining dough and filling.
Serve the hotteok immediately. Sprinkle generously with the prepared mint sugar before serving.
notes: Adjust chili powder amount to your preference for subtle warmth or more heat.
Ensure the dough is well-sealed to prevent filling from leaking during cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Szechuan Crispy Tofu with Blistered Green Beans
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Szechuan Crispy Tofu with Blistered Green Beans presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Crispy, golden-brown tofu chunks, approximately 2cm cubes, are neatly arranged in the center, glistening with a vibrant orange-hued, glossy mandarin-chili glaze. Beside the tofu, deep green, blistered green beans, showing slight char marks, are artfully placed. A few thin segments of fresh mandarin orange are scattered over the dish. The dish is garnished with thinly sliced bright green scallions and a sprinkle of toasted white sesame seeds. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table. A white ceramic bowl of steamed jasmine rice and wooden chopsticks are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the food's textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with steamed jasmine rice.
instructions: Press tofu. Wrap in paper towels. Place heavy object on top. Press 30 minutes.
Cut pressed tofu into 2cm cubes. Toss with 30g cornstarch. Coat evenly.
Heat 60ml vegetable oil in large pan or wok over medium-high heat. Add tofu cubes. Fry until golden and crispy on all sides. This takes 8-10 minutes. Remove tofu. Drain on paper towels.
Trim green beans. Blanch in boiling water 2 minutes. Drain. Plunge into ice water. Drain well.
In same pan, add 15ml vegetable oil. Add green beans. Stir-fry 5-7 minutes. Beans should blister and soften. Remove beans.

For sauce, combine mandarin juice (from 2 mandarins), mandarin zest (from 1 mandarin), chili garlic sauce, soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar, grated ginger, minced garlic, and chopped fermented black beans (if using) in a bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk 10g cornstarch with 30ml cold water to make a slurry.
Add sauce mixture to pan. Bring to a simmer. Stir in cornstarch slurry. Cook until sauce thickens.
Return crispy tofu and blistered green beans to pan. Toss to coat evenly with sauce. Stir in sesame oil.
Garnish with sliced scallions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Pasta Bruschetta Bites
recipes.visual_description: Toasted baguette rounds, golden-brown, are topped with a vibrant orzo pasta salad. Light beige orzo mixes with vivid red diced cherry tomatoes, small purple minced red onion, and stark white crumbled feta. Fresh green basil flecks dot the mixture. Each bite-sized canapé features crispy bread, tender pasta, juicy tomato, and soft cheese. A slight olive oil sheen adds luster. A thin, dark balsamic glaze drizzle provides elegant contrast. The canapés are arranged naturally on a rustic wooden board or simple white ceramic platter. It sits on a well-used wooden kitchen table, bathed in natural window light. A casually folded neutral linen napkin rests nearby. The setting is uncluttered, evoking a comfortable, lived-in kitchen. Approximately 10-12 pieces are artfully spaced on the platter.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a light white wine or sparkling water.
Best enjoyed fresh.
instructions: Cook orzo pasta according to package directions. Drain. Rinse with cold water. Drain well.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Slice baguette into 1.5 cm thick rounds.
Arrange bread slices on a baking tray. Toast 5-7 minutes until light golden. Let cool.
Dice cherry tomatoes into small cubes. Mince red onion very finely. Crumble feta cheese.
Chop fresh basil leaves.
In a bowl, combine cooked orzo, diced tomatoes, minced red onion, crumbled feta, and chopped basil.
Drizzle with olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss gently to combine.
Spoon the pasta mixture onto each toasted baguette slice.
Arrange canapés on a serving platter. Drizzle with balsamic glaze if desired. Serve immediately.
notes: These canapés are best assembled just before serving to maintain bread crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Manzo Brasato con Pappardelle al Vino Rosso
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a round, matte white bone china plate, occupying the lower left quadrant with abundant negative space. A single, dark, richly caramelized braised beef cheek, approximately 8-10 cm in diameter, rests prominently. Its surface shows subtle char and deep mahogany tones. Adjacent to the beef, a refined swirl of golden-hued pappardelle pasta is artfully arranged. The pasta has a delicate sheen and a slightly irregular, handcrafted texture. A glossy, deep ruby-red wine reduction pools elegantly around the beef and pasta, creating an organic, flowing shape. The sauce reflects light softly, indicating its rich viscosity. A single, thin, delicate shaving of ivory Parmigiano-Reggiano curls gently atop the beef. A few vibrant green micro basil leaves are precisely placed on the pasta, providing a sharp color contrast. The setting features a grey veined marble surface with dramatic, soft professional lighting creating subtle shadows. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, and elegant silver flatware are positioned to the right of the plate. The background is ultra-minimalist, emphasizing the dish's sophisticated simplicity.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of the same full-bodied red wine used in the braise, such as Barolo or Brunello.
Offer crusty artisanal bread for soaking up the rich sauce.
instructions: Pat beef cheeks dry. Season generously with sea salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over high heat. Sear beef cheeks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced carrot, celery, and onion (mirepoix) to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Deglaze the pot with red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a simmer.
Return beef cheeks to the pot. Add beef stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot tightly. Transfer to a preheated oven at 150°C. Braise for 3.5 to 4 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
While beef braises, prepare fresh pappardelle. On a clean surface, make a well with 00 flour. Crack eggs into the well. Slowly incorporate flour into eggs until a dough forms.
Knead dough for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Wrap in cling film. Rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Roll dough thinly using a pasta machine or rolling pin. Dust with semolina flour as needed. Cut into 2.5 cm wide pappardelle strips.
Once beef is tender, remove from oven. Carefully remove beef cheeks from the pot. Strain the braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan. Discard solids.

Skim any excess fat from the braising liquid. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Reduce until the sauce is glossy and coats the back of a spoon. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Whisk in butter until emulsified.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Cook fresh pappardelle for 2-3 minutes, or until al dente.
Drain pasta. Gently toss pasta with a small amount of the reduced red wine jus.

To plate, place a small, elegant swirl of sauced pappardelle slightly off-center on a pristine white plate. Carefully place one whole braised beef cheek beside the pasta. Spoon a generous amount of the rich, glossy red wine jus over the beef and around the plate, allowing it to pool artistically.
Garnish with a single delicate shaving of Parmigiano-Reggiano atop the beef and a few micro basil leaves placed precisely near the pasta.
notes: For best results, braise beef cheeks the day before; flavors deepen overnight. Reheat gently.
The quality of red wine significantly impacts the final jus flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Lamb Shoulder with Fermented Tomato-Olive Relish and Herb Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of braised lamb shoulder is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate. A mound of fluffy, pale green herb-infused rice sits to one side. The braised lamb, a rich, dark brown with tender muscle fibers, is a substantial, unsliced chunk, its natural form highlighted. A vibrant fermented tomato-olive relish cascades over the lamb, its bright red tomato pieces and dark olive fragments providing textural and color contrast. Fresh basil leaves add a pop of color. Ample white space emphasizes the natural beauty of each ingredient. The setting features a light, textured reclaimed wood table, an undyed linen napkin in natural beige, and soft, diffused natural light. The background is clean and minimalist with subtle blurred green foliage, maintaining an eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare fermented tomato-olive relish: Wash and roughly chop tomatoes. Pit and roughly chop olives. In a clean jar, combine chopped tomatoes, chopped olives, basil leaves. Dissolve 15g non-iodized salt in 500ml filtered water for brine. Pour brine over tomato-olive mixture, ensuring all solids are submerged. Seal jar with an airlock lid or burp daily. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess. Store in refrigerator.
Prepare lamb: Preheat oven to 160°C. Pat lamb shoulder dry. Season generously with sea salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear lamb shoulder on all sides until deeply browned. Remove lamb from pot.
Add chopped onion and minced garlic to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Deglaze with a splash of vegetable broth, scraping up browned bits.
Return lamb to the pot. Pour in remaining vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Cover pot tightly. Transfer to preheated oven. Braise for 2.5-3 hours, or until lamb is fork-tender.

Cook herb rice: Rinse rice until water runs clear. In a medium saucepan, combine rinsed rice with 600ml water. Add a pinch of salt and a few basil stems. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Remove basil stems. Fluff with a fork.
Rest lamb: Once braised, remove lamb from pot. Let rest for 10 minutes. The lamb will be in large, tender chunks. Do not slice.

To serve: Place a generous portion of herb rice on a plate. Place a large piece of braised lamb alongside the rice. Spoon fermented tomato-olive relish over and around the lamb. Garnish with a fresh basil leaf.
notes: For fermentation, ensure your jar is sterilized. Keep the solids submerged under the brine to prevent mold. A fermentation weight can be used.
This recipe embraces zero-waste by fermenting tomatoes, extending their shelf life and creating a flavorful condiment. Leftover lamb bones can be used for future broths.

recipes.recipe_name: Truffle-Chorizo Noir Bonbons
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine perfectly uniform miniature bonbons are arranged with architectural precision on a pristine white bone china rectangular platter. Each bonbon features a flawless, glossy dark chocolate shell. On the top of each bonbon, a small, precise dot of vibrant ruby-red chili gelee offers a striking color contrast. A delicate, dark brown chorizo praline dust is subtly sprinkled beside the gelee, adding a textural element and a hint of savory depth. The composition emphasizes abundant negative space, highlighting the minimalist elegance of each piece. The platter rests on a polished white Carrara marble surface. A crisp white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, is placed beside the platter. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the luxurious and refined aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled on an elegant serving platter as a post-meal digestif or with coffee.
Present alongside other delicate petit fours for a varied tasting experience.
instructions: Prepare the Chorizo Praline: Remove casing from chorizo. Finely dice chorizo. Render chorizo in a dry pan over medium heat until crispy. Drain fat. Add sugar to chorizo. Cook until sugar caramelizes and coats chorizo. Spread thinly on parchment paper. Cool completely. Once brittle, pulse in a food processor to a coarse praline dust. Set aside.

Prepare the Truffle Ganache: Heat cream in a small saucepan until just simmering. Remove from heat. Stir in truffle oil. Place 150g dark chocolate in a heatproof bowl. Pour hot cream over chocolate. Let stand 1 minute. Whisk gently from center outwards until smooth and emulsified. Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until firm, about 2 hours.

Prepare the Chili Gelee: Bloom gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 minutes. Heat 50ml water and hot sauce in a small saucepan until warm. Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Stir dissolved gelatin into warm hot sauce mixture until fully incorporated. Pour into a small, shallow container. Chill until set, about 1 hour. Once set, use a small spoon to break it into a fluid gel or pass through a fine sieve if preferred.

Prepare Chocolate Shells: Temper remaining 150g dark chocolate with cocoa butter. Melt chocolate and cocoa butter together to 45°C. Cool to 27°C, then reheat to 31-32°C. Fill clean polycarbonate bonbon molds with tempered chocolate. Tap molds to release air bubbles. Invert molds to drain excess chocolate, creating a thin shell. Scrape mold edges clean. Let shells set.

Assemble Bonbons: Pipe or spoon truffle ganache into each chocolate shell, filling about two-thirds. Place a small dot of chili gelee on top of the ganache in each shell. Sprinkle a small amount of chorizo praline dust over the gelee. Cap bonbons with remaining tempered chocolate. Scrape mold edges clean. Allow chocolate to crystallize and set completely, about 30 minutes. Demold carefully.
Serve 6-9 bonbons artfully arranged on a serving platter.
notes: Ensure chocolate is perfectly tempered for a shiny, stable shell.
Quality of truffle oil and hot sauce is crucial for flavor balance.

recipes.recipe_name: Lentil and Apple Warm Salad
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of warm brown lentils, simmered in savory beef stock, forms the base, showcasing their earthy, tender texture. They are tossed with crisp, uniformly diced red apple, vibrant pale green celery, and finely diced red onion, creating a colorful medley of reds, greens, and purples against the lentils' deep brown. A glossy, lightly emulsified vinaigrette, infused with a subtle kick of hot sauce, coats each component, adding a gentle sheen. The salad is casually mounded in a sturdy, off-white ceramic bowl, placed on a well-worn, light wooden kitchen table. A simple, folded linen napkin and a classic silver fork rest beside the bowl. The scene is bathed in warm, soft kitchen light, evoking a cozy, unpretentious home dining atmosphere.
instructions: Rinse brown lentils under cold water.
Combine rinsed lentils and beef stock in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until lentils are tender. Drain any excess liquid.
While lentils cook, finely dice the apples, red onion, and celery into small, uniform cubes.
Chop fresh parsley.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, apple cider vinegar, hot sauce, salt, and black pepper to create the dressing.
In a large serving bowl, combine the warm cooked lentils, diced apples, diced red onion, and diced celery.
Pour the dressing over the lentil mixture. Toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Maize & Noodle Textures with Umami Caramel
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of a sophisticated dessert is presented on an expensive bone china plate with a subtle, modern pattern, placed on a premium grey veined marble surface. The composition is artistic and minimalist, featuring abundant negative space. A smooth, pale yellow Sweet Corn Crémeux, sculpted into an elegant quenelle, occupies one side of the plate. Beside it, several irregular, golden-brown shards of Crispy Egg Noodle Tuile are delicately arranged, providing a stark textural contrast. A small, dark, glossy pool of Beef Umami Caramel is artfully drizzled, creating a rich, deep brown accent that contrasts with the crémeux's lightness. A few crystalline flakes of Maldon Sea Salt are precisely scattered over the crémeux and caramel, catching the light. The overall presentation is clean and architectural, with dramatic professional lighting creating subtle shadows. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, rests nearby. The background is ultra-minimalist and out of focus, emphasizing the dish's refined elegance.

ingredients.name: Beef Consommé, highly reduced and clarified

instructions: For the Sweet Corn Crémeux: Infuse corn kernels in heavy cream in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Remove from heat. Let steep 30 minutes. Blend mixture until very smooth. Strain through a fine mesh sieve, pressing solids. Discard solids.

Bloom gelatine leaf in cold water. In a bowl, whisk egg yolks and 50 g sugar until pale. Slowly whisk in warm corn cream. Return mixture to clean saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens and coats the back of a spoon (82°C). Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatine until dissolved. Pour crémeux into shallow dish. Cover surface with cling film. Chill minimum 4 hours, or until set.

For the Crispy Egg Noodle Tuile: Cook fine egg noodles in boiling water until al dente. Drain well. Rinse with cold water. Dry thoroughly on paper towels. Toss noodles with melted butter and remaining 50 g sugar.
Spread noodles thinly in a single layer on a baking tray lined with parchment paper. Bake at 160°C for 10-12 minutes, until golden brown and crisp. Break into irregular shards.

For the Beef Umami Caramel: In a small saucepan, combine highly reduced beef consommé, 50 g sugar, and sherry vinegar. Bring to a simmer. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until mixture reduces to a thick, glossy caramel consistency. It should coat a spoon. Be careful not to burn. Remove from heat.

To Plate: Spoon a generous quenelle or dollop of Sweet Corn Crémeux onto one side of a chilled dessert plate. Arrange a few Crispy Egg Noodle Tuile shards artfully beside the crémeux. Drizzle a small amount of Beef Umami Caramel over and around the crémeux and noodles. Finish with a delicate sprinkle of Maldon Sea Salt Flakes. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken in Red Wine Sauce with Parmesan
recipes.special_requests: 와인은 향신료로 사용해서 맛있는 치킨을 파마산 치즈와 함께 만들어줘. cuisine
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of tender chicken in a rich red wine sauce is presented centrally on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken thighs, kept as whole pieces, exhibit a deep golden-brown sear, contrasting with the glossy, deep reddish-brown sauce that generously coats them. The sauce has a smooth texture with subtle specks of herbs. A light sprinkle of freshly grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese melts softly over the chicken and sauce, adding a creamy visual element. Fresh, bright green chopped parsley is scattered as a final garnish, providing a pop of color and freshness. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware placed beside it, suggesting a modern bistro setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s inviting colors and textures, with a clean, understated background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to soak up the sauce.
Accompany with creamy polenta or simple buttered pasta.
Pair with a robust Italian red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until deeply golden brown on all sides. This takes about 4-5 minutes per side. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pan. Cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half, about 5 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Add rosemary and thyme sprigs. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.

Return seared chicken thighs to the pan. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in the sauce. Cover and simmer gently for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Remove rosemary and thyme sprigs. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and sauce is slightly thickened.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Using a good quality dry red wine will significantly enhance the sauce flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Chicken Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Classic Chicken Parmesan rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a rustic wooden table. The golden-brown, pan-fried chicken cutlet, approximately 1 cm thick, is generously covered with a vibrant red marinara sauce. Melted, bubbly fresh mozzarella and grated Parmesan cheese form a golden, gooey crust over the chicken. Scattered fresh green basil leaves provide a vivid color contrast. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, maintaining its crispy texture. The plate has moderate negative space, allowing the dish to stand out. A simple white linen napkin and a silver fork and knife are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors, with a subtly blurred background suggesting a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside a portion of spaghetti or penne pasta tossed with extra marinara sauce.
Offer a simple green salad with a light vinaigrette.
Provide crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.

ingredients.name: Fresh mozzarella cheese, sliced or shredded

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Lightly grease a baking dish.
Place each chicken breast between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound with a meat mallet to a uniform thickness of 1 cm (approx. 180g cutlets). Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Prepare a breading station: Place flour in a shallow dish. Whisk eggs in a second shallow dish. Place breadcrumbs in a third shallow dish.
Dredge each chicken cutlet in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg wash, allowing excess to drip off. Coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Fry chicken cutlets for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary.
Transfer fried chicken cutlets to the prepared baking dish.
Sauté minced garlic in the same skillet for 30 seconds until fragrant. Pour in marinara sauce. Bring to a gentle simmer. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon a generous amount of marinara sauce over each chicken cutlet. Top with fresh mozzarella slices/shreds and grated Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly, and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C. The breading should be golden brown.
Remove from oven. Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Pounding the chicken to an even thickness ensures uniform cooking and tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Berry & Chocolate Parfait
recipes.visual_description: The dessert is presented in clear glass tumblers, showcasing elegant layers. At the base, coarsely crushed biscuits form a rustic, light brown layer. Above this, a vibrant crimson layer of macerated seasonal berries, with diced strawberry pieces visible, offers a soft, natural texture. A smooth, creamy white layer of vanilla-infused yogurt follows, contrasting softly with the fruit. Dark chocolate shavings are generously sprinkled over the yogurt, adding deep brown accents. The layers are repeated, creating an appealing visual depth. The top is crowned with more chocolate shavings and a few whole, perfectly ripe berries, alongside a fresh sprig of bright green mint. The entire composition sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the dessert's natural colors and textures against a clean, minimalist background with subtle botanical elements, emphasizing sustainable beauty.

ingredients.name: Natural sweetener (maple syrup or date syrup)

instructions: Prepare berries: Wash and hull berries. Dice larger strawberries. Combine berries with natural sweetener, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt. Gently mix. Let macerate for 30 minutes.
Crush biscuits: Place biscuits in a bag. Crush coarsely using a rolling pin.
Prepare yogurt: In a bowl, combine yogurt or kefir with vanilla extract. Mix well.
Grate chocolate: Grate dark chocolate into shavings or small pieces.
Assemble parfaits: In four clear glass tumblers, layer components. Start with a spoonful of crushed biscuits.
Add berry layer: Top biscuits with a generous spoon of macerated berries.
Add yogurt layer: Follow with a layer of vanilla yogurt.
Add chocolate: Sprinkle with grated chocolate.
Repeat layers: Continue layering until tumblers are full, ending with chocolate and a few whole berries or a mint sprig for garnish.
Serve immediately or chill briefly.
notes: For zero-waste, use stale biscuits or make homemade biscuits from leftover flour scraps.
For deeper fermentation, berries can be lacto-fermented for 1-2 days in a light salt brine before macerating with sweetener.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Lamb and Tomato Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Rustic Lamb and Tomato Rice is presented on a simple, well-worn, off-white ceramic plate with a slightly uneven rim. The dish forms a natural, slightly mounded shape in the center of the plate, allowing for ample negative space around the edges. Tender, braised lamb chunks, irregularly cut, are nestled within the moist, reddish-orange rice, which is infused with tomato and hints of olive oil. Visible are plump, dark black olives and small pieces of softened tomato. Fresh green basil leaves, torn or roughly chopped, are scattered generously over the top, adding vibrant color and a fresh aroma. The texture appears comforting and hearty. The plate rests on a warm, rustic wooden dining table, showing subtle signs of use. A simple, folded cream-colored linen napkin and a heavy, unpolished silver fork are placed casually beside the plate. Warm, inviting light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, casting soft shadows and highlighting the food's natural appeal. The background suggests a cozy, lived-in family kitchen, perhaps with a blurred hint of a spice rack or a wooden cutting board.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the pot at the family table.
Accompany with crusty bread for soaking up the juices.
A simple green salad with a lemon-oregano vinaigrette.
instructions: Pat lamb chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear lamb chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove lamb and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
If using, add red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine reduces by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, stock, and a pinch of sugar. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared lamb to the pot. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until lamb is very tender.

Stir in rice and pitted olives. Increase heat to medium-low. Cook, uncovered, stirring occasionally, for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Add more stock if rice is too dry.
Stir in most of the fresh basil, chopped.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Beef & Parmesan Crostini
recipes.visual_description: Homestyle Beef & Parmesan Crostini are presented on a rustic wooden board, arranged in a casual, slightly overlapping manner. Each toasted baguette slice forms a golden-brown, crisp base. Piled generously on top is a rich, savory mixture of well-browned ground beef, finely diced caramelized onions, and minced garlic, infused with aromatic fresh thyme. The beef mixture has a tender, moist texture, contrasting with the bread's crunch. A blanket of freshly grated Parmesan cheese, melted and slightly golden from a quick broil, tops each crostini, adding a salty, umami finish. Specks of vibrant green fresh thyme leaves are scattered over the top for a pop of color and fresh aroma. The overall aesthetic is one of inviting, unpretentious comfort food, ready for casual sharing. The dish is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, under warm, cozy kitchen lighting, embodying a relaxed family setting.
instructions: Slice baguette into 1.5 cm thick rounds. Arrange on a baking sheet.
Drizzle baguette slices with 15 ml olive oil. Toast in oven at 180°C for 5-7 minutes until lightly golden. Set aside.
Dice onion finely. Mince garlic. Remove thyme leaves from stems and chop finely.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add ground beef. Cook, breaking it apart with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion to the skillet with the beef. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Stir in minced garlic and chopped thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Season beef mixture with salt and black pepper to taste.
Spoon beef mixture generously onto each toasted baguette slice.
Grate Parmesan cheese over each crostini.
Return crostini to the baking sheet. Broil for 2-3 minutes, watching closely, until cheese is melted and lightly golden.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Corn and Scallop Salad with Garlic Confit and Lemon-Chive Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented with sophisticated minimalism on a matte white or light grey designer ceramic plate, resting on a pristine white Carrara marble surface. Abundant negative space highlights the intentional composition. A delicate, elongated smear of pale yellow garlic confit puree anchors the arrangement. Beside it, a cluster of golden-charred corn kernels creates textural contrast. Three perfectly seared, caramelized scallops, with their creamy white interiors visible, are artfully positioned amongst the corn. A shimmering, light green lemon-chive vinaigrette is elegantly drizzled over the components. A few precise sprigs of vibrant green micro arugula provide a final, delicate garnish. The scene is lit with dramatic, focused lighting, casting soft shadows that enhance the dish's sculptural quality. A precisely folded white linen napkin sits beside the plate, completing the ultra-minimalist, high-end dining presentation.
instructions: Prepare Garlic Confit: Place peeled garlic cloves in a small saucepan. Cover with 100 ml olive oil. Cook over very low heat for 30-40 minutes until garlic is very tender and golden. Do not brown. Strain garlic, reserving oil. Mash garlic cloves into a smooth puree.

Prepare Corn: Carefully slice corn kernels off the cobs. Heat a large non-stick pan over high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add corn kernels in a single layer. Sear for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until kernels are charred and tender-crisp. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

Prepare Lemon-Chive Vinaigrette: In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice, white wine vinegar, and Dijon mustard. Slowly drizzle in 30 ml of the reserved garlic confit oil while whisking constantly to emulsify. Stir in finely chopped chives. Season with salt and pepper.

Sear Scallops: Pat scallops very dry with paper towels. Season with salt and pepper. Heat a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat with a thin layer of olive oil until shimmering. Place scallops in the hot pan, ensuring not to overcrowd. Sear for 2 minutes per side until deeply golden-brown and caramelized. Do not overcook.

Assemble Salad: On each plate, create a small, artistic smear or dot of garlic confit puree. Artfully scatter the seared corn kernels beside or over the puree. Arrange 3 seared scallops thoughtfully among the corn. Drizzle the lemon-chive vinaigrette over the salad components. Garnish sparingly with a few sprigs of micro arugula.

recipes.recipe_name: Uzbek-Style Beef and Vegetable Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty Uzbek-style beef and vegetable stew is presented in a rustic, dark-glazed ceramic bowl, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The stew features generous chunks of tender, braised beef with a rich, glossy, deep reddish-brown sauce. Large, earthy pieces of potato, vibrant orange carrot rounds, and bright green bell pepper pieces are nestled alongside the beef. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of freshly chopped green dill, adding a fresh contrast. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with components touching and overlapping. A traditional, simple wooden spoon rests next to the bowl. The scene is bathed in warm, natural kitchen light, conveying a homely, lived-in family atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh Uzbek non (flatbread) for dipping into the rich sauce.
Accompany with a simple 'Achichuk' (Uzbek tomato and onion salad) to add a refreshing counterpoint.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 3 medium, peeled, cut into thick rounds

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 2-3 medium, peeled, cut into large chunks

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef and set aside.
Add chopped onions to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly browned, about 8 minutes.
Stir in granulated sugar. Cook for 2 more minutes, allowing onions to caramelize slightly.
Add minced garlic, crushed cumin seeds, and crushed coriander seeds to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to loosen any browned bits. Bring to a simmer.
Cook for 5 minutes to reduce the wine slightly.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add beef broth. Bring the liquid back to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot tightly. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 1.5 hours, stirring occasionally.
Add carrot rounds, potato chunks, and bell pepper pieces to the pot. Stir well to combine.
Continue simmering, covered, for another 45-60 minutes, or until beef and vegetables are fork-tender.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot in individual bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or dill.
notes: While red wine is not a traditional ingredient in Uzbek cuisine, it is incorporated here as per ingredient requirements to create a rich, savory braise. The use of cumin, coriander, and hearty vegetables aims to evoke an 'Uzbek style' flavor profile.
traditional_techniques: Building a flavor base with caramelized onions and toasted spices

recipes.recipe_name: Coffee-Rubbed Pork Tenderloin with Mango Salsa and Brown Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Coffee-Rubbed Pork Tenderloin with Mango Salsa and Brown Rice is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The plate sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. On one side of the plate, a neat mound of fluffy, earthy brown rice is visible. Adjacent to the rice, several thick, succulent medallions of pork tenderloin are arranged. The pork boasts a deep, rich, seared crust with hints of the dark coffee rub, revealing a tender, juicy interior. Generously spooned over the pork and spilling onto the plate is a vibrant mango salsa, showcasing small, bright orange mango cubes, finely diced red onion, and verdant chopped cilantro. The salsa provides a striking color contrast against the dark pork and brown rice. A few fresh cilantro leaves are scattered artistically as a garnish. The overall composition is balanced, clean, and inviting, with appropriate negative space around the food. A folded white cotton napkin is placed neatly beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating soft shadows and highlighting the fresh textures and colors of the dish. The background is minimal and unobtrusive, focusing entirely on the plated meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cook brown rice: Combine 250 grams brown rice with 500 ml water or broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork.

Prepare coffee rub: In a small bowl, combine 2 tablespoons finely ground coffee, 1 tablespoon brown sugar, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, 0.5 teaspoon ground cumin, 0.5 teaspoon garlic powder, 1 teaspoon salt, and 0.5 teaspoon black pepper. Mix well.
Prepare pork tenderloin: Pat pork tenderloin dry. Rub the entire surface generously with the coffee spice mixture. Ensure even coating.

Sear pork: Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil and 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Once hot, sear the pork tenderloin on all sides until well browned, about 2-3 minutes per side. This creates a crust.

Finish pork in oven: Transfer the skillet with the pork to the preheated oven. Roast for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C. Remove from oven, transfer pork to a cutting board, and let rest for 5-10 minutes. This allows juices to redistribute.

Prepare mango salsa: While pork rests, dice 2 ripe mangoes into small cubes. Finely dice 1 small red onion. Coarsely chop 30 grams fresh cilantro. In a medium bowl, combine mango, red onion, and cilantro. Squeeze juice from 1 large lime over the mixture. Season with a pinch of salt. Gently toss to combine.
Slice pork: Slice the rested pork tenderloin into thick medallions, approximately 2-3 cm thick.

Plate: Place a portion of fluffy brown rice on a clean white porcelain plate. Arrange several thick pork medallions beside the rice. Spoon a generous amount of fresh mango salsa over and around the pork. Garnish with a few fresh cilantro leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Chocolate Mint Chili Hotteok
recipes.visual_description: A single warm, golden-brown Chocolate Mint Chili Hotteok rests on a simple, slightly off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections, positioned on a well-used wooden dining table. The Hotteok is round and slightly flattened, with a subtly crispy, golden exterior. Its surface shows faint, irregular patterns from pan-frying. The edges are gently puffed. A small tear in the crust, or a section where the dough is thinner, reveals the molten, dark chocolate filling, speckled with vibrant green flecks of finely chopped mint. The chocolate is glossy and soft, oozing slightly. The overall color palette is warm browns, deep greens, and dark chocolate. A few stray, fresh mint leaves are casually placed beside the Hotteok. The setting is a cozy, lived-in family kitchen, with warm light from an overhead fixture. A simple, folded cloth napkin is nearby. The portion is generous and comforting, inviting immediate enjoyment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot to enjoy the melted filling.
Can be served with a small glass of milk or a cup of warm tea.
Often eaten by hand as a street food or snack.
instructions: Combine flour, yeast, sugar, and salt in a large bowl.
Gradually add warm water. Mix until a soft, shaggy dough forms.
Knead dough on a lightly floured surface for 5 minutes. Dough should be smooth and elastic.
Place dough in a lightly oiled bowl. Cover with plastic wrap. Let rise in a warm place for 1 hour, or until doubled in size.
While dough rises, prepare filling. In a small bowl, combine chopped dark chocolate, finely chopped fresh mint leaves, granulated sugar, and gochugaru. Mix well.
Punch down risen dough. Divide into 4 equal portions.
Flatten each dough portion into a disc. Place a generous spoonful of filling in the center.
Gather dough edges around the filling. Pinch tightly to seal. Ensure no filling leaks.
Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-low heat.
Place 2 Hotteok, seam-side down, in the pan. Cook for 1 minute.
Flip Hotteok. Using a spatula or Hotteok press, flatten each Hotteok gently. Cook for 2-3 minutes until golden brown.
Flip again. Cook for another 2-3 minutes until both sides are deeply golden and crispy. Repeat with remaining Hotteok, adding more oil as needed.
Serve Hotteok immediately while hot.
notes: Adjust gochugaru quantity to your preferred spice level. A small amount provides a subtle warmth without overwhelming the mint and chocolate.
Ensure the dough is well-sealed around the filling to prevent leaks during cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Tinga with Chipotle and Tomato
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of shredded pork tinga is centrally plated in a shallow, rustic white ceramic bowl. The pork, cooked until fork-tender, is thoroughly coated in a vibrant, reddish-brown chipotle-tomato sauce, showcasing its rich, rustic texture. Visible are small, soft pieces of caramelized onion and flecks of dark red chipotle. A sprinkle of fresh, roughly chopped cilantro leaves adds a pop of bright green. Beside the tinga, a small mound of crumbled white queso fresco provides contrasting texture and color. A few thin slices of creamy green avocado are neatly arranged to one side. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded beige linen napkin and a small stack of warm corn tortillas are placed to the side, enhancing the casual bistro setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and authentic appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with warm corn tortillas for making tacos.
Offer additional garnishes like Mexican crema or pickled red onions.
Accompany with a side of refried beans or Mexican rice.
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into large chunks. Place pork in a large pot. Cover with water. Add 1 halved onion and 1 bay leaf.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer for 1.5-2 hours, until pork is fork-tender. Skim any foam.
Remove pork from pot. Reserve 250 ml of cooking broth. Shred pork into coarse strands using two forks. Set aside.
Dice the remaining onion into small cubes. Mince garlic.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

While onion cooks, blend Roma tomatoes, chipotle chilies (remove seeds for less heat if desired), remaining bay leaf, Mexican oregano, and ground cumin with 125 ml of the reserved pork broth until smooth.
Pour the blended sauce into the skillet with the sautéed onion and garlic. Bring to a simmer.
Add the shredded pork to the sauce. Add remaining 125 ml reserved broth. Stir well to combine. Season with salt and pepper.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and flavors meld. Ensure pork internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) if reheating.
Remove bay leaf before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Beef Shepherd's Pie with Cheesy Potato Topping
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Classic Beef Shepherd's Pie is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, showcasing its comforting, homemade appeal. The top layer of mashed potato is golden-brown and lightly crusted, with visible ridges from a fork, indicating its freshly baked quality. Melted, bubbly cheddar cheese forms inviting patches across the potato surface. Below the potato, the rich, savory beef mince filling, studded with diced carrots and bright green peas, peeks out from the edges where the potato topping meets the bowl. The beef is dark brown, reflecting slow simmering. The overall plating is natural and unpretentious, as if served directly from a family meal. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, soft kitchen lighting. A simple, everyday fork rests casually beside the bowl. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a lived-in kitchen environment, enhancing the homely, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread for dipping.
Often accompanied by a simple green salad.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Peel and dice onion and carrots. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add beef mince. Cook, breaking it apart, until browned. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion, diced carrots, and minced garlic to the skillet. Cook until vegetables soften, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and dried thyme. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in beef broth and Worcestershire sauce. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 10-15 minutes, until sauce thickens slightly.
Stir in frozen peas. Remove from heat.
While beef simmers, peel potatoes. Cut into large chunks. Place in a large pot. Cover with cold salted water.
Bring to a boil. Cook until potatoes are very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes thoroughly. Return to the hot pot.
Add milk, butter, and half of the shredded cheddar cheese to the potatoes. Mash until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour the beef mixture into a 2-liter baking dish or leave in the oven-safe skillet.
Spoon the mashed potato topping evenly over the beef mixture. Use a fork to create ridges.
Sprinkle remaining cheddar cheese over the mashed potato.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and the filling is bubbling. Let stand 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Irish Stout Beef with Creamy Cheddar Polenta
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of hearty Irish Stout Beef with Creamy Cheddar Polenta is presented in a clean white porcelain shallow bowl. The braised beef chunks, cut into 3-4cm pieces, are tender and dark brown, nestled among rustic 2cm chunks of tender, bright orange carrots, softened celery, and quartered mushrooms. The rich, deep brown stout gravy coats the ingredients. A generous dollop of creamy, golden-yellow cheddar polenta, with a smooth, slightly flowing texture, is placed beside the stew, creating a pleasing contrast. The dish is garnished simply with vibrant green chopped fresh parsley. The overall composition is balanced, showcasing the natural colors and textures. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the food. A small slice of crusty Irish soda bread rests on a separate small plate nearby, adding to the cultural authenticity. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere, ensuring the dish remains the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm, crusty Irish soda bread to soak up the rich gravy.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 3, peeled and cut into 2 cm chunks

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper. Dredge beef in plain flour, shaking off excess.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove seared beef and set aside.
Add chopped onions, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and quartered mushrooms. Cook for another 5 minutes until mushrooms soften.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the dark stout beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half.

Return seared beef to the pot. Add beef stock, fresh thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 2-2.5 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.

While stew simmers, prepare the polenta. In a separate saucepan, bring chicken or vegetable stock and milk to a boil. Gradually whisk in the instant polenta. Reduce heat to low and cook, stirring constantly, for 5-7 minutes, until thickened and creamy. Remove from heat.
Stir butter and grated cheddar cheese into the polenta until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaves from the stew. Adjust seasoning if needed.

Ladle the Irish stout beef stew into individual serving bowls. Spoon a generous portion of creamy cheddar polenta alongside or on top of the stew. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Cheek Velouté with Potato Espuma and Red Wine Gastrique
recipes.visual_description: A single, individual portion of Braised Beef Cheek Velouté is presented in a wide, matte black ceramic bowl, showcasing abundant negative space. The rich, dark mahogany velouté forms the base, filling about one-third of the bowl, its velvety texture apparent. A few small, tender chunks of braised beef cheek are meticulously placed off-center within the soup. Beside the beef, a delicate cloud of bright white potato espuma is piped, offering a soft contrast. A few precise, glistening drops of deep ruby-red red wine gastrique are strategically placed on the velouté. A subtle drizzle of vibrant green chive oil encircles the beef and espuma. A few miniature sprigs of fresh microgreens are precisely placed atop the espuma for a final touch of color and freshness. The bowl rests on a premium grey-veined Carrara marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, is positioned beside the bowl. The scene is lit with dramatic professional lighting, casting soft, intentional shadows, set against an ultra-minimalist background to emphasize the dish's sophisticated simplicity.
instructions: Pat beef cheeks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Sear beef cheeks in a large Dutch oven with a little oil until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Add diced carrots, onion, and celery to the Dutch oven. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add smashed garlic, thyme, and bay leaf. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pot with red wine, scraping up any browned bits. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half.

Return beef cheeks to the pot. Pour in beef stock until beef is mostly submerged. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover and transfer to a preheated oven at 150°C (300°F). Braise for 3-4 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove beef cheeks from the braising liquid. Strain the liquid through a fine-mesh sieve, discarding solids. Skim any excess fat. Reserve the braising liquid.
Shred 200g of the braised beef cheek into small, tender chunks. Set aside. Take the remaining beef and blend it with 200ml of the braising liquid until smooth. This is your beef velouté base.
For the potato espuma: Peel and dice potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Boil until very tender. Drain well. Pass potatoes through a ricer or food mill into a clean pot.

Heat milk and 20g butter until warm. Add to riced potatoes. Season with salt. Whisk vigorously until smooth and airy. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Transfer to a culinary siphon. Charge with N2O cartridge.

For the red wine gastrique: In a small saucepan, combine sugar and 20ml water. Cook over medium heat until sugar dissolves and turns light amber. Carefully add red wine vinegar and the remaining 300ml of braising liquid. Bring to a simmer and reduce until syrupy, coating the back of a spoon. Adjust sweetness/acidity if needed. Keep warm.
For chive oil: Blend chives with neutral oil until vibrant green and smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth for a clear oil. Season with a pinch of salt.
Gently reheat the beef velouté base. Adjust seasoning. Ladle the velouté into warm serving bowls. Arrange the reserved braised beef chunks artfully in the soup.
Pipe a delicate cloud of potato espuma beside the beef. Drizzle red wine gastrique precisely over the velouté. Garnish with a few drops of chive oil and delicate microgreens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Lime Crémeux, Cranberry Fluid Gel, Coconut Vinegar Meringue
recipes.visual_description: The dessert is elegantly presented on a pristine, minimalist white bone china plate. A generous, organic quenelle of the vibrant, pale green Lime Cordial Crémeux forms the central anchor. Adjacent, a delicate, irregular shard of crisp Coconut Vinegar Meringue stands artfully. A contrasting pool of ruby-red Cranberry Fluid Gel is delicately spooned beside the crémeux, creating a natural, flowing shape. A single, golden-brown Toasted Coconut Tuile is carefully placed, leaning against the crémeux, providing textural height. The arrangement emphasizes negative space, allowing each element to shine. Colors are bright and clean: verdant green, deep red, pure white, and golden brown. Textures are a sophisticated interplay of creamy, crisp, and fluid. The overall presentation is architectural yet organic, showcasing precision and restraint. A subtle dusting of micro lime zest garnishes the crémeux. The setting features a premium marble surface and dramatic professional lighting with shadows.
instructions: For the Coconut Vinegar Meringue: Preheat oven to 90°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Whip egg whites to soft peaks. Gradually add caster sugar, whipping until stiff, glossy peaks form. Fold in coconut vinegar. Pipe or spread meringue thinly onto prepared sheet. Bake 1.5-2 hours, or until crisp and dry. Turn off oven, let cool completely inside.

For the Lime Cordial Crémeux: Bloom gelatin leaf in cold water. In a saucepan, whisk lime cordial, fresh lime juice, lime zest, egg yolks, whole egg, and 80g caster sugar. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens and coats the back of a spoon (82°C). Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved. Add cold diced butter, emulsifying with an immersion blender until smooth and glossy. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Chill until set, at least 4 hours.

For the Cranberry Fluid Gel: In a small saucepan, combine cranberry juice, agar-agar, and 20g caster sugar. Bring to a boil, whisking constantly for 1 minute. Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until firm. Once firm, transfer to a blender and blend until completely smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultra-smooth texture. Store in a squeeze bottle or airtight container.

For the Toasted Coconut Tuile: Preheat oven to 160°C. In a bowl, combine desiccated coconut, 30g caster sugar, and flour. Stir in melted butter and 1 egg white until a paste forms. Spread very thin layers onto a silicone mat or parchment paper. Bake 8-12 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Cool on a wire rack. Break into irregular shards.

To Assemble: Spoon a generous, organic quenelle of Lime Cordial Crémeux onto a minimalist white bone china plate. Delicately spoon a pool of Cranberry Fluid Gel beside the crémeux, creating a natural, flowing shape. Place an irregular shard of Coconut Vinegar Meringue artfully next to the crémeux. Lean a single Toasted Coconut Tuile against the crémeux. Garnish with a very fine dusting of lime zest over the crémeux. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Herb-Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Rustic Herb-Roasted Chicken and Potatoes is presented on a simple, off-white ceramic plate, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The plate holds one golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, its skin slightly crispy. Alongside are several irregular, golden-edged potato wedges and a few tender, caramelized onion wedges. Whole roasted garlic cloves and sprigs of fresh rosemary and thyme are nestled among the components. The food is arranged naturally, with components touching, reflecting a homely, unpretentious style. Colors are warm and earthy: deep golden-browns from the chicken and potatoes, soft amber from the onions, and vibrant green from the herbs. The scene is lit with warm, cozy light, evoking a relaxed family dining atmosphere. A simple cloth napkin is casually placed nearby.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2cm thick wedges. Peel and cut onions into 2cm thick wedges. Peel garlic cloves. Leave whole or lightly crush.
In a large roasting pan, combine chicken thighs, potato wedges, onion wedges, garlic cloves, rosemary sprigs, and thyme sprigs.
Drizzle with olive oil. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Toss all ingredients to coat evenly.
Arrange in a single layer in the roasting pan. Ensure chicken skin faces up.
Roast for 40-50 minutes. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C. Potatoes should be tender and golden brown. Onions should be caramelized.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Poached Chicken Consommé Gelée Bites with Crispy Noodles & Brioche
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a modern, matte white ceramic rectangular platter. Abundant negative space surrounds a meticulously arranged cluster of elegant bites. Each bite features a small, perfectly diced piece of poached chicken breast, precisely 1 cm cubes, nestled atop a translucent, shimmering cube of golden chicken consommé gelée. The gelée, approximately 2x2x1.5 cm, catches the light. Adorning each gelée cube is a delicate, airy nest of crispy fried rice vermicelli, offering a stark textural contrast. Alongside, a few ultra-thin, irregularly shaped shards of toasted brioche tuile are artfully placed, some slightly overlapping the gelée, providing a rich, buttery counterpoint. A few tiny, vibrant green micro celery leaves are strategically scattered for a fresh pop of color and subtle aromatic lift. The overall composition is minimalist, architectural, and precise, with a focus on contrasting textures and refined forms. The lighting is dramatic, casting soft shadows that enhance the sculptural quality of the elements. The background is an ultra-minimalist grey stone surface.
instructions: Prepare Chicken Stock for Consommé: Roast chicken bones and wings at 200°C for 30 minutes until golden. Transfer to a large pot. Add mirepoix and 2 litres cold water. Bring to a simmer. Skim impurities. Simmer gently for 3 hours. Strain stock through a fine-mesh sieve. Chill completely.

Clarify Consommé: Degrease chilled stock. In a separate bowl, whisk egg whites with ground chicken. Slowly whisk this mixture into the cold stock. Heat slowly, stirring occasionally, until raft forms. Do not stir once raft forms. Simmer gently for 30 minutes. Carefully ladle clear consommé through a cheesecloth-lined sieve. Season with salt.

Set Consommé Gelée: Heat 500 ml of clarified consommé. Whisk in agar-agar powder until dissolved. Bring to a boil for 1 minute. Pour into a shallow, flat dish to a depth of 1.5 cm. Chill until firm. Once set, cut into 2x2x1.5 cm cubes. Keep chilled.

Poach Chicken Breast: Place chicken breasts in a small pot. Add salt, white peppercorns, and bay leaf. Cover with cold water. Bring to a very gentle simmer. Immediately reduce heat to lowest setting. Poach for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Let cool slightly. Dice chicken into 1 cm cubes.

Prepare Crispy Noodles: Heat neutral oil in a small pot to 180°C. Break vermicelli into small pieces. Fry small batches for a few seconds until puffed and crispy. Remove with slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels.
Make Brioche Tuiles: Preheat oven to 160°C. Thinly slice brioche bread. Brush lightly with melted butter. Bake for 8-10 minutes until golden and crisp. Break into irregular, delicate shards.

Assemble Bites: On a serving platter, artfully arrange the consommé gelée cubes. Top each gelée cube with a diced chicken piece. Place a small nest of crispy noodles on top or alongside the chicken. Arrange a few brioche tuile shards around the bites. Garnish with micro celery leaves or finely chopped chives. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Parmesan Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Chicken and Parmesan Rigatoni is centrally plated on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. Thick medallions of pan-seared chicken breast, with a golden-brown crust, are nestled among al dente rigatoni pasta. The pasta is coated in a rich, velvety cream sauce, infused with bright green wilted spinach leaves. Specks of grated Parmesan cheese are visible throughout the sauce, which clings beautifully to the ridged pasta. A light scattering of vibrant fresh chopped parsley provides a final touch of color and freshness. The dish exhibits natural, appealing colors: the golden chicken, creamy white sauce, deep green spinach, and light tan pasta. The presentation is organized but not rigid, allowing for a natural flow of ingredients. There is ample negative space on the plate, highlighting the dish. The plate rests on a simple, light-toned wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. A folded, crisp white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting from the side, creating subtle shadows that add depth without obscuring details. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere without distraction.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad.
Offer freshly grated Parmesan at the table.
instructions: Cook rigatoni according to package directions. Reserve 125 ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Internal temperature 75°C. Remove chicken. Let rest 5 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add spinach. Cook until wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and sauce thickens.
Add cooked rigatoni and reserved pasta water to the sauce. Toss to coat.
Slice rested chicken breasts into thick medallions. Add to pasta. Toss gently.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for food safety.
Adjust sauce consistency with more pasta water if needed.
traditional_techniques: Deglazing the pan for flavor base
