recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tomato Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Tomato Chicken Pasta is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table. The penne pasta is coated in a luscious, creamy reddish-orange tomato sauce, forming a gently mounded pile. Nestled within and atop the pasta are several golden-brown, seared chicken medallions, cut into thick, substantial chunks, showcasing their tender interior. The dish is garnished with vibrant green chopped fresh parsley, providing a fresh contrast. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with moderate negative space around the food. A standard silver fork and knife rest beside the plate on a white cotton napkin. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a casual yet refined bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with standard flatware.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside. Let rest 5 minutes.
Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 100 ml pasta water.
Dice onion. Mince garlic. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Sauté diced onion 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in heavy cream and American cheese slices until cheese is fully melted and sauce is smooth.
Add cooked pasta to the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually until desired consistency is reached.
Slice rested chicken breasts into thick medallions or substantial chunks.
Serve pasta onto plates. Arrange chicken medallions on top of the pasta. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Short Rib, Silken Potato, Parmesan Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A perfectly formed, dark brown chunk of slow-braised beef short rib anchors the plate, its surface glistening. Beside it, a precisely piped quenelle of pale, silken pomme purée offers a smooth, creamy contrast. A delicate, golden Parmesan crisp leans artfully against the beef, adding a refined textural element. A rich, glossy pool of concentrated beef jus elegantly embraces the components, enhancing their deep hues. The plate is pristine white bone china, presenting a single, refined portion with abundant negative space. The setting is a luxury dining table with a grey-veined marble surface, complemented by a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. Dramatic, focused lighting creates subtle shadows, highlighting the dish's architectural precision and sophisticated simplicity.
instructions: Pat beef short ribs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear short ribs on all sides until deeply browned. Remove and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze with red wine, scraping up browned bits. Reduce by half.
Return short ribs to the pot. Add beef stock, thyme, and bay leaf. Liquid should mostly cover the ribs. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the pot tightly. Braise in a preheated oven at 150°C for 3-4 hours, or until fork-tender.
Remove short ribs from liquid. Strain braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids.
Reduce strained liquid over medium-high heat until it forms a rich, glossy jus. Season to taste.
For pomme purée: Peel and cut potatoes into uniform 2 cm chunks. Place in a pot, cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil, then simmer until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes completely. Return to the hot pot over low heat for 1-2 minutes to dry them out.
Pass potatoes through a ricer or fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl.

Warm milk and cream gently. Gradually whisk in 100g cold cubed butter into the riced potatoes until fully incorporated and smooth. Slowly whisk in warm milk and cream until silky. Season with salt. Keep warm.
For Parmesan crisps: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Finely grate Parmesan cheese.
Spoon small mounds (about 15g each) of grated Parmesan onto the sheet, spacing them apart.
Bake for 5-7 minutes, until golden brown and crispy. Let cool slightly on the sheet, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
To plate: Place one warm braised short rib chunk slightly off-center on a large, pristine white plate. Pipe a precisely formed quenelle or elegant swirl of silken pomme purée beside the short rib.
Carefully place one Parmesan crisp leaning against the short rib or purée. Spoon a generous pool of rich jus around the short rib.
Garnish with a few finely chopped fresh chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Carnitas with Creamy Esquites
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pork Carnitas with Creamy Esquites is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table. The focal point is a generous mound of golden-brown, rustic shredded pork carnitas, offering a crisp exterior and tender, juicy interior. Alongside, a vibrant serving of creamy esquites features charred yellow corn kernels mixed with crumbled white Cotija cheese, finely chopped green cilantro, and a rich, creamy sauce. The dish is garnished with fresh cilantro leaves scattered over the pork and esquites, and a bright lime wedge. A small stack of warm, soft corn tortillas is neatly placed beside the plate, ready for assembly. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for building tacos.
Offer additional lime wedges for fresh acidity.
Provide a side of salsa roja or green salsa.
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 5-7 cm chunks. Season generously with salt.
Heat a large Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium-high heat. Add 15 ml vegetable oil.
Sear pork chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove pork from pot.
Add quartered onion, smashed garlic, bay leaves, cumin, and oregano to the pot. Sauté for 2 minutes.
Return pork to the pot. Add orange halves, water or broth. Ensure pork is mostly submerged.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 3-4 hours. Pork should be fork-tender.
Remove pork from liquid. Shred pork into rustic chunks using two forks. Discard solids from braising liquid.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil. Add shredded pork.
Cook pork, stirring occasionally, until edges are crispy and golden-brown. Set aside.
For the esquites, heat a separate skillet over medium-high heat. Add corn kernels. Cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly charred, about 5-7 minutes.
In a medium bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, sour cream, lime juice, and chili powder.
Add charred corn, half of the chopped cilantro, and half of the crumbled Cotija cheese to the dressing. Stir to combine.
Warm corn tortillas according to package directions.
Serve crispy pork carnitas alongside creamy esquites. Garnish with remaining cilantro and Cotija cheese. Serve with warm tortillas and lime wedges.
notes: Ensure pork reaches an internal temperature of 63°C (145°F) for safe consumption, although braising will typically exceed this significantly for tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Baked Rigatoni with Artichokes and Cherry Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Creamy Baked Rigatoni with Artichokes and Cherry Tomatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The rigatoni is coated in a rich, creamy, light ivory sauce, with visible curds from the cottage cheese and golden-brown spots from baking. Quartered artichoke hearts are nestled throughout the pasta, displaying their pale green to light brown hues. Bright red halved cherry tomatoes add vibrant pops of color and slight acidity. Wilted dark green spinach leaves are interspersed, providing additional color and texture. The top of the dish is lightly golden and bubbly from the baked Parmesan cheese. A generous sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped basil leaves garnishes the top, adding a fresh aroma and visual appeal. The pasta is arranged in a natural, slightly mounded portion, showcasing its comforting texture. The plate is set on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, with a folded natural cotton napkin placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, with a softly blurred, casual bistro background.

ingredients.name: Artichoke hearts (canned or jarred, quartered, drained)

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 125 ml pasta water.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in quartered artichoke hearts and halved cherry tomatoes. Cook 3 minutes.
Add fresh spinach. Cook until wilted, about 2 minutes.
In a blender, combine cottage cheese and vegetable broth until mostly smooth.
Pour cottage cheese mixture into the pan. Bring to a gentle simmer. Season with salt and pepper.
Add cooked rigatoni and 30 g grated Parmesan cheese to the pan. Stir well to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water as needed.
Transfer mixture to a 2.5-liter baking dish if not using an oven-safe pan.
Sprinkle remaining Parmesan cheese over the top.
Bake 20-25 minutes, or until bubbling and golden on top.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Garnish with chopped fresh basil before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Beef & Bell Pepper Hand Pies
recipes.visual_description: A collection of golden-brown, rustic Homestyle Beef & Bell Pepper Hand Pies are casually arranged on a well-used wooden dining table. The flaky puff pastry is visibly puffed and has a rich, inviting golden hue. Some hand pies may show a hint of the savory filling peeking from the edges, revealing the vibrant red and green diced bell peppers and browned ground beef. The pies are presented on a simple, slightly imperfect ceramic platter or a rustic wooden board, conveying a lived-in, comfortable kitchen atmosphere. A loosely folded, natural linen napkin rests beside the platter. The scene is bathed in warm, natural light, creating a cozy and inviting ambiance. The focus is entirely on the comforting, generously portioned hand pies, ready for casual family eating. There are no decorative garnishes, only a few stray, fresh parsley leaves scattered on the platter for a touch of natural green.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add ground beef. Break up with a spoon. Cook until browned. Drain excess fat.
Stir in minced garlic and diced bell peppers. Cook for 5-7 minutes, until peppers are slightly tender.
Season with salt and black pepper. Remove from heat. Let cool completely.
Once cool, stir in grated Parmesan cheese.
Roll out puff pastry sheets slightly on a lightly floured surface. Cut each sheet into 4 equal squares.
Spoon a generous amount of beef filling onto one half of each pastry square.
Fold the other half over the filling to create a rectangle. Press edges firmly to seal.
Use a fork to crimp the edges, ensuring a tight seal.
Beat the egg with 15 ml water for an egg wash.
Brush the tops of the hand pies with egg wash.
Place pies on the prepared baking tray.
Bake for 18-22 minutes, or until golden brown and puffed.
Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Chocolate Raspberry Coffee Tartlets
recipes.visual_description: A single Chocolate Raspberry Coffee Tartlet rests on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with a rustic feel. The 10 cm tartlet, slightly off-center, features a crisp, golden-brown shortcrust shell. Inside, a dark, glossy chocolate ganache base is perfectly set. A generous dollop of pale, fluffy coffee cream, showing soft peaks, is spooned over the ganache. Vibrant, plump fresh raspberries are artfully scattered on the cream, their deep red contrasting with the pale cream and dark chocolate. A light dusting of powdered sugar subtly covers parts of the raspberries and cream. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, revealing natural grain. A casually placed linen napkin and a simple dessert fork complete the homely setting. Warm, natural kitchen light illuminates the scene, highlighting the dessert's textures and colors, with a blurred background focusing solely on the tartlet.
instructions: Combine flour, sugar, and salt in a bowl. Add cold butter. Rub butter into flour mixture until it resembles breadcrumbs. Add egg yolk. Mix until dough forms. Add cold water if needed, one teaspoon at a time, until dough comes together. Do not overmix. Form into a disc, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.

Preheat oven to 180°C. Roll out dough to 3 mm thickness. Cut out four circles to fit 10 cm tartlet molds. Press dough into molds. Prick bottoms with a fork. Line with parchment paper, fill with baking beans. Bake for 15 minutes. Remove beans and parchment. Bake for another 5-7 minutes, until golden. Cool completely on a wire rack.
Heat cream in a small saucepan until simmering. Remove from heat. Add chopped chocolate. Let sit for 2 minutes. Stir until smooth and glossy.
In a cold bowl, whisk very cold cream, powdered sugar, and instant coffee powder until stiff peaks form.
Pour chocolate ganache into cooled tartlet shells, filling about halfway. Refrigerate for 15 minutes until set.

Pipe or spoon coffee cream over the set ganache. Arrange fresh raspberries artfully on top of the coffee cream. Lightly dust with powdered sugar. Grate a tiny bit of orange zest over if desired. Serve immediately or chill until serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Corn & Basil Cake with Savory Tuna Floss Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of a golden-yellow corn and basil cake is presented on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The cake slice reveals visible specks of green basil and embedded corn kernels, showcasing its moist, tender crumb. A glossy, translucent amber glaze, subtly glistening from toasted sesame oil, is drizzled over the top of the slice, pooling slightly at the base. Generously sprinkled over the glaze is a light brown, fluffy topping of finely flaked, slightly crisped yellowfin tuna, providing a contrasting texture. The plate is placed on a well-worn wooden dining table, reflecting warm, natural light. In the background, the rest of the round cake sits on a simple cooling rack, partially visible. A casually placed, light-colored cloth napkin and a simple fork complete the homely, lived-in scene, emphasizing comfort and approachability.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside small cups of unsweetened green tea or jasmine tea to balance the unique sweet and savory flavors.
Offer as a unique dessert or a creative tea-time snack.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 20 cm round cake pan.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate bowl, cream softened butter until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time until well combined.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients, alternating with milk. Mix until just combined.
Fold in fresh corn kernels and chopped basil.
Pour batter into prepared cake pan. Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let cake cool in pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
For the savory glaze, combine minced garlic, toasted sesame oil, soy sauce, powdered sugar, and water in a small saucepan.
Heat over low heat, stirring until sugar dissolves and mixture is smooth. Remove from heat.
For tuna topping, flake drained tuna finely with a fork. Optional: gently dry-toast flaked tuna in a dry pan over low heat for 5-7 minutes until slightly crisped, resembling floss.
Once cake is cooled, drizzle the savory glaze over the top.
Evenly sprinkle the flaked tuna over the glazed cake.
notes: For a more pronounced savory tuna flavor, you can gently dry-toast the flaked tuna until it becomes crispier, resembling tuna floss.
Adjust garlic amount in glaze to your preference; a small amount adds umami without overpowering the sweetness.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Grape-Lime Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A pan-seared salmon fillet, approximately 180g, sits prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The salmon features a crisp, golden-brown skin on top, contrasting with its moist, flaky pink interior. Beside the salmon, a vibrant mound of fresh grape-lime salsa is artfully arranged. The salsa is composed of halved red and green grapes, small diced red onion, and finely chopped fresh cilantro. The colors are bright and natural: deep pink salmon, translucent purple and green grapes, and hints of white onion and bright green cilantro. A light sheen from the olive oil on the salmon is visible. The plate has moderate negative space, ensuring the dish is the focal point without being overcrowded. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table surface, standard silver flatware placed neatly beside the plate, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating a professional yet approachable ambiance.
instructions: Pat salmon fillets dry. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Wash and halve all grapes.
Finely dice red onion.
Chop fresh cilantro.
In a bowl, combine halved grapes, diced red onion, and chopped cilantro.
Zest one lime into the grape mixture. Squeeze juice from both limes into the mixture. Add honey if desired. Mix gently. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Place salmon fillets skin-side down in the hot pan. Press gently to ensure even contact.
Sear for 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy and golden brown.
Flip salmon fillets. Cook for another 3-5 minutes, depending on thickness, until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove salmon from pan. Let rest for 2 minutes.
Spoon grape-lime salsa onto plates.
Place one salmon fillet on top of or beside the salsa. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Endive Salad with Caramelized Shallot Vinaigrette, Capellini, and Chèvre
recipes.visual_description: The Endive Salad is meticulously composed on a large, pristine white bone china plate, showcasing abundant negative space. Crisp, pale green Belgian endive leaves are artfully arranged as the base, creating an organic, flowing shape. Delicate al dente capellini pasta, lightly tossed in a rich, golden caramelized shallot and roasted garlic vinaigrette, is nestled amidst tender frisée lettuce. Crumbles of creamy white fresh chèvre and roughly chopped, toasted hazelnuts are precisely scattered for textural contrast. A subtle drizzle of the golden vinaigrette elegantly adorns the plate. Fresh chervil sprigs serve as a refined garnish. The plate rests on a superpremium wooden table, under dramatic professional lighting, with a pristine white linen napkin. The ultra-minimalist background emphasizes the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a sophisticated starter course.
Accompany with a thin slice of freshly baked baguette.
Pair with a crisp, dry white wine like Sauvignon Blanc or Sancerre.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Toss garlic cloves with 10ml olive oil. Roast until very soft and golden, about 20-25 minutes. Cool.
Finely slice shallots. Heat 10ml olive oil in a small pan over low heat. Add shallots. Cook slowly, stirring often, until deeply caramelized and sweet, about 25-30 minutes. Cool.
Break capellini into 3-4 cm pieces. Cook in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain well. Rinse with cold water to cool. Drain thoroughly again.

For the vinaigrette: Combine roasted garlic, caramelized shallots, sherry vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper in a blender. Slowly emulsify with 100ml extra virgin olive oil until smooth. Adjust seasoning.
Wash and dry endive leaves and frisée. Separate endive leaves. Tear frisée into bite-sized pieces.
Toast hazelnuts in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant and skins loosen. Rub in a clean towel to remove skins. Roughly chop.
In a large bowl, gently toss the cooled capellini with a small amount of the vinaigrette.
Arrange endive leaves artfully on four large plates. Place a small mound of dressed capellini and frisée in the center of each plate.
Crumble chèvre over the salad. Sprinkle with chopped hazelnuts.
Drizzle remaining vinaigrette around and over the salad. Garnish with fresh chervil sprigs.
notes: The vinaigrette can be made ahead and stored in the refrigerator. Bring to room temperature before serving.
Ensure all greens and pasta are thoroughly dried to allow the vinaigrette to adhere properly.

recipes.recipe_name: Cherry & Panang Cremeux, Kewra Spheres, Coconut Tuile
recipes.visual_description: The dessert is presented with ultra-minimalist elegance on a pristine, large, round white bone china plate with a subtle, delicate rim. The plate occupies the majority of the frame, emphasizing abundant negative space. In the center, a perfectly smooth, glossy quenelle of the pale, creamy Cherry Panang Cremeux is placed, its soft, inviting curve forming the dish's anchor. The cremeux has a subtle pinkish-red hue from the cherries, with an almost imperceptible hint of orange from the Panang, exuding a luxurious sheen. Adjacent to the cremeux, three or four Kewra Spheres (caviar) are meticulously placed, resembling glistening, translucent dewdrops. Their delicate, spherical forms catch the light, adding a touch of sophisticated whimsy and a promise of aromatic burst. A single, gracefully curved, golden-brown Coconut Tuile stands upright or leans artfully against the cremeux, providing a dramatic textural contrast and an architectural element. Its delicate, crisp texture is evident in its slightly irregular edges. Finally, two or three halves of Compressed Cherries are precisely positioned around the cremeux, their vibrant, deep ruby-red color intensified by the compression, appearing almost jewel-like. Their firm, slightly translucent flesh contrasts with the creamy cremeux. The overall composition is organic and flowing, avoiding any rigid symmetry or geometric patterns. The setting features a luxurious, light grey veined Carrara marble surface, reflecting subtle ambient light. A pristine white linen napkin, precisely folded into a sharp triangle, rests subtly in the lower corner. The lighting is dramatic and professional, casting soft, intentional shadows that add depth and dimension to the elements, highlighting their textures and forms. The background is utterly minimalist, allowing the dessert to command full attention, creating an atmosphere of refined culinary artistry.

ingredients.name: gelatin sheets (approx. 1 leaf), bloomed in cold water
cherry liqueur (optional, for flavor and compression)

instructions: Place pitted cherries in a small saucepan. Cook over medium heat until softened. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve to obtain 150 ml cherry puree. Discard solids.
In a heatproof bowl, whisk egg yolks and sugar until pale.
In a clean saucepan, heat cherry puree and Panang curry paste until simmering.
Slowly pour hot cherry mixture into egg yolk mixture, whisking constantly.
Return mixture to the saucepan. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly with a spatula, until thickened to a custard consistency (82-84°C). Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed and squeezed gelatin until dissolved.
Let cool slightly (to about 40°C). Gradually whisk in cold butter cubes until fully incorporated and smooth.
Pour cremeux into a shallow dish. Cover surface with plastic wrap. Chill for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until firm.
For the Kewra Spheres: In a medium bowl, whisk sodium alginate into 200 ml water until fully dissolved and no lumps remain. Let stand for 1 hour to remove air bubbles.
In a separate small bowl, whisk calcium lactate gluconate into kewra water until dissolved.
Fill a syringe or dropper with the kewra solution. Gently drip small drops into the sodium alginate bath from a height of about 5-10 cm. The drops will form spheres.
Let spheres sit in the bath for 1-2 minutes.
Carefully scoop spheres out with a slotted spoon. Rinse thoroughly in a bowl of clean water to remove excess alginate.
Store spheres in a small amount of fresh kewra water or a light sugar syrup in the refrigerator until ready to use.
For the Coconut Tuiles: Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone mat.
In a bowl, whisk melted butter, sugar, and coconut cream until combined.
Gradually whisk in flour until a smooth batter forms.
Spread very thin layers of batter onto the prepared baking sheet using an offset spatula or a stencil, creating desired shapes.
Bake for 8-12 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Watch carefully as they burn quickly.
Immediately remove from oven. If desired, gently curve tuiles over a rolling pin or dowel while still warm to create elegant shapes.
Let cool completely on a wire rack until crisp. Store in an airtight container.
For the Compressed Cherries: Place pitted and halved cherries in a vacuum seal bag with cherry liqueur (if using).
Vacuum seal the bag. The compression will intensify the cherry flavor and give them a slightly translucent, firm texture.
If no vacuum sealer, gently press cherries with a flat object for a few minutes.
Chill until ready to plate.
notes: The amount of Panang curry paste is extremely small; its purpose is to provide a subtle aromatic warmth and a hint of spice, not to make the dessert overtly savory. Taste and adjust carefully.
Precision in spherification is key for perfect spheres. Ensure the alginate bath is lump-free and rested.
Tuiles can be delicate; handle with care. Store in an airtight container to maintain crispness.
This dessert emphasizes balance: sweet, floral, a hint of spice, and varied textures (creamy, bursting, crisp, firm).
For best results, prepare components in advance and assemble just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Carnitas with Esquites and Queso Fresco
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple light wooden table. Rustic, irregular chunks of golden-brown pork carnitas, boasting crispy edges and tender interiors, are piled slightly off-center. Beside the pork sits a generous scoop of vibrant yellow esquites, creamy with visible corn kernels, finely chopped cilantro, and specks of red chili powder. Crumbled white queso fresco is scattered generously over both the pork and esquites, adding a contrasting texture and color. Fresh cilantro sprigs are artfully placed as a garnish. A vibrant lime wedge is positioned near the plate's edge. The overall presentation is clean, professional, and inviting, with moderate negative space. A white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for making tacos
Salsa verde or salsa roja on the side
Pickled red onions

ingredients.name: Fresh cilantro
ingredients.quantity: 30 g, chopped, plus sprigs for garnish

instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 5-7 cm rustic chunks.
In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, melt the lard over medium heat.
Add pork chunks to the pot. Add orange halves, onion quarters, smashed garlic, bay leaves, and salt.
Pour in enough water or broth to just cover the pork.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook uncovered for 2-3 hours, or until pork is fork-tender and liquid has mostly evaporated, leaving rendered fat.
Remove pork from the pot. Increase heat to medium-high. Allow the rendered fat to get hot.
Return pork chunks to the hot fat. Cook, stirring occasionally, until pork is golden brown and crispy on all sides. Remove from heat.
For the esquites: In a large skillet, sauté corn kernels over medium-high heat until slightly charred, about 5-7 minutes.
In a mixing bowl, combine mayonnaise, crema Mexicana, lime juice from half a lime, and chili powder. Stir well.
Add warm charred corn to the dressing mixture. Add most of the chopped cilantro. Stir to combine.
Taste and adjust seasoning for both carnitas and esquites.
Serve crispy pork carnitas alongside a generous portion of esquites. Garnish with crumbled queso fresco, fresh cilantro sprigs, and lime wedges.
notes: Using a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven is crucial for even cooking and browning of the carnitas.
traditional_techniques: Confit (pork cooked slowly in its own fat)

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Basil Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Chicken and Basil Tagliatelle is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The tagliatelle is twirled into an elegant, organized nest, revealing its creamy, off-white sauce that clings beautifully to each strand. Tender, golden-brown chicken cubes (2 cm) are nestled organically amongst the pasta. Vibrant green, roughly chopped basil leaves are generously mixed throughout, with a few fresh whole basil leaves scattered on top as garnish. Freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano lightly dusts the dish, adding a subtle texture. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The dish sits on a simple, light wooden table surface. A grey linen napkin and standard silver fork and knife are placed beside the plate. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread like ciabatta to sop up the sauce.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette is also a traditional accompaniment.
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 2 cm cubes. Season chicken with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken cubes until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil and butter to the skillet. Add diced shallot and minced garlic. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Reduce wine by half, about 2 minutes.
Add chicken stock and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low.
Meanwhile, cook tagliatelle in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml pasta cooking water before draining.
Add cooked chicken and grated Parmigiano Reggiano to the sauce in the skillet. Stir until cheese melts and sauce thickens slightly.
Add drained tagliatelle to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to coat pasta evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30 ml at a time, until desired consistency.
Stir in roughly chopped fresh basil.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory White Chocolate with Cherry-Ginger Gastrique and Basil Oil
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a pristine, matte white bone china plate, leaving abundant negative space. A perfectly circular, thin, translucent disc of savory white chocolate, smooth and gleaming, is centered on one side. On it, an elegantly formed quenelle of glossy, ruby-red cherry-ginger gastrique sits. Adjacent, two or three delicate, translucent rings of pickled red onion are artfully arranged, their soft pink hues providing a gentle accent. Precise dots of vibrant emerald-green basil oil are meticulously placed around the components. A single, tiny sprig of micro basil provides the final touch. The composition embodies sophisticated simplicity, balancing color, texture, and form. The plate rests on a polished dark wood table, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting creating soft shadows, emphasizing the dish's sculptural qualities.

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger, peeled and finely grated

instructions: Prepare Pickled Red Onion: Thinly slice red onion into very fine rings. In a small saucepan, combine white wine vinegar, water, sugar, and salt. Bring to a boil, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. Pour hot liquid over sliced onion in a heatproof bowl. Let cool completely. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Make Cherry-Ginger Gastrique: In a small saucepan, combine pitted cherries, grated ginger, red wine vinegar, sugar, and water. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 10-15 minutes, until cherries soften and liquid reduces slightly. Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids. Return liquid to the saucepan. Reduce over low heat until syrupy and coats the back of a spoon (about 10-15 ml total). Set aside to cool.

Form Savory White Chocolate Disc: In a small saucepan, heat heavy cream, water, and sea salt until simmering. In a separate bowl, melt white chocolate gently over a bain-marie or in a microwave. Whisk agar-agar powder into the hot cream mixture until fully dissolved. Slowly pour the hot cream mixture over the melted white chocolate, whisking continuously until smooth and emulsified. Pour the mixture thinly onto a silicone mat or parchment-lined tray. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour, or until firm. Once firm, use a small (approx. 5-6 cm diameter) round cutter to cut out 4 perfect discs.

Create Basil Oil: Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Prepare an ice bath. Blanch basil leaves for 10-15 seconds. Immediately transfer to the ice bath to stop cooking and preserve color. Squeeze out excess water from basil leaves. In a high-speed blender, combine blanched basil, grapeseed oil, and sea salt. Blend on high until completely smooth and vibrant green. Strain the oil through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth for a perfectly clear oil.

Plating (per serving): Place one savory white chocolate disc slightly off-center on a pristine white dinner plate. Carefully spoon a small, artful quenelle or swirl of the cherry-ginger gastrique onto the disc. Arrange 2-3 delicate rings of pickled red onion next to the disc. Drizzle a small amount of basil oil in an artistic line or dots around the components. Garnish with a few tiny sprigs of micro basil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Gochujang King Oyster Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Crispy Gochujang King Oyster Mushrooms is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, typical of modern bistro settings. Three to four thick, golden-brown king oyster mushroom medallions, coated in a glossy, vibrant red-orange gochujang glaze, are artfully stacked in the center. The mushrooms exhibit a visibly crispy exterior and tender interior. Each medallion is a thick chunk, not fanned. A generous sprinkle of toasted white sesame seeds adds textural contrast and a nutty aroma, while thinly sliced bright green scallions are scattered over the top for a fresh, herbaceous accent. The plate has appropriate negative space around the dish, highlighting the food. The setting includes a simple wooden table surface, with a small white rice bowl and a pair of dark wood chopsticks placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, with a softly blurred background suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice.
Accompany with traditional Korean banchan (side dishes) such as kimchi or pickled radishes.
instructions: Slice king oyster mushrooms into 1.5 cm thick medallions. Pat dry with paper towels.
In a medium bowl, whisk together tempura flour and cold water until just combined. Do not overmix; lumps are acceptable.
In a separate small saucepan, combine gochujang, soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar, minced garlic, minced ginger, and sesame oil. Whisk well.
Heat the sauce over medium-low heat. Simmer for 3-5 minutes, stirring constantly, until slightly thickened. Remove from heat.
Heat neutral oil in a deep pot or wok to 170°C. Ensure oil is hot enough for frying.
Dip each mushroom medallion into the tempura batter, allowing excess to drip off.
Carefully place battered mushrooms into the hot oil. Fry in batches to avoid overcrowding.
Fry mushrooms for 3-4 minutes per side, or until golden brown and crispy. Use tongs to turn.
Remove fried mushrooms from oil. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
In a large bowl, add the crispy mushrooms. Pour the gochujang glaze over them. Toss gently to coat all mushrooms evenly.
Thinly slice green onions for garnish.
Arrange glazed mushrooms on serving plates. Garnish with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure oil temperature is maintained for optimal crispiness.
For extra spice, add a pinch of gochugaru (Korean chili flakes) to the glaze.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Peppermint Vanilla Roasted Almonds
recipes.visual_description: A generous pile of golden-brown roasted almonds is presented in a simple, rustic ceramic bowl with natural imperfections. The almonds are whole, not chopped, showcasing their inherent texture. Flecks of dark green, finely chopped peppermint leaves are visible, subtly contrasting with the warm brown of the almonds. A faint, glossy sheen from the egg white coating is present, indicating a crisp texture. The bowl is casually placed on a well-used wooden dining table, with a casually folded, light-colored cloth napkin nearby. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy family kitchen. The overall arrangement is unpretentious and homely, inviting immediate snacking. The entire bowl is visible, with ample negative space around it on the wooden surface, emphasizing the natural, comfort-food appeal of the snack.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a medium bowl, whisk the egg white until frothy.
Add the finely chopped fresh peppermint, vanilla extract, olive oil, salt, black pepper, and garlic powder to the egg white. Whisk well to combine.
Add the raw almonds to the bowl. Toss thoroughly until all almonds are evenly coated with the mixture.
Spread the coated almonds in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the almonds are golden brown and crisp. They will become crispier as they cool.
Remove from oven. Let cool completely on the baking sheet before serving. Store in an airtight container.

recipes.recipe_name: Lavender Milk Chocolate Yogurt Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single generous wedge of Lavender Milk Chocolate Yogurt Cake sits on an everyday cream-colored ceramic plate. The cake has a golden-brown crust and a moist, tender crumb. A smooth, shiny milk chocolate glaze is casually poured over the top, cascading down the sides of the slice. Fine curls of shaved milk chocolate are sprinkled on the glazed surface. A few tiny, dark purple lavender buds are visible within the cake and on the glaze, hinting at the flavor. The plate is placed on a well-worn wooden dining table. In the background, the remaining whole cake, lightly glazed, rests on a simple cake stand. A casual folded cloth napkin and a metal fork are nearby. Warm, cozy light illuminates the scene, suggesting a home kitchen setting. The focus is on the comfort and inviting nature of the homemade dessert.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Grease and flour a 20 cm bundt pan or round cake pan.
In a large bowl, cream softened butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, and lavender buds.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients, alternating with yogurt and milk. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into prepared pan. Smooth the top.
Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean. Baking time varies with oven.
Cool cake in the pan for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
For the glaze, chop milk chocolate. Place in a heatproof bowl.
Heat heavy cream in a small saucepan until just simmering. Pour hot cream over chopped chocolate.
Let stand for 5 minutes. Whisk until smooth and glossy. If too thick, add a tiny bit more warm milk.
Pour glaze over the cooled cake. Let glaze set before serving.
Optionally, shave extra milk chocolate over the glazed cake.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Coconut-Kiwi Risotto and Savory Confetti Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined serving is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table surface. A generous, fluid mound of creamy, pale green coconut-kiwi risotto sits to one side. The risotto is subtly speckled with small, soft kiwi pieces. A golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, left whole, rests partially atop the risotto, displaying a beautiful crust. The chicken is seasoned simply, showcasing its natural form. Finely diced, vibrant green fresh kiwi is scattered sparingly over the risotto, adding a pop of fresh color and natural texture. A 'Savory Confetti Crumble' is lightly sprinkled over the chicken and a portion of the risotto. This crumble consists of finely textured, multi-colored elements from the 100s and 1000s, subtly integrated with golden toasted panko and small flecks of fresh green herbs like parsley and chives, providing a delicate crunch and unexpected visual interest without overwhelming the dish. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space, highlighting the dish's textures and colors. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating a professional yet approachable ambiance.
instructions: Peel 2 kiwis. Dice them into 5mm cubes. Set aside. Peel remaining 2 kiwis. Dice finely for garnish. Set aside.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine (if using). Stir until absorbed.
Add coconut milk. Stir until absorbed.
Begin adding warm broth, one ladle at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for each ladleful to be mostly absorbed before adding the next.
After half the broth is added, stir in the 5mm kiwi cubes and heavy cream. Continue adding broth and stirring.
Cook risotto until creamy and al dente, about 18-20 minutes. Stir in Parmesan and butter. Season with salt and pepper. Cover and keep warm.
While risotto cooks, prepare chicken. Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper.

Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 6-8 minutes per side, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from skillet. Rest for 5 minutes.
For Savory Confetti Crumble: In a small dry skillet, lightly toast panko breadcrumbs over medium-low heat until golden. Remove from heat. Transfer to a small bowl.
Add 100s and 1000s, chopped parsley, and chopped chives to the toasted panko. Add a pinch of salt and pepper. Gently toss to combine.

To serve, spoon a generous portion of risotto onto each plate. Place one seared chicken breast on top or beside the risotto. Garnish with finely diced fresh kiwi. Sprinkle Savory Confetti Crumble lightly over the chicken and risotto.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Chocolate Mousse with Toasted Biscuit Crumb
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of dark chocolate mousse rests in a handcrafted, organic beige ceramic bowl. The mousse is a deep, matte brown, scooped into a natural, slightly uneven mound, showcasing its dense yet aerated texture. Coarse, golden-brown toasted biscuit crumbs are generously scattered over the mousse, providing textural contrast. A delicate, glossy drizzle of reduced milk, a rich caramel hue, artfully trails across the mousse and onto the bowl's clean white space. The minimalist composition emphasizes natural colors and textures. The bowl sits on a light reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually folded nearby. Soft natural light illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows. The background is clean and uncluttered, with subtle out-of-focus greenery, maintaining an eco-conscious aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in individual, handcrafted ceramic bowls to emphasize natural materials and a rustic feel.
Present on a clean, uncluttered surface, such as reclaimed wood or stone, allowing ample white space.
instructions: Pour 50ml milk into a small saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer over low heat. Reduce until thickened and slightly caramelized, about 10-15 minutes. Set aside.
Gently melt chopped dark chocolate in a heatproof bowl set over a pot of simmering water (bain-marie). Stir until smooth. Remove from heat.
In a separate saucepan, gently warm 400ml milk. Do not boil.
Gradually whisk the warm milk into the melted chocolate until smooth and well combined. Stir in the maple syrup and a pinch of sea salt.
Once the chocolate mixture has cooled to lukewarm (around 30-35°C), gently stir in the kombucha or water kefir.
Pour the chocolate mixture into a clean bowl. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until set and firm.
Crush biscuits into coarse crumbs. Spread on a baking tray. Lightly toast in a preheated oven at 160°C for 5-7 minutes until fragrant and lightly golden. Let cool.
Spoon the chilled chocolate mousse into four individual serving bowls or plates.
Sprinkle toasted biscuit crumbs generously over each mousse. Drizzle a small amount of the reduced milk around or on top of the mousse.
Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust maple syrup quantity to preferred sweetness.
For a richer flavor, use a higher percentage dark chocolate.
Ensure chocolate mixture is lukewarm before adding fermented liquid to prevent curdling.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Tropical Fruit Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Homestyle Tropical Fruit Crumble is presented in an off-white ceramic bowl with a slightly chipped rim, sitting on a well-worn wooden dining table. The golden-brown, rustic crumble topping, studded with rolled oats, is visibly crisp and uneven, showcasing its homemade appeal. Beneath, the warm, vibrant fruit filling of diced mango, pineapple, and peach peeks through, bubbling gently at the edges with natural, inviting colors. A casual dollop of melted vanilla ice cream or a spoonful of thick cream sits partially on the crumble, slowly melting down into the warm fruit. The scene is lit by soft, warm kitchen light, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere. A casually folded plain linen napkin and a simple spoon are placed beside the bowl, reinforcing the homely, unpretentious setting of a family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with a scoop of vanilla ice cream
Serve with a dollop of whipped cream or custard
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Peel and dice mangoes into 2 cm cubes. Core and dice pineapple into 2 cm cubes. Peel, pit, and dice peaches into 2 cm cubes.
In a large bowl, combine diced fruits. Add 50 g granulated sugar, cornstarch, and lemon juice. Toss gently to coat.
Pour fruit mixture into a 20x20 cm baking dish.
In a separate bowl, combine flour, rolled oats, remaining 50 g granulated sugar, brown sugar, and pinch of salt.
Cut cold butter into small cubes. Add butter to dry ingredients. Use your fingertips or a pastry blender to mix until coarse crumbs form.
Evenly sprinkle the crumble topping over the fruit mixture in the baking dish.
Bake for 35-45 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and the fruit filling is bubbly.
notes: Ensure fruits are ripe for best flavor.
Adjust sugar amount based on fruit sweetness.

recipes.recipe_name: Mango Lychee Panna Cotta with Lime Syrup
recipes.visual_description: A smooth, pale yellow Mango Lychee Panna Cotta is centered on a clean white round porcelain plate. Its surface is glossy and perfectly set. A vibrant, clear lime syrup is artfully drizzled around the base of the panna cotta, creating a delicate pool. Beside the panna cotta, a small, neat cluster of finely diced fresh mango and halved lychee pieces provides a textural contrast and pop of color. A few bright green mint leaves are delicately placed on top of the panna cotta and next to the fruit garnish. A final sprinkle of bright lime zest enhances the aroma and visual appeal. The dish is presented on a light wooden table surface, with a simple grey cotton napkin placed neatly beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, capturing the dessert's refined simplicity against a softly blurred, modern bistro background.

ingredients.name: Lime zest
ingredients.quantity: Zest of 1 lime, plus extra for garnish

instructions: Bloom gelatin sheets in a bowl of cold water for 5 minutes. If using powdered gelatin, mix with 30ml cold water and let sit 5 minutes.
Combine heavy cream and 100g sugar in a saucepan. Heat over medium heat until sugar dissolves and cream is hot, but do not boil.
Remove from heat. Squeeze excess water from gelatin sheets and stir into hot cream mixture until fully dissolved. If using powdered, add bloomed gelatin directly.
Stir in mango puree until well combined.
Divide mixture evenly into four 150ml molds or ramekins. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or until firmly set.
For the lime syrup, combine lime juice, 50g sugar, 50ml water, and zest of 1 lime in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves.
Simmer for 2-3 minutes until slightly thickened. Remove from heat and let cool completely.
To serve, carefully unmold each panna cotta onto a clean white dessert plate. A quick dip of the mold in warm water helps.
Spoon the cooled lime syrup artfully around the base of each panna cotta.
Garnish each plate with a small cluster of finely diced fresh mango and halved lychee pieces. Add a few fresh mint leaves and a sprinkle of fresh lime zest.
notes: For best results, prepare the panna cotta the day before serving to ensure it is perfectly set.
Adjust sugar in the panna cotta based on the sweetness of your mangoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Simple Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single modest portion of simple roasted chicken and potatoes sits on an everyday round ceramic plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh is the centerpiece, nestled against roasted potato chunks with a slightly charred exterior and fluffy interior. Large, caramelized onion pieces and whole, roasted garlic cloves are interspersed among the potatoes. The dish displays natural, earthy tones of browns, golden yellows, and a touch of green from a few fresh rosemary leaves. The components are arranged casually, touching and overlapping, as if served directly from a family pot. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen light. A standard fork and knife are placed beside the plate. The scene evokes a comfortable, lived-in kitchen atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Cut potatoes into large 2-3 cm chunks or wedges.
Roughly chop onion into large pieces.
Smash garlic cloves with the side of a knife. Do not peel.
In a large roasting pan, toss potatoes, onion, and garlic with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Add rosemary sprigs if using.
Nestle chicken thighs among the vegetables in the pan. Ensure skin is facing up.
Roast for 45-55 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Beef Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of wide, golden pappardelle ribbons nested in a shallow white porcelain bowl. Large, 3cm tender chunks of braised beef are distributed naturally throughout the pasta, coated in a thick, mahogany-colored tomato sauce. The sauce has a glossy sheen and visible small bits of diced carrots and onions. The dish is topped with a light, airy snowfall of finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano. A small pinch of fresh, chopped flat-leaf parsley is scattered over the center. The bowl sits on a rustic light-wood bistro table next to a folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork. Natural daylight illuminates the textures of the shredded beef fibers and the silkiness of the pasta ribbons.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of full-bodied red wine like Chianti
Accompany with crusty sourdough bread for 'fare la scarpetta'
Present in wide-rimmed pasta bowls
instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy-based pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the same pot. Sauté 8 minutes until soft.
Stir in garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to release browned bits.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef stock, and herb sprigs.
Bring to a simmer. Cover and reduce heat to low.
Cook for 2.5 to 3 hours until beef is fork-tender.
Remove herb sprigs. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Boil salted water in a large pot. Cook pappardelle until al dente.
Drain pasta. Reserve 60ml of pasta water.
Toss pasta with the ragu and reserved water over low heat for 1 minute.
Serve immediately with grated cheese.
notes: Ensure the beef is seared deeply for maximum flavor development.
If the sauce is too thick, add more pasta water during the finishing stage.
Chuck roast or shin are the best cuts for this long-braising method.

recipes.recipe_name: Black Truffle Celeriac Puree with Madeira Reduction and Apple
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white, shallow designer plate holds a single, elegantly composed starter. At its center, a smooth, glossy mound of celeriac puree forms a fluid, organic shape, its creamy white tone providing a clean canvas. Nestled delicately atop the puree are a few precisely cut small cubes of vibrant green apple, offering a subtle pop of fresh color and crisp texture. A rich, dark amber Madeira reduction is artfully drizzled in a flowing line across one side, creating a striking visual contrast. The dish is crowned with delicate, paper-thin shavings of fresh black truffle, their intricate patterns adding a luxurious dark accent and earthy aroma. Abundant negative space surrounds the composition. The plate rests on a polished white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting casting soft shadows. A perfectly folded white linen napkin sits beside the plate. This single starter portion is designed for a refined, minimalist presentation.
instructions: Prepare the celeriac puree: Peel celeriac. Cut into 2 cm cubes. Place celeriac cubes in a saucepan. Cover with vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook until very tender, approximately 15-20 minutes. Drain celeriac, reserving a small amount of cooking liquid. Transfer celeriac to a high-speed blender. Add butter, heavy cream, salt, and white pepper. Blend until perfectly smooth. Add a few thin slices of fresh black truffle to the puree. Blend briefly to incorporate truffle aroma. Adjust consistency with reserved stock if needed.

Prepare the Madeira reduction: Pour Madeira wine into a small saucepan. Add granulated sugar. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to low. Simmer until liquid is syrupy and reduced by half, approximately 10-15 minutes. Set aside.

Prepare the apple: Peel and core the apple. Cut into precise 5 mm small cubes. Immediately toss with lemon juice to prevent browning. Lightly blanch apple cubes in simmering water for 30 seconds. Drain well. Chill.

To plate: Spoon a generous quenelle or an organic swirl of the warm celeriac puree onto the center of each plate. Arrange a small cluster of the chilled apple cubes delicately on one side of the puree. Drizzle a precise line of the rich Madeira reduction across the plate, bordering the puree. Finish by shaving thin, delicate slices of fresh black truffle over the puree and apple using a mandoline or truffle shaver. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Beef Chili with Cheese
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of rich, reddish-brown beef chili is served in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl, placed on a worn wooden dining table. The chili is thick and chunky, with visible ground beef, diced red and green bell peppers, and kidney beans. A generous mound of shredded yellow cheddar cheese melts slightly over the top, creating a creamy texture. A few fresh green cilantro leaves are scattered as a simple garnish. The bowl sits on a beige linen placemat. Adjacent to the bowl, a stack of crisp, golden tortilla chips are ready for dipping. The scene is lit with warm, inviting light, suggesting a cozy home kitchen. The background shows a hint of a casual family dining area, with natural imperfections on the table surface. Portions are ample and inviting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm cornbread or a side of steamed rice.
Offer tortilla chips for scooping.
Garnish with a dollop of sour cream or a sprinkle of fresh green onions.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add ground beef. Cook until browned, breaking it apart with a spoon. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion and diced bell pepper to the pot. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic, chili powder, and ground cumin. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in diced tomatoes (undrained) and beef broth. Stir well.
Add drained and rinsed kidney beans. Stir to combine all ingredients.
Bring the chili to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot and cook for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Uncover the pot and continue to simmer for 15-20 minutes more, or until the chili has thickened to your desired consistency.
Season the chili with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot, topped generously with shredded cheddar cheese.
notes: This chili is excellent for meal preparation and freezes well.
Adjust the amount of chili powder to suit your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Fudgy Brownies
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous square of Classic Fudgy Brownie rests on a simple, slightly chipped, cream-colored ceramic dessert plate. The brownie boasts a deep, rich brown color with a characteristic delicate, crackled crust on top. Its edges are neatly cut, revealing a dense, moist, and fudgy interior. A light dusting of powdered sugar, sprinkled unevenly, graces one corner of the brownie. Beside the brownie, a small, elegant scoop of vanilla bean ice cream slowly begins to melt, creating a creamy pool. The plate sits on a well-worn, light wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen light from an overhead fixture. A casual, folded cloth napkin and a simple silver fork are placed nearby. The scene evokes a comforting, homely dessert moment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
Serve with a cold glass of milk.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Line a 20x20 cm baking pan with parchment paper. Leave an overhang for easy removal.
Melt chocolate and butter together in a heatproof bowl set over a pot of simmering water. Stir until smooth. Remove from heat.
In a separate large bowl, whisk eggs and sugar vigorously until light in color and slightly fluffy.
Pour the melted chocolate mixture into the egg mixture. Stir gently until just combined.
Sift flour, cocoa powder, and salt directly into the wet ingredients. Fold gently with a spatula until no dry streaks remain. Do not overmix.
Pour the batter into the prepared baking pan. Spread evenly to the corners.
Bake for 25-30 minutes. A toothpick inserted into the center should come out with moist crumbs, not wet batter.
Let the brownies cool completely in the pan on a wire rack before cutting into squares.
notes: For the fudgiest brownies, be careful not to overbake.
Cooling completely is essential for clean, neat cuts.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Beef Stroganoff
recipes.visual_description: The Beef Stroganoff is presented in a deep, wide-rimmed white porcelain bowl set on a dark oak bistro table. A bed of wide, buttery egg noodles supports the main dish. The beef is featured as thick, irregular seared chunks, not slices, thoroughly coated in a glossy, pale beige cream sauce. Large, quartered cremini mushrooms with golden-brown edges and soft onion strands are visible throughout the sauce. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh dill is concentrated in the center. To the side, a small wooden board holds two thick wedges of dark, crusty rye bread and a small ceramic ramekin filled with additional chilled sour cream. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the textures of the meat and the velvety consistency of the sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of fermented pickles (ogurtsy).
Accompany with dark sourdough rye bread.
Pair with a glass of chilled vodka or kvass.
Can be served over buckwheat kasha for a more rustic variation.
instructions: Pat beef chunks dry with paper towels.
Season beef with salt and black pepper.
Heat oil in a large skillet over high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides.
Remove beef from skillet and set aside.
Melt butter in the same skillet over medium heat.
Add onions and sauté until translucent.
Add mushrooms and garlic.
Cook until mushrooms are golden brown and liquid evaporates.
Stir in mustard and beef stock.
Simmer until the liquid reduces by half.
Reduce heat to low.
Stir in sour cream gradually to incorporate.
Return beef to the skillet.
Heat for 1 minute until warmed through.
Do not let the sauce boil.
Garnish with chopped dill before serving.
notes: Use room temperature sour cream to prevent the sauce from breaking.
Ensure the pan is very hot before searing beef to achieve a deep crust without overcooking the center.
High-fat sour cream (20% or more) provides the most authentic flavor and stable texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Tenderloin with Black Garlic Puree and Slow-Roasted Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of seared beef tenderloin is the focal point on a pristine white bone china plate. Two or three thick, perfectly cooked beef medallions, displaying a deep brown crust and a rosy pink interior, are positioned elegantly. A lustrous, deep black swirl of black garlic puree anchors the composition, providing a striking contrast. Around the beef, a cluster of four to five slow-roasted cherry tomato halves, their skins slightly shriveled and glossy, add concentrated red hues and textural interest. A rich, dark mahogany beef jus is artfully drizzled over the beef and across the plate, creating subtle pools. The plate features abundant negative space, emphasizing the minimalist presentation. A few tiny, vibrant green thyme leaves are precisely placed as a delicate garnish. The dish rests on a polished grey veined marble surface, accompanied by a precisely folded white linen napkin and elegant silver flatware, under dramatic, focused lighting that casts soft shadows.

ingredients.name: Fresh Thyme
ingredients.quantity: 1 sprig plus a few tiny leaves

instructions: Prepare slow-roasted tomatoes: Preheat oven to 120°C. Halve 200g cherry tomatoes. Toss with 15ml olive oil, 1 sprig fresh thyme, salt, pepper. Roast on a tray for 1.5 to 2 hours until shriveled.
Make black garlic puree: Peel 50g black garlic. Simmer with 100ml vegetable stock in a small pan for 5 minutes. Blend with 20g unsalted butter until smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Keep warm.
Reduce beef jus: Simmer 500ml high-quality beef stock in a saucepan until reduced by two-thirds to a nappe consistency. Season. Keep warm.

Cook beef tenderloin: Pat 600g beef tenderloin dry. Season with sea salt and black pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a heavy pan over high heat. Sear tenderloin on all sides until deeply browned, 2-3 minutes per side. Transfer to a 180°C oven. Roast until internal temperature reaches 54°C (medium-rare), about 8-12 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes.

Plate the dish: Slice rested beef into thick medallions. Spoon black garlic puree onto one side of each plate. Arrange 2-3 beef medallions alongside. Artfully place 4-5 slow-roasted tomato halves around the beef. Drizzle beef jus over and around the beef. Garnish with a few tiny fresh thyme leaves.
notes: Use highest quality beef tenderloin for best results.
Ensure beef is well-rested before slicing to retain juices.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Lemon & Cacao Savory Spread with Root Crisps
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a round, unglazed ceramic plate in a natural, light beige tone. At the center, a generous, organic dollop of the dark, earthy Fermented Lemon & Cacao Savory Spread sits, its surface showing a subtle, smooth texture. The spread is a deep, rich brown, almost black, with a hint of glossy sheen from the olive oil. Around the spread, a scattering of thin, irregularly shaped root vegetable crisps creates a vibrant, natural border. The crisps are varied in color: deep ruby red from beetroot, pale cream from parsnip, and warm orange from sweet potato. Each crisp is crisp and slightly curled, showcasing its natural form and texture. They are arranged with mindful negative space, allowing each piece to be appreciated. A whisper of bright yellow fresh lemon zest is finely grated over the spread, offering a subtle visual contrast and a hint of freshness. The overall composition is clean and minimalist, emphasizing natural ingredients and their inherent beauty. The background features a light, textured wooden surface and soft, diffused natural light.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Wash and scrub beetroot, parsnip, and sweet potato. Do not peel.
Slice all vegetables very thinly using a mandoline.
Arrange slices in a single layer on baking sheets lined with parchment paper.
Lightly drizzle with olive oil. Sprinkle with sea salt.
Bake 20-30 minutes until crisp. Flip halfway. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
Cool crisps completely on a wire rack. They will crisp further as they cool.
Rinse fermented lemon. Discard any seeds.
Chop the pulp and a small piece of the rind (about 1/4 of one lemon's rind).
Combine chopped lemon, cacao powder, 60ml olive oil, sugar, black pepper, and 30ml water in a food processor.
Blend until smooth. Add more water, 5ml at a time, to reach a thick, spreadable consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Spoon the savory spread onto the center of a handcrafted ceramic plate.
Arrange the assorted root crisps organically around the spread.
Garnish with a very small amount of fresh lemon zest, if desired.
notes: To make fermented lemons: Wash organic lemons thoroughly. Slice them into quarters or eighths, but do not cut all the way through, leaving the bottom intact. Pack lemons tightly into a clean, sterilized jar, layering with generous amounts of sea salt (about 1 tablespoon per lemon). Press down to release juices. If not fully submerged, add more lemon juice or a brine (1 tbsp salt per 250ml water). Seal the jar. Store in a cool, dark place for 3-4 weeks, turning daily for the first week. Refrigerate after opening. This recipe assumes pre-made fermented lemons are available.

recipes.recipe_name: Dak Gamja Guk (Spicy Chicken and Potato Soup)
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Dak Gamja Guk is presented in a deep, rustic Korean ceramic dolsot bowl. The hearty soup features a rich, reddish-orange broth, hinting at its savory and spicy flavors. Generous chunks of tender, bone-in chicken are nestled amongst substantial 3cm potato wedges and quartered button mushrooms. Diced onion pieces are visible throughout the broth. The soup is generously garnished with vibrant green slices of fresh green onion and a few thin rounds of red chili for a pop of color. The setting is a well-used dark wooden dining table, with natural, warm light illuminating the scene. A simple, traditional Korean metal spoon rests beside the bowl. A small, white ceramic dish containing a side of bright yellow pickled radish (danmuji) is subtly placed in the background, adding an authentic cultural touch to the homely, comfortable family kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with a bowl of steamed white rice.
Accompany with various banchan (small side dishes) such as kimchi, pickled radish, or seasoned bean sprouts.

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.quantity: 1, thinly sliced (remove seeds for less heat)

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken thighs, skin-side down. Sear until skin is golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Pour off excess fat, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the pot. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Add minced garlic, gochugaru, and gochujang. Stir constantly for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return chicken to the pot. Add potato chunks, quartered mushrooms, and sliced red chili.
Pour in water or chicken broth. Add soy sauce. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Cover and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender.
Stir in sesame oil. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Ladle soup into individual bowls. Garnish generously with chopped green onions.
traditional_techniques: Saeu-jeot (salted fermented shrimp) or guk-ganjang (Korean soup soy sauce) can be used for seasoning instead of regular soy sauce for deeper umami.

recipes.recipe_name: Bell Pepper & Lentil Salad
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Bell Pepper & Lentil Salad is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate with a slightly uneven, rustic glaze, sitting on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. The salad features a hearty mix of earthy green Puy lentils, vibrant small-diced red and yellow bell peppers, and finely minced red onion, all glistening lightly with a classic French vinaigrette. The ingredients are casually mounded in the center of the plate, allowing some natural negative space. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley adds a final touch of color and freshness. The overall arrangement is natural and unpretentious, as if served directly from a family bowl. The setting is a cozy, homely kitchen with warm, soft light illuminating the dish, highlighting the natural colors and textures. A simple, folded cloth napkin and basic, well-used flatware rest beside the plate. A crusty slice of baguette is casually placed next to the plate, ready for serving.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh, crusty baguette.
Enjoy as a light lunch or a side dish.
instructions: Rinse lentils under cold water. Place lentils in a medium saucepan. Add vegetable broth or water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until lentils are tender but still hold their shape.
Drain any excess liquid from lentils. Let them cool completely.
While lentils cool, prepare vegetables. Dice red and yellow bell peppers into small cubes (approximately 1 cm). Finely mince the red onion and garlic cloves.
Prepare the vinaigrette. In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, and black pepper until emulsified.
In a large mixing bowl, combine cooled lentils, diced bell peppers, minced red onion, and minced garlic.
Pour the prepared vinaigrette over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.
Stir in the fresh chopped parsley just before serving.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Serve at room temperature.
notes: For best flavor, let the salad sit for 30 minutes before serving. This allows the flavors to meld.

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni with Spicy Sausage Ragu and Smoked Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: A generous single serving of rigatoni pasta is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, showcasing the rich, deep red of the spicy sausage ragu. The rigatoni tubes are perfectly al dente, their ridged surfaces coated in the thick, rustic sauce. Visible within the ragu are tender, browned crumbled pieces of spicy Italian sausage and small, glistening cubes of smoked mozzarella, some partially melted and stretching with a creamy sheen. A generous sprinkle of finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano crowns the dish, adding a light, golden hue. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are artfully scattered over the pasta, providing a sharp color contrast and aromatic garnish. The composition is balanced, allowing for moderate negative space around the pasta. The bowl rests on a simple, light wooden table surface, accompanied by a silver fork and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for 'scarpetta' (mopping up sauce).
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Pair with a robust red Italian wine, such as a Sangiovese or Montepulciano.

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.quantity: 1/4 cup chopped, plus sprigs for garnish

instructions: Remove sausage from casings. Break into small pieces.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown sausage pieces until cooked through and lightly crispy. Remove sausage with a slotted spoon. Drain excess fat, leaving 15ml in pot.
Dice onion, carrot, and celery. Add to pot. Cook 8-10 minutes until softened.
Mince garlic. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using) to pot. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape bottom of pot to deglaze. Cook 2-3 minutes until liquid reduces by half.
Stir in crushed San Marzano tomatoes and chicken stock. Return browned sausage to pot. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until ragu thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, cook rigatoni in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package instructions until al dente. Drain, reserving 120ml pasta water.
Add drained rigatoni to ragu. Stir well to coat.

Cut smoked mozzarella into small cubes. Add cubed smoked mozzarella and chopped fresh basil. Stir until mozzarella begins to melt and becomes stringy. Add reserved pasta water if needed to reach desired consistency.
Serve immediately in warm bowls. Garnish with grated Parmigiano Reggiano and fresh basil sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Garlic Chicken Pasta with Arugula
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Lemon Garlic Chicken Pasta with Arugula is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Golden linguine pasta is artfully swirled into a neat mound, glistening with a light, emulsified lemon-garlic sauce. Generous, irregularly cut chunks of seared chicken, with a beautiful golden-brown crust, are nestled among the pasta. Vibrant green arugula leaves are gently folded into the dish, providing a fresh, slightly peppery contrast. A generous sprinkling of finely grated white Parmesan cheese covers the pasta and chicken. A few bright yellow strands of lemon zest are visible, adding a pop of color. The dish exhibits a balance of colors and textures: the smooth pasta, the tender chicken, and the delicate greens. The overall presentation is clean, professional, and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, beside a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and refined execution. The background is minimal, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Cook linguine according to package directions. Reserve 120 ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Cut chicken into 2 cm thick chunks. Season with salt and black pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks to skillet. Sear chicken 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 30 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Reduce heat to medium.
Thinly slice garlic cloves. Add sliced garlic and red pepper flakes to skillet. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Pour in chicken broth and reserved pasta water. Bring to a simmer. Cook 2 minutes to reduce slightly.
Zest half the lemon directly into the sauce. Squeeze juice from the entire lemon into the sauce.
Add cooked linguine to the skillet. Toss pasta with sauce until well coated.
Add seared chicken chunks to the pasta. Gently toss to combine.
Add fresh arugula to the pasta. Toss briefly until arugula slightly wilts.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with grated Parmesan cheese and a pinch of fresh lemon zest.

recipes.recipe_name: Chocolate & Roasted Garlic Caramel Cake with Umami Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of a rich, dark chocolate cake stands elegantly on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing its distinct layers. The cake is moist and deep brown, topped with a glossy, amber-hued roasted garlic caramel that drips slightly down the sides. A generous sprinkle of golden-brown Umami Crumble, composed of crispy panko, dark mushroom powder, and tiny, dark, almost imperceptible beef bits, covers the top, providing a textural contrast. The slice reveals the even crumb of the cake and the smooth layer of caramel between the two cake halves. The plate features moderate negative space, highlighting the cake. A cotton napkin is folded beside the plate on a simple wooden table surface. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dessert, emphasizing its unique texture and color variations. The overall presentation is modern bistro style, professional yet approachable.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Cut top off garlic head. Drizzle with olive oil. Wrap in foil. Roast 45 minutes until soft. Squeeze out cloves. Mash into a smooth puree. Set aside.
Melt butter in a pan. Add panko breadcrumbs. Toast until golden. Stir in mushroom powder, crispy beef bits, and sugar. Cook 2 minutes. Remove from heat. Set aside.
Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour two 20 cm round cake pans.
In a large bowl, whisk flour, cocoa powder, sugar, baking soda, and salt.
Add eggs, milk, oil, and vanilla. Beat until smooth.
Stir in hot water until just combined. Batter will be thin.
Divide batter evenly between prepared pans.
Bake 30-35 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into center comes out clean.
Cool cakes in pans for 10 minutes. Invert onto wire racks. Cool completely.
In a saucepan, combine sugar and water. Cook over medium heat without stirring until golden amber caramel forms.
Carefully pour in warm heavy cream. Stir until smooth. Add butter, roasted garlic puree, and salt. Stir until butter melts and caramel is smooth. Let cool to thicken.
